key_works: Tsao et al. (2018), ultrawide-bandgap research assessment, DOI:10.1002/aelm.201600501.

title: From pulsed ultrawide-bandgap power to continuous service
open: Translate high pulsed-power demonstrations into reliable repetitive or continuous operation with quantified switching, thermal, packaging, and lifetime performance.
status: Gong et al. reported a megawatt ultrawide-bandgap module for pulsed power in 2026; this does not establish continuous grid-service capability.
why: Separates peak-power demonstrations from usable energy-conversion duty.
key_works: H. Gong et al. (2026), *A megawatt ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor module for pulsed power electronics*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-71274-6.

title: Extreme-environment power-device qualification
open: Predict long-term device and package behavior under combined temperature, radiation, electrical stress, and chemically aggressive conditions.
status: Wide- and ultrawide-bandgap research targets these environments; combined-stressor lifetime remains more demanding than isolated tolerance tests.
why: Supports nuclear, geothermal, aerospace, and high-temperature industrial electronics.
key_works: National Laboratory of the Rockies (2025), *Ultra-Wide Bandgap Semiconductors Research*; R. Chu et al., extreme-environment electronics collection.

title: Fast expansion of transformer supply
open: Expand production, repair, standardization, and deployment of transformers without compromising reliability or creating new bottlenecks in electrical steel, components, testing, and skilled labor.
status: IEA’s 2025 transmission assessment identifies equipment supply and delivery constraints as material barriers.
why: Generation and electrification projects cannot connect without essential equipment.
key_works: IEA (2025), *Building the Future Transmission Grid*.

title: Reliable dynamic line ratings during extremes
open: Increase transmission utilization using measured weather and conductor state while maintaining valid safety margins during sensor faults, spatially uneven conditions, and extreme events.
status: Dynamic ratings are deployable technology; the unresolved issue is dependable integration and uncertainty management at scale.
why: Extracts more value from existing corridors without treating favorable weather as guaranteed capacity.
key_works: IEA (2023), *Electricity Grids and Secure Energy Transitions*; IEA (2025), transmission-grid assessment.

title: Low-disruption heat-pump retrofits
open: Decarbonize difficult existing buildings without requiring prohibitively expensive envelope reconstruction, oversized equipment, major electrical upgrades, or unacceptable comfort compromises.
status: Heat pumps are mature; heterogeneous building stock and installation costs remain deployment barriers.
why: Existing buildings dominate the near-term retrofit problem.
key_works: IEA (2022), *The Future of Heat Pumps*.

title: Efficient frost management in cold-climate heat pumps
open: Minimize frosting and defrost penalties while preserving capacity, comfort, drainage, and reliability across difficult temperature–humidity combinations.
status: Cold-climate heat pumps already work; the open problem is improved seasonal and extreme-condition performance, not basic operation below freezing.
why: Reduces winter electricity peaks and backup-heating requirements.
key_works: IEA (2022), heat-pump assessment.

title: High-lift industrial heat pumps
open: Deliver useful industrial heat over demanding temperature lifts with durable compressors, suitable working fluids, and attractive performance at actual factory operating conditions.
status: High-temperature demonstrations exist; integration, lifetime, and economics vary strongly with the process.
why: Electrifies heat that cannot be served by ordinary building equipment.
key_works: Aalborg University (2024–2026), *Demonstrating high-temperature heat pumps at different integration levels*; IEA (2022), heat-pump study.

title: Low-impact refrigerants without unacceptable tradeoffs
open: Identify refrigerant–equipment combinations that jointly satisfy climate impact, toxicity, flammability, efficiency, leakage, manufacturability, and serviceability requirements.
status: Multiple low-impact refrigerants are available; there is no universally best substitute across applications.
why: Avoids reducing operational emissions while increasing lifecycle or safety burdens.
key_works: IEA (2022), *The Future of Heat Pumps*.

title: Low-temperature district heat in existing cities
open: Convert heterogeneous buildings and networks to lower-temperature heat supply while managing return temperatures, domestic hot water, seasonal demand, and phased retrofit constraints.
status: Low-temperature networks exist; brownfield conversion is a coordination problem across assets with different replacement schedules.
why: Improves access to waste heat, geothermal heat, and efficient heat pumps.
key_works: IEA (2026), *Electrification*; DOE (2019), geothermal heat-use assessment.

title: Fatigue-resistant elastocaloric refrigeration
open: Retain useful cooling power and efficiency through appliance-relevant cycling while reducing actuation work, hysteresis, mechanical fatigue, and heat-transfer losses.
status: Elastocaloric effects and device demonstrations are established; durable complete-system performance remains the engineering frontier.
why: Could provide cooling without conventional vapor-compression refrigerants.
key_works: X. Moya, S. Kar-Narayan, and N. D. Mathur (2014), *Caloric materials near ferroic phase transitions*, DOI:10.1038/nmat3951.

title: Electrocaloric cooling with practical heat throughput
open: Convert large material-level electrocaloric responses into reliable cooling systems without dielectric breakdown, excessive electrical losses, or insufficient heat-transfer area.
status: Strong effects and multilayer concepts exist; useful device throughput and lifetime require more than a large measured temperature change.
why: Tests a solid-state cooling route with potentially compact actuation.
key_works: Moya, Kar-Narayan, and Mathur (2014), caloric-materials review, DOI:10.1038/nmat3951.

title: Durable radiative cooling in humid, dirty environments
open: Deliver verified annual building-energy savings from radiative-cooling surfaces despite humidity, clouds, soiling, weathering, and competing winter heating needs.
status: Daytime subambient cooling was demonstrated in 2014; universal annual benefit does not follow from that physical demonstration.
why: Determines where passive radiative cooling is genuinely useful.
key_works: A. P. Raman et al. (2014), *Passive radiative cooling below ambient air temperature under direct sunlight*, DOI:10.1038/nature13883.

title: Transferable building predictive control
open: Deploy predictive control across previously unseen buildings with low commissioning effort, calibrated comfort constraints, occupant changes, and reliable fallback behavior.
status: Model-predictive control has long demonstrated potential; obtaining and maintaining useful models remains a deployment challenge.
why: Avoids bespoke optimization for every building.
key_works: F. Oldewurtel et al. (2012), *Use of model predictive control and weather forecasts for energy efficient building climate control*, DOI:10.1016/j.enbuild.2011.09.022.

title: Closing the building energy-performance gap
open: Predict and verify actual post-construction or post-retrofit energy use while separating model error, installation defects, occupant behavior, weather, and rebound effects.
status: The performance gap has been systematically analyzed for more than a decade and remains the subject of 2026 research.
why: Turns modeled savings into dependable investment outcomes.
key_works: P. de Wilde (2014), *The gap between predicted and measured energy performance of buildings: A framework for investigation*, DOI:10.1016/j.autcon.2014.02.009.

title: Hydrogen ironmaking with lower-grade ores
open: Produce high-quality iron economically from a broader range of ores while controlling impurities, sticking, reduction kinetics, hydrogen demand, and downstream furnace requirements.
status: Hydrogen-based reduction is demonstrated; ore quality and integrated process economics limit universal substitution.
why: Avoids shifting steel decarbonization into a narrow premium-ore supply bottleneck.
key_works: DOE (2022), *U.S. Department of Energy’s Industrial Decarbonization Roadmap*, OSTI:1961393.

title: Electrified cement calcination at industrial scale
open: Supply calcination heat electrically with adequate throughput, material quality, equipment lifetime, and integration with concentrated process-carbon-dioxide handling.
status: Electrification pathways are under development; eliminating combustion does not eliminate limestone-derived emissions.
why: Addresses both process heat and the configuration needed for process-emission management.
key_works: DOE (2022), industrial decarbonization roadmap.

title: Low-clinker binders with long-term assurance
open: Qualify low-clinker cement systems across locally available feedstocks and exposure conditions while predicting decades-long structural durability.
status: Alternative binders and supplementary materials are widely studied and used; composition variability and long-term assurance remain limiting for broader substitution.
why: Reduces energy and process emissions without transferring risk into infrastructure.
key_works: DOE (2022), industrial roadmap.

title: Electrified cracking with industrial selectivity and availability
open: Electrify high-temperature chemical cracking while preserving heat-flux control, product selectivity, tube lifetime, decoking performance, and continuous plant availability.
status: Process-electrification development is active; replacing a burner does not solve reactor-material and integration requirements.
why: Targets a major source of industrial fuel consumption.
key_works: DOE (2022), industrial roadmap; IEA (2026), *Electrification*.

title: Recovering low-grade industrial waste heat
open: Recover economically useful heat from dirty, intermittent, spatially dispersed streams without prohibitive exchanger fouling, transport cost, or mismatch with nearby demand.
status: Heat recovery is mature in favorable settings; fragmented and contaminated low-grade sources remain difficult.
why: Exploits efficiency opportunities excluded by idealized heat-integration studies.
key_works: J. Cresko et al. (2022), *Thermal Process Intensification: Transforming the Way Industry Uses Thermal Process Energy*; DOE industrial roadmap.

title: Sustainable aviation-fuel feedstock expansion
open: Expand fuel supply without unacceptable land-use change, food competition, biodiversity loss, water burdens, or misleading treatment of waste and residue counterfactuals.
status: Approved pathways and commercial production exist; sustainably scalable feedstock is a separate constraint.
why: Prevents fuel-volume targets from outrunning actual environmental benefit.
key_works: DOE/DOT/USDA/EPA (2022), *SAF Grand Challenge Roadmap: Flight Plan for Sustainable Aviation Fuel*; DOE (2025), Energy Earthshots report.

title: Affordable synthetic aviation fuel with complete accounting
open: Produce aviation-compatible synthetic fuels at useful scale with low lifecycle emissions after hydrogen, carbon sourcing, synthesis, refining, and electricity opportunity costs are included.
status: Individual conversion steps exist; the complete low-cost, low-emission chain remains difficult.
why: Offers a route beyond limited biological feedstocks.
key_works: DOE et al. (2022), SAF roadmap; IEA (2025), hydrogen review.

title: High-utilization heavy-truck charging networks
open: Coordinate vehicle schedules, megawatt-class charging, grid connections, queues, and infrastructure utilization so electrified freight remains reliable under real logistics variability.
status: Heavy-vehicle electrification is progressing; network and operational integration can be harder than vehicle capability.
why: Avoids replacing fuel stops with costly delays and stranded charging assets.
key_works: IEA (2026), *Electrification*; Chen, Tan, and Quek (2012), online charging foundations, arXiv:1208.4743.

title: Maritime ammonia without harmful slip and by-products
open: Use ammonia in marine propulsion while controlling unburned ammonia, nitrogen oxides, nitrous oxide, safety burdens, and complete lifecycle emissions.
status: Ammonia is an active maritime fuel pathway; carbon-free molecular composition does not establish climate-neutral or clean operation.
why: Avoids replacing carbon emissions with other harmful emissions and operational hazards.
key_works: IEA (2025), *Global Hydrogen Review 2025*.

title: Aviation batteries at pack-level specific energy
open: Achieve aviation-relevant specific energy together with high power, reserves, thermal containment, cycle life, and acceptable performance across flight conditions at the complete-pack level.
status: High-energy cells exist; packaging, safety systems, and operational reserves reduce usable aircraft-level performance.
why: Determines the range of aircraft that can be directly electrified.

title: Selective lignin valorization without excessive process energy
open: Convert heterogeneous lignin into useful products while suppressing repolymerization, minimizing separations, and preserving a favorable integrated biorefinery energy balance.
status: Many depolymerization routes exist; feedstock variability and product mixtures continue to impede consistent high-value conversion.
why: Improves the economics and material efficiency of lignocellulosic processing.
key_works: A. J. Ragauskas et al. (2014), *Lignin valorization: improving lignin processing in the biorefinery*, DOI:10.1126/science.1246843.

title: Robust mixed-sugar biomass conversion
open: Convert variable lignocellulosic hydrolysates efficiently despite mixed sugars, pretreatment inhibitors, contamination, and changing feedstock composition.
status: Individual pretreatment and conversion technologies work; economical integration across diverse feedstocks remains unresolved.
why: Prevents a process from working only on unusually clean laboratory substrates.
key_works: S. G. Wettstein et al. (2012), *A roadmap for conversion of lignocellulosic biomass to chemicals and fuels*, DOI:10.1016/j.coche.2012.04.002.

title: Positive-net-energy algal fuel production
open: Produce algal fuels with favorable whole-system energy and environmental performance after cultivation, nutrients, harvesting, dewatering, extraction, and conversion are included.
status: High biological productivity does not settle the integrated energy balance; dewatering and cultivation logistics remain central constraints.
why: Tests whether algae can be an energy source rather than an energy-intensive feedstock.
key_works: Y. Chisti (2007), *Biodiesel from microalgae*, DOI:10.1016/j.biotechadv.2007.02.001; DOE biological-energy research programs.

title: Stable waste-to-energy microbial communities
open: Maintain predictable conversion of changing wet-waste mixtures despite inhibitors, pathogens, community shifts, and disturbances without excessive pretreatment or process downtime.
status: Anaerobic conversion is mature; reliable control of complex microbial communities remains incomplete.
why: Expands energy recovery from heterogeneous waste rather than carefully selected feedstocks.
key_works: DOE, *Genomic Science Program*, plant and microbial systems research; Wettstein et al. (2012), biomass-conversion integration.

title: Dynamic bioenergy carbon counterfactuals
open: Estimate climate effects of biomass use against realistic alternative ecosystem, land-management, and product-use trajectories, including timing rather than only cumulative carbon.
status: Carbon-debt analysis has been prominent since 2008; conclusions remain sensitive to feedstock and counterfactual assumptions.
why: Prevents “renewable” from being used as a substitute for demonstrated climate benefit.
key_works: J. Fargione et al. (2008), *Land Clearing and the Biofuel Carbon Debt*, DOI:10.1126/science.1152747.

title: Verifiable net-negative bioenergy with carbon capture
open: Demonstrate net atmospheric removal after cultivation, land-use effects, processing, capture energy, transport, leakage risk, and alternative biomass uses are counted.
status: Capture at biogenic sources exists; net-negative status remains a lifecycle claim requiring evidence.
why: Distinguishes genuine removal from shifting emissions across accounting boundaries.
key_works: M. Bui et al. (2018), *Carbon capture and storage (CCS): the way forward*, DOI:10.1039/C7EE02342A; Fargione et al. (2008).

title: Detection-to-repair closure for methane super-emitters
open: Detect intermittent large leaks rapidly, attribute them correctly, ensure repair, and verify durable cessation despite limited revisit frequency and changing operating states.
status: Satellite, aerial, and ground observations have expanded; the 2026 IEA assessment still treats measurement and abatement as distinct tasks.
why: A detected plume is not an avoided emission.
key_works: IEA (2026), *Global Methane Tracker 2026*.

title: Finding and durably sealing undocumented wells
open: Locate undocumented wells, prioritize actual leakage risk, verify plugging quality, and monitor long-term integrity at costs compatible with the scale of legacy infrastructure.
status: DOE supports locating and characterizing undocumented wells; inventories and durable remediation remain incomplete.
why: Prevents persistent emissions and groundwater pathways from disappearing into missing records.
key_works: DOE, *Consortium Advancing Technology for Assessment of Lost Oil & Gas Wells* research program.

title: Durable low-energy solvent capture
open: Reduce regeneration energy while controlling solvent degradation, corrosion, volatile emissions, contaminants, and performance under changing flue-gas conditions.
status: Solvent capture is commercially established; simultaneous reductions in energy use and lifecycle burden remain active research objectives.
why: Capture efficiency alone does not determine economical, low-impact operation.
key_works: Bui et al. (2018), CCS assessment, DOI:10.1039/C7EE02342A.

title: Climate-robust low-energy direct air capture
open: Sustain low lifecycle energy and material consumption across humidity, temperature, dust, and seasonal variability while delivering verifiably durable carbon storage.
status: Direct air capture exists; universal low-cost performance across climates is not established.
why: Avoids extrapolating favorable pilot conditions to global deployment.
key_works: Bui et al. (2018), DOI:10.1039/C7EE02342A; IEA (2020), *CCUS in Clean Energy Transitions*.

title: Pressure-constrained carbon-storage capacity
open: Estimate and manage usable storage capacity when pressure interference, fault limits, displaced brine, and neighboring projects constrain injection.
status: Pore-volume estimates and geological screening are insufficient to determine sustainable injection rates.
why: Converts nominal storage resources into operationally credible capacity.
key_works: M. A. Celia et al. (2015), *Status of CO2 storage in deep saline aquifers with emphasis on modeling approaches and practical simulations*, DOI:10.1002/2015WR017609.

title: Affordable long-term storage verification
open: Detect and attribute consequential leakage or migration with defensible confidence while keeping monitoring affordable over long periods and after site closure.
status: Monitoring methods exist; observability, sparse sampling, legacy wells, and long timescales complicate assurance.
why: Makes permanence claims auditable without requiring impossible continuous observation everywhere.
key_works: Celia et al. (2015), saline-aquifer storage assessment, DOI:10.1002/2015WR017609.

title: Shared carbon-dioxide networks with variable streams
open: Coordinate capture sources, transport, intermediate storage, and injection despite changing impurity mixtures, interruptions, and mismatched commissioning schedules.
status: Shared infrastructure can reduce cost, but creates coupled operational and commercial dependencies.
why: Individual capture projects may fail without a dependable common network.
key_works: IEA (2020), *CCUS in Clean Energy Transitions*.

title: Very-dilute methane abatement
open: Destroy or recover methane in low-concentration, high-volume streams with low auxiliary energy, reliable operation, and a favorable complete emissions balance.
status: Abatement options exist for selected streams; dilute and variable sources remain harder than concentrated leaks.
why: Addresses emissions that are too dispersed for conventional recovery.
key_works: IEA (2026), *Global Methane Tracker 2026*.

title: Selective, durable direct lithium extraction
open: Extract lithium from diverse brines while preserving selectivity, sorbent or membrane life, recovery, water balance, and manageable waste streams.
status: Direct-extraction technologies are being deployed and developed; performance remains strongly dependent on brine chemistry and process boundaries.
why: Expands supply without assuming all lithium-bearing waters are economical resources.
key_works: IEA (2026), *Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026*.

title: Lower-impact nickel production from difficult ores
open: Produce suitable nickel intermediates with lower energy, emissions, water, and residue burdens while retaining high recovery and commercially acceptable economics.
status: Established extraction routes involve significant tradeoffs; demand growth increases the importance of ore-specific lifecycle performance.
why: Prevents battery-material expansion from locking in avoidable upstream burdens.
key_works: IEA (2026), critical-minerals outlook.

title: High-performance magnets with reduced rare-earth dependence
open: Obtain magnet systems with useful energy product, coercivity, temperature stability, and manufacturability while substantially reducing vulnerable rare-earth inputs.
status: Alternatives exist but have application-specific performance and mass tradeoffs.
why: Reduces supply concentration risks in generators and motors.
key_works: IEA (2026), *Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026*; Tsao et al. (2018), contrasting semiconductor material-substitution principles.

title: High-value recovery of rare-earth magnets
open: Recover magnets from heterogeneous end-of-life products and restore useful magnetic performance without excessive dismantling, oxidation, contamination, or chemical processing.
status: Recycling routes exist; collection, separation, and quality retention constrain closed-loop scale.
why: Creates secondary supply rather than merely recovering low-value mixed metals.
key_works: IEA (2026), critical-minerals assessment.

title: Economical recycling of low-value battery chemistries
open: Recycle lithium iron phosphate and other low-metal-value cells with positive lifecycle value while recovering useful lithium, graphite, and preferably functional electrode material.
status: Recycling is easier to finance when valuable metals dominate; lower-value chemistries change the economics.
why: Prevents safer or cheaper batteries from becoming economically unrecoverable waste.
key_works: G. Harper et al. (2019), *Recycling lithium-ion batteries from electric vehicles*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-019-1682-5; L. Li et al. (2018), *The Recycling of Spent Lithium-Ion Batteries*, DOI:10.1007/s41918-018-0012-1.

title: Safe robotic battery disassembly
open: Disassemble mixed, damaged, undocumented, or partly charged packs while recognizing configuration and condition and preventing electrical, fire, and chemical hazards.
status: Automation and safety procedures exist; heterogeneous returned packs defeat simple repetitive factory assumptions.
why: Safe recovery must scale beyond manual expert handling.
key_works: J. Jeevarajan et al. (2024), *Safety in the Recycling of Lithium-Ion Batteries*, DOI:10.60752/102376.27006670.

title: High-purity photovoltaic material recovery
open: Recover glass, silicon, metals, and emerging absorber materials at purity and cost sufficient for meaningful closed-loop reuse rather than predominantly low-value downcycling.
status: Photovoltaic recycling exists; multi-terawatt deployment makes recovery quality and scalable logistics increasingly important.
why: Reduces future primary-material demand and waste burden.
key_works: Haegel et al. (2023), photovoltaic scaling study, DOI:10.1126/science.adf6957.

title: Closed-loop wind-blade composite recycling
open: Recover fibers and matrix value from large blades while retaining useful material properties and avoiding process energy or cost that defeats reuse.
status: Mechanical, thermal, and chemical routes exist; closed-loop quality and economics remain unresolved across blade generations.
why: Addresses the difficult composite fraction of otherwise substantially recyclable turbines.
key_works: P. Liu and C. Y. Barlow (2017), *Wind turbine blade waste in 2050*, DOI:10.1016/j.wasman.2017.02.007; IEA Wind, long-term research-needs assessment.

title: Climate-conditioned compound energy-weather datasets
open: Construct open ensembles representing correlated wind, solar, hydro, temperature-driven demand, outages, and prolonged extremes under changing climate conditions.
status: Weather and energy datasets exist; consistent treatment of compound tails and future nonstationarity remains incomplete.
why: Reliability conclusions can change when missing correlations are restored.
key_works: Denholm et al. (2021), renewable-system challenges, DOI:10.1016/j.joule.2021.05.011; Holttinen et al. (2022), system-impact study.

title: Globally representative end-use and distribution data
open: Build privacy-protecting, reusable datasets of subhourly demand, feeder structure, outages, and appliance behavior across underrepresented climates and income levels.
status: Open Power System Data demonstrates reusable electricity datasets; geographic and end-use coverage remain uneven.
why: Avoids exporting conclusions from well-instrumented systems to fundamentally different contexts.
key_works: F. Wiese et al. (2019), *Open Power System Data – Frictionless data for electricity system modelling*.

title: Closed-loop grid-control benchmarks
open: Benchmark controllers against realistic dynamics, hidden disturbances, sensor faults, protection actions, and out-of-distribution conditions, with reproducible safety and cost metrics.
status: PGLib provides important static optimization benchmarks; it does not by itself supply a comprehensive dynamic-control evaluation environment.
why: Prevents controllers from being judged only on friendly simulators or average reward.
key_works: IEEE PES Task Force et al. (2019), PGLib-OPF paper, arXiv:1908.02788; Lin et al. (2020), inverter roadmap.

title: Auditable energy-project failure and cost census
open: Publish comparable project-level data on cancellations, delays, redesigns, financing, completed cost, and operating performance, including unsuccessful projects.
status: Historical studies reveal how definitions and selection affect conclusions; no single clean dataset settles cross-technology delivery risk.
why: Reduces survivorship bias in learning curves and investment forecasts.
key_works: Lovering, Yip, and Nordhaus (2016), DOI:10.1016/j.enpol.2016.01.011; Koomey, Hultman, and Grubler (2017), methodological reply.

title: Verifiable material and lifecycle provenance
open: Trace energy-device materials, processing, repair, and recycling with uncertainty-aware records that remain usable across firms without treating supplier declarations as automatically true.
status: Traceability initiatives exist; interoperability, verification, and data quality remain limiting.
why: Makes lifecycle and responsible-sourcing claims testable.
key_works: IEA (2026), critical-minerals outlook; Titirici et al. (2024), sustainable-battery roadmap, DOI:10.1088/2515-7655/ad6bc0.

title: Explaining disagreement among energy-system models
open: Attribute differences in recommended investments to input data, weather sampling, constraints, temporal aggregation, solver choices, and structural assumptions using reproducible experiments.
status: Model comparisons exist; similar headline scenarios can conceal materially different formulations.
why: Turns disagreement into identifiable assumptions rather than competing authoritative projections.
key_works: Wiese et al. (2019), open-data infrastructure; Denholm et al. (2021), system-design challenges.

title: Causal marginal electricity-emissions estimates
open: Estimate emissions caused or avoided by changed electricity demand or procurement across dispatch, imports, storage, and long-run investment responses.
status: Marginal-emissions methods date back well before current carbon-aware computing applications; short-run and long-run counterfactuals remain distinct.
why: Average grid intensity can misstate the effect of an actual intervention.
key_works: A. D. Hawkes (2010), *Estimating marginal CO2 emissions rates for national electricity systems*, DOI:10.1016/j.enpol.2010.05.053; J. A. de Chalendar et al. (2019), *Why 100% Renewable Energy Is Not Enough*.

title: Auditable AI and data-center energy accounting
open: Measure and forecast complete computational energy demand, including utilization, cooling, networking, embodied infrastructure, inference growth, and efficiency-driven demand changes.
status: Earlier estimates required recalibration; IEA’s 2025 assessment highlights rapidly changing demand and infrastructure interactions.
why: Supports realistic grid planning and evaluates whether computational efficiency reduces total demand.
key_works: E. Masanet et al. (2020), *Recalibrating global data center energy-use estimates*, DOI:10.1126/science.aba3758; IEA (2025), *Energy and AI*.

title: Lower clean-energy financing costs in emerging economies
subfield: Energy access, markets, institutions, and funding
open: Design risk-sharing, currency protection, and contracting mechanisms that demonstrably reduce financing costs without unsustainable public liabilities or hidden transfers of risk.
status: IEA’s Cost of Capital Observatory documents financing differences; identifying durable, scalable remedies remains a policy and market-design problem.
why: Identical hardware can have very different affordability depending on financing conditions.
key_works: IEA, *Cost of Capital Observatory*.

title: Sustained clean-cooking adoption
subfield: Energy access, markets, institutions, and funding
open: Achieve affordable, reliable clean cooking that households continue using, rather than temporary appliance adoption followed by fuel stacking or reversion.
status: Clean technologies exist; fuel affordability, supply, household preferences, and financing continue to obstruct universal access.
why: Health and environmental benefits depend on actual long-term cooking practices.
key_works: IEA (2023), *A Vision for Clean Cooking Access for All*.

title: Reliable electricity access beyond first connection
subfield: Energy access, markets, institutions, and funding
open: Deliver affordable service with adequate capacity, uptime, repair, and safety over years, including remote and low-income communities.
status: Connection counts and access tracking are essential but do not alone establish reliable, useful service.
why: Development benefits depend on electricity that works when needed.
key_works: IEA/IRENA/UNSD/World Bank/WHO, *Tracking SDG 7: The Energy Progress Report* and associated access datasets.

title: Financeable mini-grids under uncertain demand growth
subfield: Energy access, markets, institutions, and funding
open: Forecast and stimulate productive demand sufficiently to support reliable mini-grid service without unaffordable tariffs, excessive subsidy dependence, or stranded capacity.
status: Mini-grids operate successfully in some settings; load growth and revenue uncertainty remain important deployment constraints.
why: Small systems must survive economically after installation funding ends.
key_works: *Tracking SDG 7* access assessments; IEA, *Cost of Capital Observatory*.

title: Fair transmission benefit and cost allocation
subfield: Energy access, markets, institutions, and funding
open: Allocate costs and benefits of interregional transmission under uncertain future generation, demand, reliability needs, and distributional consequences in ways that enable timely agreement.
status: Planning methods exist; cross-jurisdiction coordination and benefit attribution remain major delivery barriers.
why: Socially useful lines can remain blocked when no accepted allocation exists.
key_works: IEA (2023), *Electricity Grids and Secure Energy Transitions*; IEA (2025), *Building the Future Transmission Grid*.

title: First-of-a-kind completion-risk financing
subfield: Energy access, markets, institutions, and funding
open: Structure financing that permits technically justified first plants to be built while revealing and allocating construction, performance, and market risks rather than socializing unlimited downside.
status: Grants, guarantees, offtake contracts, and regulated approaches exist; effective combinations differ by technology and institutional setting.
why: Laboratory success can stall before the operating evidence needed for ordinary finance exists.
key_works: National Academies (2023), advanced-reactor report, DOI:10.17226/26630; IEA, capital-cost observatory.

title: Credible coal-transition support for affected communities
subfield: Energy access, markets, institutions, and funding
open: Retire or transform coal-dependent assets while providing durable employment, local fiscal replacement, land restoration, and reliable energy rather than short-lived compensation alone.
status: Transition programs exist; outcomes depend on regional economic structure and implementation.
why: Unaddressed local losses can undermine otherwise beneficial system-wide transitions.
key_works: IEA (2022), *Coal in Net Zero Transitions*.

title: Shared fusion qualification infrastructure
subfield: Energy access, markets, institutions, and funding
open: Fund and govern shared facilities for materials, blankets, fuel-cycle components, and integrated testing with usable access, comparable measurements, and publication of failures as well as successes.
status: The 2026 DOE roadmap and ORNL’s FULCRA-related collaboration recognize infrastructure needs; announced coordination is not equivalent to complete operating capability.
why: Individual developers cannot efficiently duplicate every expensive qualification environment.
key_works: DOE (2026), fusion roadmap; ORNL (2026), *ORNL, REV launch innovative collaboration on fusion infrastructure*.

title: Exact quasisymmetry throughout a finite plasma volume
open: Construct a genuinely non-axisymmetric, finite-volume toroidal equilibrium with exactly quasisymmetric magnetic-field strength, smooth scalar pressure, and physically realizable boundary conditions—or prove nonexistence under clearly specified assumptions.
status: Extremely accurate numerical quasisymmetry is established, but numerical smallness is not exact existence. Landreman’s September 2026 analytic-equilibrium work explicitly retains exact quasisymmetric equilibria as a question beyond its constructions.
why: Separates fundamental geometric restrictions from limitations of numerical optimization.
key_works: M. Landreman and E. Paul (2022), *Magnetic Fields with Precise Quasisymmetry for Plasma Confinement*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.035001; Landreman (2026), arXiv:2609.26742.

title: Exact nested-surface, non-axisymmetric vacuum fields
open: Construct an analytic, non-axisymmetric vacuum magnetic field in a torus embedded in ordinary three-dimensional space, with globally nested invariant surfaces and nontrivial rotational transform, or establish the relevant obstruction.
status: Special topological-torus constructions and approximate numerical configurations exist. The 2026 analytic pressure-supported equilibria do not automatically supply the corresponding vacuum-field construction.
why: Would clarify which confinement geometries can exist without plasma-current assistance.
key_works: W. Weitzner and W. Sengupta (2020), *Exact non-symmetric closed line vacuum magnetic fields in a topological torus*, Physics of Plasmas 27, 022509; Landreman (2026), arXiv:2609.26742.

title: Structural stability of smooth three-dimensional MHD equilibria
open: Determine which smooth, nested-surface, non-axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic equilibria persist under small boundary, pressure-profile, and current-profile perturbations, and which survive only in exceptional families.
status: September 2026 preprints construct counterexamples to forms of Grad’s conjecture. Consequently, unrestricted non-axisymmetric existence must not simply be relisted as open; robustness and classification remain distinct questions.
why: An exact equilibrium is not necessarily a configuration that manufacturing and operation can preserve.
key_works: J. Gómez-Serrano, L. Liehr, and M. A. Taylor (2026), *Counterexamples to Grad’s conjecture*, arXiv:2609.24739.

title: Convergence of all-orders near-axis expansions
open: Establish convergence radii or useful remainder bounds for stellarator near-axis expansions, including finite pressure, rather than only generating formal coefficients to arbitrary order.
status: An all-orders axis-expansion framework was developed in 2024. Formal solvability does not establish convergence at the finite minor radius needed by an actual device.
why: Converts a powerful design construction into a quantitatively certified approximation.
key_works: W. Sengupta et al. (2024), *Stellarator equilibrium axis-expansion to all orders in distance from the axis for arbitrary plasma beta*, arXiv:2402.17034; DOI:10.1017/S002237782400076X.

title: A physically calibrated quasisymmetry-error metric
open: Develop a computable quasisymmetry-error measure with bounds on relevant transport or particle-loss observables across energy, pitch angle, collisionality, and equilibrium variation.
status: Existing measures need not rank configurations consistently. The 2022 comparison of quasisymmetry measures demonstrates why minimizing a convenient geometric norm is not equivalent to minimizing every physical loss.
why: Prevents optimization from improving a surrogate while worsening confinement.
key_works: E. Rodríguez, E. J. Paul, and A. Bhattacharjee (2022), *Measures of quasisymmetry for stellarators*, arXiv:2109.13080; DOI:10.1017/S0022377821001331.

title: Physical validity of iso-action confinement
open: Determine when iso-action or symmetry-agnostic confinement survives finite orbit width, collisions, profile evolution, and realizable coil errors, rather than only the ordering used to derive the confinement criterion.
status: Sengupta, Bhattacharjee, and Buller introduced a symmetry-agnostic construction in August 2026 using modulation theory and a solvable model. Reactor-relevant robustness remains a separate validation task.
why: Could enlarge the design space beyond conventional quasisymmetric and quasi-isodynamic configurations.
key_works: W. Sengupta, A. Bhattacharjee, and S. Buller (2026), *Symmetry-agnostic stellarators for collisionless confinement*, arXiv:2608.20042.

title: Lower bounds on the non-maximum-J particle fraction
open: Derive tight bounds on the fraction of trapped particles that cannot satisfy the maximum-J condition under specified vacuum-field, smoothness, aspect-ratio, and engineering constraints.
status: A 2024 study constructed a vacuum configuration in which approximately 99.6% of trapped particles satisfy maximum-J, while identifying difficulties associated with barely trapped particles. That result does not establish a universal attainable bound.
why: Quantifies how close optimized configurations can approach favorable trapped-particle behavior.
key_works: E. Rodríguez, P. Helander, and A. G. Goodman (2024), *The maximum-J property in quasi-isodynamic stellarators*, arXiv:2311.14439.

title: Collisional boundary layers in piecewise-omnigenous fields
open: Determine the transport produced near boundaries between differently trapped orbit classes in piecewise-omnigenous fields, including collisions, finite orbit width, and realistic smoothing of idealized geometry.
status: Piecewise omnigenity was introduced in 2024 with favorable transport properties. The construction does not eliminate the need to resolve transitions between orbit regions.
why: Tests whether a larger, more manufacturable confinement family retains its apparent transport advantage.
key_works: J. L. Velasco et al. (2024), *Piecewise omnigenous stellarators*, arXiv:2405.07634; DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.185101.

title: Robust zero-bootstrap-current stellarators
open: Preserve acceptably small bootstrap current when a nominally zero-bootstrap configuration experiences finite collisionality, changing pressure profiles, impurities, and coil perturbations.
status: A 2025 construction establishes piecewise-omnigenous configurations with zero bootstrap current under its assumptions. Operational robustness is not implied by exact cancellation in the design calculation.
why: Reduces equilibrium drift and the need for active current-profile compensation.
key_works: I. Calvo et al. (2025), *Piecewise omnigenous stellarators with zero bootstrap current*, arXiv:2505.02546; DOI:10.1103/tnh1-mq88.

title: Simultaneous optimization of all turbulent transport channels
open: Optimize ion heat, electron heat, fuel-particle, impurity, and helium-ash transport together without assuming that improvement in one turbulence metric improves the others.
status: Low-turbulence quasi-isodynamic reactor candidates were reported in 2024. Integrated optimization across channels and self-consistent evolving profiles remains more demanding than optimizing selected fluxes.
why: Good heat confinement can coexist with undesirable impurity accumulation or inadequate fueling.
key_works: A. G. Goodman et al. (2024), *Quasi-Isodynamic Stellarators with Low Turbulence as Fusion Reactor Candidates*, arXiv:2405.19860; DOI:10.1103/PRXEnergy.3.023010.

title: Certified localized fast-ion wall-load tails
open: Bound the probability and spatial concentration of energetic-particle losses over complete birth distributions and uncertain equilibria, rather than reporting only average lost-particle fractions.
status: Direct fast-ion optimization and identification of loss mechanisms are established. Low average loss does not certify that rare trajectories cannot concentrate damaging power on a small wall region.
why: Protects components against losses hidden by aggregate confinement metrics.
key_works: D. Bindel, M. Landreman, and M. Padidar (2023), *Direct optimization of fast-ion confinement in stellarators*, PPCF 65, 065012; E. J. Paul et al. (2022), *Energetic particle loss mechanisms in reactor-scale equilibria close to quasisymmetry*, Nuclear Fusion 62, 126054.

title: Performance-based stellarator coil tolerances
open: Allocate fabrication and positioning tolerances according to their effect on confinement, islands, and localized losses, including correlated errors and achievable correction-coil actions.
status: Coil optimization for quasi-helical configurations has advanced; a small magnetic-field fitting error is not a complete tolerance specification.
why: Avoids both unnecessarily expensive tolerances and inexpensive errors with disproportionate consequences.
key_works: A. V. Wiedman, S. Buller, and M. Landreman (2024), *Coil optimization for quasi-helically symmetric stellarator configurations*, Journal of Plasma Physics 90, 905900307.

title: Kinetic validation of the L–H power-threshold mechanism
open: Predict transition thresholds across machines using independently measured inputs, including regimes where kinetic electrons, neutral interactions, electromagnetic turbulence, and geometry challenge reduced-fluid assumptions.
status: A May 2026 preprint derives threshold behavior, a density minimum, and field-direction asymmetry from three-dimensional flux-driven two-fluid simulations. Broad kinetic and experimental validation remains the next discriminator.
why: Makes access to high confinement predictable before constructing a new device.
key_works: B. De Lucca et al. (2026), *The L-H transition in tokamaks: power threshold, density minimum and toroidal-field asymmetry*, arXiv:2605.00624.

title: Causal origin of L–H field-direction asymmetry
open: Experimentally separate collisionality-driven symmetry breaking from neutral, orbit-loss, and geometric explanations of the difference between favorable and unfavorable magnetic-field directions.
status: The 2026 two-fluid theory supplies a specific collisionality-based mechanism. Distinguishing that mechanism from correlated changes in experiments remains open.
why: Identifies which design or operating changes can actually lower the threshold.
key_works: De Lucca et al. (2026), *The L-H transition in tokamaks*, arXiv:2605.00624; F. Ryter et al. (2014), *Experimental evidence for the key role of the ion heat channel in the physics of the L-H transition*, Nuclear Fusion 54, 083003.

title: Predicting pedestal density without prescribing it
open: Predict pedestal density and temperature profiles jointly from fueling, recycling, neutral penetration, turbulence, and stability rather than supplying density as an external input to a pedestal-height model.
status: EPED established a successful stability-based framework for pedestal height and width. A closed prediction of particle balance and the entire pedestal state is a stronger requirement.
why: Density assumptions strongly affect predicted fusion performance and operating margins.
key_works: P. B. Snyder et al. (2011), *A first-principles predictive model of the pedestal height and width: development, testing and ITER optimization with the EPED model*.

title: Nonlinear saturation of pedestal microtearing turbulence
open: Predict saturated electron heat transport from global pedestal microtearing modes, including profile evolution, magnetic stochasticity, and interaction with other instability families.
status: Global microtearing theory and mode identification have advanced. Identifying a linear instability does not establish its nonlinear transport contribution.
why: Addresses an electron-energy-loss channel not captured by a stability boundary alone.
key_works: J. L. Larakers et al. (2021), *Global Theory of Microtearing Modes in the Tokamak Pedestal*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.126.225001; D. Dickinson et al. (2012), *Microtearing modes at the top of the pedestal*, arXiv:1209.3695.

title: Predictive isotope scaling of core heat transport
open: Explain and predict how replacing hydrogen, deuterium, or tritium changes heat transport while independently controlling heating deposition, density profiles, rotation, and impurity content.
status: A 2025 JET study combines deuterium–tritium comparisons with gyrokinetic simulations. Agreement for selected discharges does not establish a transferable isotope-scaling law.
why: Reduces uncertainty when extrapolating nontritium experiments to burning plasmas.
key_works: JET Contributors (2025), *Experimental study and gyrokinetic simulations of isotope effects on core heat transport in JET tokamak deuterium and tritium plasmas*, DOI:10.1088/1741-4326/adab04.

title: Isotope dependence of zonal-flow regulation
open: Establish when isotope-dependent zonal-flow generation, damping, and residual response explain confinement changes, and when other mechanisms dominate.
status: Gyrokinetic calculations explicitly examining isotope effects on zonal-flow response were published in 2025. Their connection to complete, experimentally observed confinement changes remains to be quantified.
why: Provides a mechanistic alternative to empirical isotope correction factors.
key_works: S. Li et al. (2025), *Gyrokinetic simulation of isotope effect on zonal flow response in tokamaks*, Physics of Plasmas 32, 023902.

title: Separate control of core and edge density saturation
open: Develop controls that independently postpone edge radiative saturation and core avalanche-like transport in negative-triangularity plasmas without exchanging one limit for the other.
status: Hong et al. report sustained operation up to 1.8 times the Greenwald density and distinguish core and edge mechanisms. Exceeding the empirical Greenwald value itself is therefore not the open problem.
why: Expands usable density through identified mechanisms rather than a single empirical ceiling.
key_works: R. Hong et al. (2026), *Disentangling Core and Edge Mechanisms of the Density Limit in DIII-D Negative Triangularity Plasmas*, arXiv:2504.02773; DOI:10.1088/1741-4326/ae1c50.

title: Reactor-relevant impurity seeding in negative triangularity
open: Maintain favorable confinement and particle exhaust while radiating a large fraction of input power using reactor-relevant impurities, without unacceptable core accumulation.
status: Highly radiating negative-triangularity plasmas have been demonstrated; the remaining problem is a transferable operating window with self-consistent impurity transport.
why: A confinement configuration must also solve its exhaust problem.
key_works: L. Casali et al. (2025), *Achievement of highly radiating plasmas in negative triangularity and effect of reactor-relevant seeded impurities on confinement and transport*; A. Marinoni, O. Sauter, and S. Coda (2021), *A brief history of negative triangularity tokamak plasmas*.

title: Reactor-scale scrape-off-layer heat-width prediction
open: Predict divertor heat-flux width across the transition from present devices to reactor-scale plasmas, resolving the competing roles of magnetic drifts, turbulence, and machine size.
status: Heuristic scaling and large kinetic simulations provide different forms of evidence. A validated extrapolation across the relevant regime change remains necessary.
why: Small errors in heat width translate into large errors in component heat loading.
key_works: R. J. Goldston (2012), *Heuristic drift-based model of the power scrape-off width in low-gas-puff H-mode tokamaks*; PPPL (2021), research account of XGC reactor-scale divertor-heat-load simulations.

title: Nonlocal parallel heat-flux closure without tuning
open: Replace empirical flux limiters with reduced closures that reproduce kinetic parallel heat transport through steep, evolving edge gradients without discharge-specific tuning.
status: Nonlocal kernels and kinetic comparisons were developed in 2018, and subsequent scrape-off-layer studies incorporated nonlocal transport. General accuracy across rapidly changing collisionality remains unresolved.
why: Improves predictions of detachment, transient heat loads, and target temperatures.
key_works: G. Ciraolo et al. (2018), *Fluid and kinetic modelling for non-local heat transport in magnetic fusion devices*, arXiv:1801.01177; DOI:10.1002/ctpp.201700222.

title: Kinetic sheath boundary conditions for evolving electron distributions
open: Derive practical wall boundary conditions that remain accurate when the incident electron distribution is non-Maxwellian, anisotropic, or rapidly evolving.
status: Ciraolo et al. model contributions from suprathermal particles that become important at low collisionality. A fixed heat-transmission coefficient cannot represent every such distribution.
why: Incorrect boundary conditions can invalidate otherwise sophisticated upstream simulations.
key_works: Ciraolo et al. (2018), *Fluid and kinetic modelling for non-local heat transport*, arXiv:1801.01177.

title: Quantitative molecular-recombination networks for seeded divertors
open: Determine isotope-resolved reaction rates and population balances for molecular-assisted recombination involving nitrogen–hydrogen compounds under actual divertor conditions.
status: Hydronitrogen-assisted recombination was demonstrated in ammonia-seeded deuterium plasma in 2019. Its quantified contribution in complex divertor mixtures requires broader conditions and diagnostic closure.
why: Molecular chemistry can alter particle removal and the inferred detachment balance.
key_works: S. Abe et al. (2019), *Hydronitrogen Molecular Assisted Recombination (HN-MAR) process in ammonia seeded deuterium plasmas*, DOI:10.1016/j.nme.2019.03.011.

title: Runaway-avalanche prediction during impurity injection
open: Predict runaway-electron multiplication while impurity charge states, electric fields, radiation, and plasma temperature evolve together during mitigation.
status: Partially ionized impurities can change avalanche generation substantially; dedicated models show that simply increasing injected material does not guarantee suppression.
why: Avoids mitigation strategies that reduce thermal loads while worsening energetic-electron risk.
key_works: L. Hesslow et al. (2019), *Influence of massive material injection on avalanche runaway generation during tokamak disruptions*; Hesslow (2020), *Kinetic modeling of runaway-electron dynamics in partially ionized plasmas*.

title: Error-controlled switching between runaway-electron models
open: Construct adaptive models that switch between reduced and kinetic runaway descriptions while preserving the evolving distribution and bounding errors in predicted seed populations.
status: Olasz et al. identified a collision-timescale criterion for failure of quasi-stationary Dreicer approximations in 2021. A complete error-controlled switching scheme is a stronger requirement.
why: Makes integrated disruption simulations affordable without silently losing essential kinetic memory.
key_works: S. Olasz et al. (2021), *Validity of models for Dreicer generation of runaway electrons in dynamic scenarios*, arXiv:2101.02740; DOI:10.1088/1741-4326/abf0de.

title: Tungsten nanostructure evolution under mixed particle fluxes
open: Predict how helium exposure, simultaneous metal deposition, temperature, and transients determine tungsten-fuzz growth, erosion, and release into the plasma.
status: Experiments demonstrate enhanced large-scale nanostructure growth when metallic-ion precipitation accompanies helium exposure. Pure-helium growth laws therefore do not cover every relevant surface history.
why: Surface morphology can change sputtering, thermal response, and impurity generation.
key_works: S. Kajita et al. (2018), *Enhanced growth of large-scale nanostructures with metallic ion precipitation in helium plasmas*, DOI:10.1038/s41598-017-18476-7.

title: Tritium inventory from evolving tungsten defect populations
open: Infer and predict retained tritium when irradiation defects, helium bubbles, grain boundaries, and surface deposits evolve during service rather than remaining fixed trapping sites.
status: Laboratory retention studies identify strong material-history effects. Extrapolating those measurements to simultaneous neutron, thermal, and plasma exposure remains unresolved.
why: Connects material degradation to recoverable fuel inventory and component handling.
key_works: E. Bernard et al. (2019), *Tritium retention in W plasma-facing materials: Impact of…* — full subtitle **(verify)**, Nuclear Materials and Energy, article PII:S2352179118302424.

title: Predictive high-Z-dopant tradeoffs in ablator instability
open: Predict when a dopant reduces instability growth but worsens the initial perturbation transmitted from an internal interface, including three-dimensional spherical geometry.
status: Xiong et al. show that dopants can affect instability seeding and later growth differently. Their 2025 calculations do not establish a universal optimum for realistic defect spectra.
why: Prevents mitigation of one instability stage from strengthening another.
key_works: W. Xiong et al. (2025), *Evolution of the rippled inner-interface-initiated ablative Rayleigh-Taylor instability in laser-ablating high-Z doped targets*, arXiv:2505.02715.

title: Equation-of-state uncertainty propagated to implosion outcomes
open: Determine which equation-of-state uncertainties materially change implosion timing, compression, and ignition margin, and design measurements that discriminate between competing models.
status: Gaffney et al. documented differences among equation-of-state models for fusion materials in 2018. Agreement in one thermodynamic region does not validate an entire implosion trajectory.
why: Targets experiments at uncertainties that actually govern predictive error.
key_works: J. A. Gaffney et al. (2018), *A Review of Equation-of-State Models for Inertial Confinement Fusion Materials*, OSTI:1476340.

title: Spatiotemporal mix reconstruction from radiochemical products
open: Recover when, where, and how much ablator material mixed with fuel using radiochemical products together with other diagnostics, while quantifying nonuniqueness.
status: A 2025 study measured technetium–molybdenum isotope ratios across a NIF campaign. Integrated product yields constrain mix but do not uniquely reconstruct its complete history.
why: Distinguishes different failure mechanisms that produce similar final yields.
key_works: K. N. Kmak et al. (2025), *Using radiochemistry to diagnose fuel-ablator mix in inertial confinement fusion studies at the National Ignition Facility…*, DOI:10.3389/fchem.2025.1632948.

title: Single-shot crossed-beam diagnostics in nonuniform implosion plasmas
open: Infer spatially varying plasma conditions from broadband pump–probe measurements when gradients, multiple beam interactions, and time evolution invalidate homogeneous-plasma assumptions.
status: Longman et al. demonstrated single-shot measurements of crossed-beam energy-transfer spectra in 2025. Extending the diagnostic to strongly nonuniform operating environments remains a separate task.
why: Supplies measurements needed to validate laser-energy-transfer models.
key_works: A. Longman et al. (2025), *Pump with Broadband Probe Experiments for Single-Shot Measurements of Plasma Conditions and Crossed-Beam Energy Transfer*, DOI:10.1103/96yh-96pw.

title: Broadband-driver crossed-beam energy-transfer control
open: Predict and control the net redistribution of laser energy among many beams when bandwidth, plasma flow, nonlinear saturation, and evolving ion-acoustic response interact.
status: Broadband probing now provides direct experimental leverage on crossed-beam interactions. A useful diagnostic is not yet a validated many-beam control law.
why: Improves drive symmetry without depending on empirical adjustments for each configuration.
key_works: Longman et al. (2025), crossed-beam pump–probe study, DOI:10.1103/96yh-96pw; R. Betti and O. A. Hurricane (2016), *Inertial-confinement fusion with lasers*, DOI:10.1038/nphys3736.

title: Inter-shot chamber clearing for inertial-fusion plants
open: Remove or redistribute vapor, aerosols, and debris quickly enough for repeatable target injection and laser propagation while preserving chamber surfaces and useful plant availability.
status: Demonstration-reactor planning identifies chamber and repetition-rate integration as requirements beyond individual successful shots. Clearing cannot be assessed independently of target and chamber design.
why: The next shot must encounter acceptable conditions left by the previous one.
key_works: P. A. Norreys et al. (2021), *Preparations for a European R&D roadmap for an inertial fusion demonstration reactor*, Philosophical Transactions A 379, 20200005.

title: Irradiated breeder-pebble-bed contact mechanics
open: Predict how pebble swelling, fracture, rearrangement, and thermal expansion alter effective conductivity, local stress, purge flow, and tritium release throughout blanket operation.
status: European helium-cooled pebble-bed designs include detailed thermal and mechanical analyses. Lifetime behavior requires coupled evolution rather than fixed effective material properties.
why: Local contact changes can create hot spots and alter fuel recovery.
key_works: G. Zhou et al. (2023), *The European DEMO Helium Cooled Pebble Bed Breeding Blanket: Design Status at the Conclusion of the Pre-Concept Design Phase*, DOI:10.3390/en16145377.

title: Magnetohydrodynamic flow distribution in blanket networks
open: Predict flow partition, stagnation, pressure loss, and heat transfer throughout conducting liquid-metal blanket networks under strong, nonuniform magnetic fields.
status: Detailed lead–lithium blanket architectures and component analyses exist. Channel-level predictions do not automatically establish behavior of interconnected manifolds and penetrations.
why: Poor flow distribution can compromise both heat removal and tritium extraction.
key_works: P. Arena et al. (2023), *Design and Integration of the EU-DEMO Water-Cooled Lead Lithium Breeding Blanket*.

title: Where the solid-electrolyte interphase actually grows
open: Determine the reaction locations and moving growth fronts within heterogeneous interphases as electrolyte composition, electrode potential, and age change.
status: Isotope-assisted depth profiling demonstrated bottom-up growth in a studied system in 2018. A single mechanism should not be assumed universal across chemistries and cycling histories.
why: Growth location determines which species must cross the interphase and how passivation can be improved.
key_works: Z. Liu et al. (2018), *A Bottom-Up Formation Mechanism of Solid Electrolyte Interphase Revealed by Isotope-Assisted Time-of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry*, DOI:10.1021/acs.jpclett.8b02350.

title: Self-limiting decomposition at lithium–argyrodite interfaces
open: Establish when interphase formation at lithium–argyrodite contacts stops, continues slowly, or reactivates, using a model that includes transport through the evolving products.
status: Atomistic simulations reported a two-step growth mechanism in 2024. Nanosecond-scale calculations do not establish long-duration passivation.
why: Distinguishes a tolerable initial reaction from continuous electrolyte consumption.
key_works: G. Chaney et al. (2024), *Two-step growth mechanism of the solid electrolyte interphase in argyrodyte/Li-metal contacts*, arXiv:2402.04095.

title: Why lithium fluoride sometimes helps and sometimes does not
open: Identify which spatial arrangements, interfaces, defect populations, and mechanical properties make lithium-fluoride-containing interphases beneficial, rather than treating lithium fluoride concentration alone as causal.
status: Studies show synergistic effects among inorganic interphase components. Correlation between lithium fluoride abundance and performance does not identify the controlling mechanism.
why: Replaces a widely used compositional heuristic with design rules.
key_works: Q. Zhang et al. (2016), *Synergetic effects of inorganic components in solid electrolyte interphase on high cycle efficiency of lithium ion batteries*.

title: Electron leakage through nominally insulating interphases
open: Quantify electronic transport through interphase defects, grain boundaries, tunneling paths, and mixed phases, and connect it to continued electrolyte reduction.
status: Interphase chemistry and morphology are increasingly resolved, but bulk insulating properties do not directly determine leakage through a nanoscale heterogeneous layer.
why: Explains why apparently passivating products can still permit long-term consumption.
key_works: M. S. Johnson et al. (2025), *Solid Electrolyte Interphase Formation in Lithium Batteries*, DOI:10.1021/acs.jpcc.5c00507; Chaney et al. (2024), arXiv:2402.04095.

title: Interlaboratory-consistent transference numbers
open: Establish measurement and reporting procedures that distinguish true transport coefficients from method-dependent apparent transference numbers in concentrated electrolytes.
status: Shao and Zhang derived the Bruce–Vincent quantity from Onsager coefficients in 2023. That theoretical reconciliation does not automatically calibrate every experimental protocol or reference-frame convention.
why: Prevents electrolyte selection based on incomparable transport measurements.
key_works: Y. Shao and C. Zhang (2023), *Bruce-Vincent transference numbers from molecular dynamics simulations*, arXiv:2302.07017; DOI:10.1063/5.0146608.

title: Transport closure far from electrolyte equilibrium
open: Predict ion transport under steep concentration gradients and rapidly changing solvation without assuming that equilibrium transport coefficients remain locally adequate.
status: Equilibrium molecular dynamics can connect measurable and fundamental coefficients. Extending that connection to strongly driven, spatially heterogeneous battery operation requires additional validation.
why: Fast charging and thick electrodes create conditions unlike uniform equilibrium measurements.
key_works: Shao and Zhang (2023), *Bruce-Vincent transference numbers from molecular dynamics simulations*, DOI:10.1063/5.0146608.

title: Generalized Sand-time prediction in heterogeneous cells
open: Predict local salt depletion and its relation to unstable deposition when transport properties, geometry, interphase resistance, and current distribution vary spatially and temporally.
status: Sand-type depletion arguments remain useful, including for solid-state systems, but idealized one-dimensional assumptions do not determine the first failing location in a heterogeneous cell.
why: Links charging limits to local rather than average transport conditions.
key_works: L. Stolz et al. (2021), *The Sand Equation and Its Enormous Practical Relevance for Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries*, DOI:10.1016/j.mattod.2020.11.025.

title: Agreement between inactive-lithium quantification methods
open: Reconcile chemical titration, magnetic resonance, microscopy, and electrochemical accounting for electrically isolated metal, trapped ions, and chemically consumed lithium.
status: Quantitative inactive-lithium methods and noninvasive NMR have been demonstrated. Different observables and sample handling can still produce incompatible partitions.
why: Mechanism-specific improvement requires knowing which inventory-loss process dominates.
key_works: C. Fang et al. (2019), *Quantifying inactive lithium in lithium metal batteries*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-019-1481-z; A. B. Gunnarsdóttir et al. (2020), *Noninvasive In Situ NMR Study of “Dead Lithium” Formation and Lithium Corrosion in Full-Cell Lithium Metal Batteries*.

title: Separating calendar corrosion from cycling-induced lithium loss
open: Quantify lithium consumption during rest independently of deposition and stripping losses, including changes caused by state of charge and previous morphology.
status: In-situ NMR has resolved both dead-lithium formation and corrosion. A transferable model for arbitrary rest–cycle histories remains more demanding than identifying both mechanisms.
why: High cycling efficiency can coexist with poor calendar life.
key_works: Gunnarsdóttir et al. (2020), *Noninvasive In Situ NMR Study of “Dead Lithium” Formation and Lithium Corrosion in Full-Cell Lithium Metal Batteries*, PMCID:PMC7729915.

title: Quantifying cryogenic-microscopy preparation artifacts
open: Measure how freezing, transfer, vacuum exposure, sectioning, and electron dose alter battery interfaces before or during imaging.
status: Cryogenic electron microscopy greatly improves access to fragile interfaces, but the 2021 workflow assessment documents the importance of preparation and interpretation.
why: A high-resolution image is not necessarily a faithful operating-state measurement.
key_works: S. Weng, Y. Li, and X. Wang (2021), *Cryo-EM for battery materials and interfaces: Workflow, achievements, and perspectives*, DOI:10.1016/j.isci.2021.103402.

title: Linking frozen interphase snapshots to operating potential
open: Preserve a known electrochemical state during rapid trapping and establish the temporal resolution with which cryogenic snapshots represent evolving interfaces.
status: Electrified cryo-EM was introduced in a 2024 preprint to trap dynamic nanointerfaces. Its general temporal fidelity and applicability across chemistries remain validation questions.
why: Connects observed nanostructures to the reactions that produced them.
key_works: C. Wang et al. (2024), *Trapping and imaging dynamic battery nanointerfaces via electrified cryo-EM*, DOI:10.21203/rs.3.rs-4920923/v1.

title: Quantitative electrode-to-electrode chemical cross-talk
open: Attribute degradation to transported metal ions, dissolved organic products, gases, and acid-generating species using species-resolved flux and reaction balances.
status: Cross-talk mechanisms and high-voltage transition-metal crossover are established. Isolated half-cell testing cannot reproduce the complete coupled reaction network.
why: Prevents optimizing an electrode in conditions that omit its dominant full-cell damage source.
key_works: O. C. Harris et al. (2020), *Review: Mechanisms and Consequences of Chemical Cross-Talk in Advanced Li-Ion Batteries*, Journal of Physics: Energy 2, 032002; W. Li et al. (2023), *Crossover effects of transition metal ions in high-voltage lithium metal batteries*, DOI:10.1007/s12274-022-5334-y.

title: Identifiability limits for impending battery-aging knees
open: Determine which abrupt-aging precursors can be identified from ordinary voltage, current, and temperature data, and prove when extra sensing or diagnostic excitation is necessary.
status: The 2022 knee review distinguishes hidden, threshold, and accelerating pathways. Some precursors can remain weakly visible in conventional capacity measurements.
why: Establishes the limits of prediction rather than promising that a larger model will always detect failure early.
key_works: P. M. Attia et al. (2022), *“Knees” in lithium-ion battery aging trajectories*, arXiv:2201.02891.

title: Microstructure-to-knee prediction through percolation
open: Predict when gradual pore blockage, contact loss, or conductive-network damage causes a sharp performance transition, using measurable microstructure rather than fitted knee locations.
status: Percolation and threshold mechanisms are recognized explanations for knees. Quantitative prediction across realistic evolving electrode networks remains incomplete.
why: Connects abrupt macroscopic aging to controllable microscopic design features.
key_works: Attia et al. (2022), *“Knees” in lithium-ion battery aging trajectories*, arXiv:2201.02891.

title: The useful-water window in Prussian-blue cathodes
open: Distinguish beneficial structural water from harmful water populations and control their evolution during manufacturing, storage, and cycling.
status: Water removal improves some systems, while other studies report structural benefits from retained water. Rehydration and vacancy chemistry complicate any universal “dry is better” rule.
why: Resolves a processing tradeoff affecting capacity, calendar life, and reproducibility.
key_works: W. Wang et al. (2022), *Effect of Eliminating Water in Prussian Blue Cathode for Sodium-Ion Batteries*; Q. Li et al. (2026), *Balancing crystal water and cyanide vacancies in Prussian blue analogues towards ultrastable potassium-ion storage*, DOI:10.1016/j.cej.2026.178250.

title: Cyanide-vacancy-controlled spin and lattice transitions
open: Predict how the concentration and spatial arrangement of cyanide vacancies determine spin transitions, lattice distortion, ion transport, and irreversible framework change.
status: A 2025 study introduced tunable vacancy synthesis and a vacancy-driven mechanism. A transferable configuration-level theory remains beyond a single composition series.
why: Turns “defect reduction” into targeted defect engineering.
key_works: X. Gao et al. (2025), *Unveiling the Influence of Cyanogen Vacancies in Prussian Blue for Sodium-ion Batteries*.

title: Predicting cation-vacancy ordering in Prussian-blue analogues
open: Determine which cation-vacancy patterns improve reversible insertion without destabilizing the host, and how synthesis selects those patterns.
status: Liu et al. reported new insights into cation vacancies in 2026. Average composition alone does not specify the ordering and local environments relevant to insertion.
why: Enables reproducible synthesis rather than empirical tuning of nominal stoichiometry.
key_works: J. Liu et al. (2026), *Insights into Cationic Vacancies in a Prussian Blue Analogues Cathode for Enhanced Reversible Sodium Insertion*, DOI:10.1021/jacsau.6c00272.

title: Synthesis-to-percolation control in disordered-rocksalt cathodes
open: Predict how synthesis history fixes short-range order and thereby the connected lithium-migration network, including its evolution during cycling.
status: A 2025 study maps local tetrahedral probabilities and short-range order. Those maps do not alone establish processing routes that reproducibly produce an optimal transport network.
why: Disorder is useful only when the resulting pathways remain connected.
key_works: T.-C. Liu, S. B. Torrisi, and C. Wolverton (2025), *Short-Range Order and LiₓTM₄₋ₓ Probability Maps for Disordered Rocksalt Cathodes*, arXiv:2508.08112.

title: Causal contribution of singlet oxygen to lithium–oxygen degradation
open: Quantify when singlet oxygen is a dominant degradation agent and when other reactive intermediates or direct electrochemical pathways dominate.
status: A 2024 paper argues that singlet oxygen is not the main electrolyte-degradation source in its systems; later work reports improved life through singlet-oxygen suppression. These findings require condition-specific reconciliation, not blanket acceptance of either claim.
why: Identifies which protective strategies address the actual limiting chemistry.
key_works: C. Zor et al. (2024), *Singlet oxygen is not the main source of electrolyte degradation in lithium–oxygen batteries*; K. Chae et al. (2025), DOI:10.1007/s40820-025-01885-z.

title: Regenerable redox mediators for oxygen batteries
open: Maintain mediator activity through repeated operation while preventing chemical attack, crossover, irreversible conversion, and contamination of the opposite electrode.
status: Mediators can reduce reaction overpotentials, but research demonstrates deactivation pathways, including reactions involving singlet oxygen.
why: A catalyst-like additive must remain catalytic rather than become a hidden consumable.
key_works: Argonne National Laboratory publication record, *Deactivation of redox mediators in lithium-oxygen batteries by singlet oxygen*, publication 151608.

title: Calcium–oxygen cells under practical reactant inventories
open: Retain useful energy density and lifetime with limited electrolyte, realistic electrode loading, and controlled gas handling rather than favorable laboratory inventories.
status: Ye et al. demonstrated room-temperature calcium–oxygen cycling, including a reported 700-cycle experiment, in 2024. Room-temperature rechargeability itself is no longer the open target.
why: Determines whether an intriguing chemistry becomes a useful complete cell.
key_works: L. Ye et al. (2024), *A rechargeable calcium–oxygen battery that operates at room temperature*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06949-x.

title: Practical room-temperature fluoride-ion full cells
open: Combine sufficient fluoride-ion transport with reversible high-loading electrodes and limited electrolyte while controlling passivation and parasitic chemistry.
status: Room-temperature cycling of metal-fluoride electrodes was demonstrated in 2018. Full-cell practicality is a stronger requirement than that foundational result.
why: Tests a high-capacity anion-shuttle route without relying on elevated-temperature operation.
key_works: V. K. Davis et al. (2018), *Room-temperature cycling of metal fluoride electrodes: Liquid electrolytes for high-energy fluoride ion cells*, DOI:10.1126/science.aat7070.

title: Stable fluoride-conducting polymer electrolytes
open: Preserve fluoride conductivity, electrochemical stability, mechanical integrity, and useful electrode contact without relying on uncontrolled hydration or solvent excess.
status: A 2026 study develops a quaternary-ammonium fluoride-exchange membrane as a quasi-solid electrolyte. Long-lived full-cell compatibility remains distinct from membrane conductivity.
why: Could make fluoride-ion systems safer and easier to package.
key_works: F. M. Scesa et al. (2026), *Toward room temperature fluoride-ion batteries: quaternary ammonium-bearing fluoride-exchange membrane as a quasi-solid polymer electrolyte*, DOI:10.1016/j.ensm.2026.105410.

title: What stores charge in aqueous zinc–manganese-oxide cells?
open: Resolve the quantitative contributions of zinc insertion, proton insertion, conversion, dissolution, and redeposition as a function of electrolyte and operating history.
status: Proton-conversion behavior has been demonstrated for β-MnO₂. Calling every such device a zinc-ion intercalation battery can obscure materially different mechanisms.
why: Correct mechanisms are necessary for meaningful capacity, lifetime, and inventory accounting.
key_works: W. Liu et al. (2021), *β-MnO₂ with proton conversion mechanism in rechargeable zinc ion battery*, DOI:10.1016/j.jechem.2020.07.027.

title: Persistent low-overpotential aluminum deposition
open: Suppress the evolution of aluminum-deposition overpotential across long cycling while maintaining efficiency and compatibility with the complete aluminum–graphite cell.
status: A 2025 study directly addresses high deposition overpotential. Improvements must persist after surface evolution and electrolyte-composition changes rather than only during initial cycling.
why: Reduces voltage losses and prevents anode behavior from negating cathode improvements.
key_works: Mukundan et al. (2025), *Mitigating the Effect of High Overpotential during Al Deposition on Aluminium-Graphite Battery Performance*, DOI:10.1002/batt.202400718.

title: Chlorine confinement in rechargeable calcium–chlorine cells
open: Retain and reversibly use chlorine-containing cathode species at practical loading while preventing escape, crossover, and corrosive side reactions.
status: A rechargeable calcium–chlorine cell was demonstrated in 2024. The remaining target is a robust, contained full-cell architecture rather than first rechargeability.
why: High-energy conversion chemistry must be compatible with safe handling and durable materials.
key_works: *A rechargeable Ca/Cl₂ battery* (2024), DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-45347-3.

title: Tight topology-dependent counts of physically admissible power-flow solutions
open: Derive tight bounds on real, physically admissible solutions for specified network classes, including realistic voltage constraints and bus-control changes.
status: Algebraic bounds based on topology are established, but counts of complex roots or unconstrained real roots do not answer the operational question.
why: Clarifies multiplicity and supports complete rather than locally convergent solvers.
key_works: T. Chen and D. Mehta (2015), *On the Network Topology Dependent Solution Count of the Algebraic Load Flow Equations*, arXiv:1512.04987; D. K. Molzahn et al. (2015), arXiv:1509.09227.

title: Large certified uniqueness domains for realistic AC networks
open: Compute broad, efficiently checkable operating regions in which a realistic AC network has a unique admissible power-flow solution, with limited conservatism.
status: Monotonicity and graph-theoretic methods establish useful sufficient conditions. They do not completely characterize uniqueness for arbitrary networks and controls.
