open: Select sorbents and operating cycles using the complete effects of water on capacity, kinetics, regeneration energy, and productivity across varying climates.
status: Wang and Li quantified how co-adsorbed water affects direct-air-capture energy and productivity in 2025. Water can improve uptake while simultaneously increasing regeneration demands.
why: Maximizing dry-gas carbon-dioxide capacity can select the wrong material for humid ambient air.
key_works: Y. Wang and G. K. Li (2025), *The impact of co-adsorbed water on energy consumption and CO2 productivity in direct air capture systems*, DOI:10.1016/j.seppur.2024.129415.

title: Regime-dependent oxidation of amine sorbents
open: Predict when carbon dioxide accelerates or suppresses oxidative degradation as temperature, loading, water, and amine structure change during repeated cycles.
status: Li and colleagues demonstrated competing kinetic consequences of carbon dioxide for branched polyethylenimine oxidation in 2024. A single oxidation-rate constant cannot represent every operating state.
why: More conservative regeneration conditions are useful only when they actually reduce the dominant degradation pathway.
key_works: S. Li et al. (2024), *Competing Kinetic Consequences of CO2 on the Oxidative Degradation of Branched Poly(ethylenimine)*, JACS 146, 28201–28213.

title: Long-lived oxygen-tolerant electrochemical carbon capture
open: Maintain capture capacity and electrochemical efficiency in oxygen-containing feeds over long campaigns, including water variability and accumulation of trace reaction products.
status: Abdinejad and colleagues demonstrated an oxygen-stable redox-active capture chemistry in 2024. Oxygen tolerance in a selected experiment is not equivalent to complete long-term electrolyte stability.
why: Avoiding oxygen removal is valuable only if the capture medium survives direct exposure.
key_works: M. Abdinejad et al. (2024), *Oxygen-Stable Electrochemical CO2 Capture using Redox-Active Heterocyclic Benzodithiophene Quinone*, DOI:10.1002/anie.202412229.

title: Capture-affinity versus regeneration-voltage tradeoffs
open: Establish achievable relationships between carbon-dioxide binding, oxygen resistance, release conditions, and electrical work for redox-mediated capture chemistries.
status: Barlow and Yang showed that alcohol additives can enable oxygen-stable quinone capture under studied conditions. Stronger binding or improved oxygen resistance can alter the electrical and chemical work needed for regeneration.
why: Prevents molecular optimization from improving capture while making release disproportionately expensive.
key_works: J. M. Barlow and J. Y. Yang (2022), *Oxygen-Stable Electrochemical CO2 Capture and Concentration with Quinones Using Alcohol Additives*, JACS 144, 14161 onward.

title: Predictive water-dissociation kinetics at bipolar-membrane junctions
open: Predict water-dissociation rates from junction chemistry, electric field, hydration, and local structure without fitting a separate effective rate law for each membrane.
status: Oener, Foster, and Boettcher demonstrated accelerated water dissociation through interface engineering in 2020. The result supplies design leverage but not a complete transferable kinetic description.
why: Junction losses influence many electrochemical separation and conversion processes.
key_works: S. Z. Oener, M. J. Foster, and S. W. Boettcher (2020), *Accelerating water dissociation in bipolar membranes and for electrocatalysis*, DOI:10.1126/science.aaz1487.

title: Durable catalytic junctions in bipolar membranes
open: Preserve junction activity and adhesion during repeated hydration changes, pressure differences, current reversals, and exposure to realistic dissolved species.
status: Highly active junction catalysts have been demonstrated. Initial water-dissociation performance does not establish resistance to redistribution, delamination, or long-term chemical change.
why: A low-voltage membrane interface must remain intact through the operating cycle that makes the process useful.
key_works: Oener, Foster, and Boettcher (2020), bipolar-interface study, DOI:10.1126/science.aaz1487.

title: Sustained injectivity during rapid peridotite mineralization
open: Maintain adequate injection and flow while reactions consume carbon dioxide and change porosity, mineral volume, and fracture surfaces.
status: Matter and colleagues reported rapid peridotite mineralization in 2025. Demonstrating fast reaction does not establish sustained injectivity through repeated or prolonged operation.
why: A highly reactive rock can become operationally unattractive if it seals the pathways needed to use it.
key_works: J. M. Matter et al. (2025), *Rapid mineralisation of carbon dioxide in peridotites*, DOI:10.1038/s43247-025-02509-5.

title: Identifiability of mineralized carbon fractions from tracers
open: Determine when tracer and fluid measurements uniquely distinguish mineralization from dissolution, unobserved migration, sampling bias, and delayed recovery.
status: The 2025 peridotite study infers rapid mineralization using tracer-based balances. Such inference is powerful but should not be confused with direct enumeration of every newly formed solid.
why: Storage-credit and process-performance claims require explicit treatment of alternative explanations.
key_works: Matter et al. (2025), peridotite mineralization study, DOI:10.1038/s43247-025-02509-5.

title: Geometry-dependent passivation of reactive mineral fractures
open: Predict how fracture aperture and roughness determine the formation, location, and persistence of iron-oxide passivation layers.
status: Yang and colleagues demonstrated strong geometric control of passivation in olivine fractures in 2026. A bulk mineral dissolution rate does not capture these spatial effects.
why: Small-scale surface coatings can govern the usable capacity of a much larger rock volume.
key_works: Y. Yang et al. (2026), *Aperture and roughness govern iron oxide passivation in olivine fractures during carbon mineralization*, DOI:10.1038/s43247-026-03235-2.

title: Predicting when mineralization fractures rather than seals rock
open: Establish experimentally validated criteria for whether reaction-generated stress creates new accessible pathways or whether precipitation instead closes existing ones.
status: Reaction-induced fracture has been observed, and coupled fracture–geochemistry models continue to develop. Opposing outcomes depend on stress, reaction location, transport, and material properties.
why: The same volume-expanding reaction can either accelerate storage or terminate it.
key_works: W. Zhu et al. (2016), *Experimental evidence of reaction-induced fracturing during olivine carbonation*, DOI:10.1002/2016GL070834; R. Feng et al. (2025), *Coupled fracture mechanics-geochemical model of reaction-driven cracking*, DOI:10.1029/2025GL116162.

title: Accessing reactive capacity beyond connected fractures
open: Quantify how much mineral volume can react through matrix diffusion away from a sparse fracture network on useful operational timescales.
status: Novakowski’s 2026 analysis emphasizes fractures and matrix diffusion in mafic and ultramafic formations. Total mineral abundance does not determine the fraction that injected reactants can reach.
why: Resource estimates based only on rock composition can greatly exceed practically accessible storage.
key_works: K. Novakowski (2026), *The importance of fractures and matrix diffusion to the success of carbon mineralization in terrestrial mafic/ultramafic rock bodies*, DOI:10.5194/egusphere-egu26-15459.

title: Predicting dissolution–precipitation feedback from evolving surfaces
open: Couple dissolution, secondary precipitation, surface-area changes, and passivation so reaction rates remain predictive after the starting mineral surface has substantially changed.
status: Iyare and colleagues experimentally examined interacting dissolution and precipitation during olivine carbonation in 2025. Separately measured initial rates do not close the evolving coupled process.
why: Long-term conversion depends on the surface the reaction creates, not merely the surface it starts with.
key_works: U. C. Iyare et al. (2025), *Interaction between dissolution and precipitation during olivine carbonation: Implications for CO2 mineralization*, DOI:10.1016/j.chemgeo.2025.122645.

title: Low-water mineralization without hidden grinding penalties
open: Achieve useful carbon mineralization with limited water while counting the energy and material handling required to create sufficient reactive surface area.
status: Low-hydration basalt experiments demonstrate promising chemistry in prepared materials. Results obtained using finely processed samples do not establish the same benefit for intact formations or an energy-efficient industrial route.
why: Reducing water demand is not beneficial if the process requires excessive comminution energy.
key_works: *The future of carbon capture: Basalt’s role in low-hydration CO2 sequestration* (2025), DOI:10.1016/j.gsf.2025.102056.

title: Nucleation uncertainty in carbon-mineralization forecasts
open: Predict when and where secondary minerals nucleate, and propagate uncertainty in nucleation into conversion, passivation, and injectivity forecasts.
status: Boampong and colleagues explicitly examined nucleation-driven precipitation and secondary passivation in 2024. Assuming immediate local equilibrium can bypass the kinetics controlling actual mineral formation.
why: Similar fluid chemistry can produce different storage outcomes when nucleation histories differ.
key_works: L. Boampong et al. (2024), *Characterizing the combined impact of nucleation-driven precipitation and secondary passivation on carbon mineralization*, DOI:10.1016/j.chemgeo.2024.122256.

title: Flow-controlled precipitation without destructive clogging
open: Use flow conditions to promote useful mineralization while avoiding localized precipitation that blocks the available pathways.
status: Yang and colleagues showed in 2024 that fluid inertia can control precipitation and clogging from pore to network scales. Increasing flow or mixing is therefore not guaranteed to improve the complete outcome.
why: Efficient contact between reactants must be balanced against where the resulting solids accumulate.
key_works: W. Yang et al. (2024), *Fluid inertia controls mineral precipitation and clogging in pore to network-scale flows*, DOI:10.1073/pnas.2401318121.

title: Transferable mineralization predictions across fracture networks
open: Identify a small set of measurable network properties sufficient to predict mineralization and flow redistribution across heterogeneous three-dimensional fracture systems.
status: Hyman and colleagues investigated dominant controls on mineralization in fracture networks in 2024. Predictions remain sensitive to how connectivity and heterogeneity are represented.
why: Detailed simulation of an inaccurately reconstructed fracture network can create false precision.
key_works: J. Hyman et al. (2024), *Determining the dominant factors controlling mineralization in three-dimensional fracture networks*, DOI:10.1016/j.ijggc.2024.104265.

title: Mechanical integrity after extensive basalt mineralization
open: Predict how reaction-induced changes in mineralogy, porosity, and interfaces alter strength, fracture resistance, and future flow under changing stress.
status: Li and colleagues examined basalt dissolution–precipitation from a mesoscale mechanical perspective in 2026. Demonstrating chemical conversion does not establish the mechanical properties of the altered formation.
why: Long-term storage assurance must include the rock that remains after reaction.
key_works: M. Y. Li et al. (2026), *Unraveling Dissolution-Precipitation Evolution in Basalt During Supercritical CO2-Water-Rock Interaction: A Mesoscale Mechanical Perspective*, DOI:10.1029/2025JB033125.

title: Peroxide delivery that accelerates LPMOs without destroying them
open: Control peroxide supply at the enzyme and substrate scale so oxidative cellulose cleavage improves while enzyme inactivation and unwanted substrate oxidation remain limited.
status: Controlled peroxide and reductant addition has been demonstrated for LPMO-catalyzed fiber oxidation. The useful operating window depends on substrate access and local reaction rates.
why: Faster biomass deconstruction is not useful if it sharply increases enzyme replacement.
key_works: K. Marjamaa et al. (2025), *LPMO-Catalyzed Oxidation of Cellulosic Fibers with Controlled Addition of a Reductant and H₂O₂*, DOI:10.1021/acssuschemeng.4c06802.

title: Closed electron balances for LPMO-assisted saccharification
open: Quantify electron donors, oxidants, enzyme states, and side reactions well enough to predict the net benefit of LPMOs in mixed commercial enzyme systems.
status: Research demonstrates that peroxide supply changes both LPMO activity and overall saccharification. Improved activity of one enzyme does not necessarily maximize the complete cocktail’s conversion efficiency.
why: Enables rational dosing instead of empirical additions that may generate damaging oxidants.
key_works: G. Müller et al. (2018), *The impact of hydrogen peroxide supply on LPMO activity and overall saccharification efficiency of a commercial cellulase cocktail*, DOI:10.1186/s13068-018-1199-4.

title: Closing the hemicellulose balance in reductive catalytic fractionation
open: Recover useful products from the hemicellulose fraction while preserving lignin and cellulose value, with sufficiently complete carbon balances to identify unmeasured degradation products.
status: KU Leuven’s 2025–2027 research program explicitly targets full biomass conversion by coupling reductive fractionation and product separation. Strong lignin-monomer yields do not establish efficient use of the entire feedstock.
why: An apparently successful biorefinery can discard a substantial fraction of its original carbon.
key_works: KU Leuven (2025–2027), *Mass balancing the biomass: a route towards the full conversion of lignocellulose to chemicals by coupling reductive catalytic fractionation and product separation*, project 3E250059.

title: Catalyst-impurity effects on whole-biomass product value
open: Predict how trace catalyst impurities alter the complete product distribution rather than evaluating them only through a selected lignin yield metric.
status: Zhu and colleagues showed in 2025 that catalyst impurities can affect different biomass fractions differently. Similar phenolic-monomer yields can conceal different losses elsewhere in the process.
why: Catalyst qualification should optimize total useful output, not one convenient analytical endpoint.
key_works: Y. Zhu et al. (2025), *Reductive Catalytic Fractionation of Lignocellulosic Biomass: The Impact of Impurities in Catalyst*, DOI:10.1002/cssc.202500199.

title: Closed-loop product-derived solvents for biomass fractionation
open: Recycle lignin-derived phenolic cosolvents without progressive impurity accumulation, loss of separation efficiency, or diversion of too much product into the solvent inventory.
status: Webber and colleagues demonstrated that lignin-derived phenolics and water can serve as effective cosolvents in 2025. A successful fresh solvent mixture does not establish a stable industrial recycle loop.
why: Internally sourced solvents can reduce external inputs only when their recovery and quality are maintained.
key_works: M. S. Webber et al. (2025), *Lignin-Derived Phenolic Compounds and Water Are Effective Cosolvents for Reductive Catalytic Fractionation*, DOI:10.1021/acssuschemeng.5c08161.

title: Net-positive recovery from hydrothermal-liquefaction aqueous streams
open: Recover useful carbon and energy from dilute aqueous by-products while counting heating, pressurization, catalyst replacement, separation, and residual wastewater treatment.
status: Kenney and colleagues investigated integrated supercritical catalytic upgrading of the aqueous phase in 2025. Recovering additional products does not automatically improve the complete process energy balance.
why: A substantial waste stream should not be “valorized” through a process that consumes more useful resources than it returns.
key_works: D. H. Kenney et al. (2025), *Integrated process for catalytic upgrading of hydrothermal liquefaction aqueous phase in the supercritical state*, DOI:10.3389/fceng.2025.1532384.

title: Nitrogen partitioning in mixed-feed hydrothermal liquefaction
open: Predict where nitrogen ends up when proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, salts, and degradation intermediates react together, rather than extrapolating directly from isolated model compounds.
status: Bao and colleagues demonstrated structure-dependent nitrogen transformations for amino acids in 2025. Real feed mixtures introduce additional cross-reactions and partitioning behavior.
why: Nitrogen distribution affects fuel upgrading, catalyst life, nutrient recovery, and wastewater treatment simultaneously.
key_works: T. Bao et al. (2025), *Structure-dependent nitrogen transformation in hydrothermal liquefaction of amino acids*, DOI:10.1002/aic.70086.

title: Causal proof of direct interspecies electron transfer in digesters
open: Demonstrate when direct electron transfer materially causes improved digestion, distinguishing it from hydrogen transfer, adsorption, buffering, and other effects of conductive additives.
status: Van Steendam and colleagues identified inadequate characterization as a central obstacle in 2019. Improved methane production alone does not identify the electron-transfer pathway.
why: Reliable process design requires knowing what the intervention actually changes.
key_works: C. Van Steendam et al. (2019), *Improving anaerobic digestion via direct interspecies electron transfer requires development of suitable characterization methods*, DOI:10.1016/j.copbio.2019.03.018.

title: Persistent benefits from conductive digester additives
open: Maintain a favorable whole-process benefit after additive aging, loss, fouling, recovery, and community adaptation are included.
status: Conductive-material interventions can improve selected digester outcomes, but the mechanism and persistence of the benefit must be established rather than assumed from short trials.
why: A recurring additive burden can negate gains in gas production or stability.
key_works: Van Steendam et al. (2019), DIET characterization assessment, DOI:10.1016/j.copbio.2019.03.018.

title: Transferable ammonia adaptation in anaerobic communities
open: Determine whether ammonia-tolerant communities developed under controlled acclimation retain useful performance after changes in feedstock, temperature, hydraulic retention, and competing inhibitors.
status: Wu and colleagues reported stepwise domestication to overcome very high ammonia inhibition in 2025. Successful adaptation within one regime does not establish robust transfer to another digester.
why: Adaptation could reduce pretreatment burdens, but only if it survives realistic operational changes.
key_works: H. Wu et al. (2025), *An innovative strategy for overcoming ultra-high ammonia nitrogen inhibition on anaerobic methanogenesis via stepwise domestication*, DOI:10.1186/s40168-025-02255-y.

title: Long-lived ammonia-recovery membranes inside digesters
open: Recover ammonia selectively while controlling fouling, wetting, chemical consumption, membrane damage, and interference with the microbial process.
status: Ferri da Silva and colleagues investigated in-situ recovery using tubular gas-permeable membranes in 2025. Useful initial recovery does not establish sustained performance in a biologically active slurry.
why: Simultaneous nutrient recovery and inhibition control depends on a maintainable interface.
key_works: J. F. Ferri da Silva et al. (2025), *Enhancing anaerobic digestion of nitrogen-rich substrates through in situ ammonia recovery using tubular gas-permeable membranes*, PMID:40754075.

title: Identifying causal organisms in algal-pond collapse
open: Establish which organisms or interactions cause a cultivation crash through reproducible perturbation and reconstitution experiments, rather than inferring causality from a bloom near collapse.
status: Gilbert and colleagues associated a dominant bacterial bloom with outdoor diatom-culture collapse in 2025, but did not establish that the implicated bacterium alone caused it.
why: Targeting a correlated organism may fail—or remove a protective community member.
key_works: N. E. Gilbert et al. (2025), *A bloom of a single bacterium shapes the microbiome during outdoor diatom cultivation collapse*, DOI:10.1128/msystems.00375-25.

title: Prospective early warning of algal-culture crashes
open: Predict impending collapse early enough for useful intervention, with validated false-alarm rates across seasons, pond conditions, and microbial communities.
status: Detailed crash-associated microbiome measurements provide candidate signals. Retrospective association does not establish that a signal reliably precedes collapse in independent future cultures.
why: Operators need actionable warning, not an accurate explanation after the biomass is lost.
key_works: Gilbert et al. (2025), outdoor diatom-collapse study, DOI:10.1128/msystems.00375-25.

title: Transferable annual algal-productivity forecasts
open: Predict annual recoverable biomass across sites using weather, strain selection, crop rotation, harvesting, contamination, and downtime rather than extrapolating peak seasonal growth.
status: McGowen and colleagues demonstrated annual productivity improvements through crop rotation and operational management in 2023.
why: Fuel and bioproduct economics depend on annual output from the complete cultivation system.
key_works: J. McGowen et al. (2023), *Outdoor annual algae productivity improvements at the pre-pilot scale through crop rotation and pond operational management strategies*, DOI:10.1016/j.algal.2023.102995.

title: Stable protective microbiomes for open algal cultivation
open: Design microbial communities that suppress harmful invasions and support production without becoming unstable, outcompeting the crop, or losing function under seasonal change.
status: Pilot-scale cultivation literature documents multiple causes and management approaches for pond crashes. A protective community that works in one culture need not persist in an open pond.
why: Durable ecological protection could reduce chemical treatment and catastrophic production loss.
key_works: F. A. Ansari et al. (2024), *Pilot Scale Microalgae Cultivation: Challenges and Practical Solutions to Pond Crash*, ISBN:9780323959629.

title: High boron rejection without excessive desalination penalties
open: Reject neutral boron species at relevant feed conditions while preserving water permeability, membrane stability, and acceptable pressure or chemical-adjustment requirements.
status: Huang and colleagues improved boron rejection and permeability using tailored thin-film nanocomposite membranes in 2025. Promising coupons do not establish durable module performance in real seawater.
why: Meeting boron specifications can otherwise require additional treatment that increases energy and complexity.
key_works: J. Huang et al. (2025), *Enhanced boron rejection and permeability of thin-film nanocomposite membranes via g-C₃N₄-tuned diffusion and reaction*, DOI:10.1016/j.desal.2025.118902.

title: Long-cycle integrity of flexible-bladder batch reverse osmosis
open: Maintain bladder, seal, and pressure-management performance through repeated cycles while preserving the energy advantage and avoiding contamination or failure.
status: Tow and colleagues piloted flexible-bladder batch reverse osmosis on scaling-prone brine in 2025. Pilot feasibility does not establish commercial component life.
why: A thermodynamically attractive cycle must have equally credible mechanical durability.
key_works: E. W. Tow et al. (2025), *Piloting batch reverse osmosis with a flexible bladder for water recovery from scaling-prone brine*, DOI:10.1038/s41545-025-00462-6.

title: Purge-and-refill control in scaling-prone batch desalination
open: Minimize mixing, residual brine, scaling, and downtime during batch transitions while maintaining predictable recovery and product quality.
status: Patel and colleagues documented experimental challenges and troubleshooting in batch reverse osmosis in 2025. The transition between batches introduces losses absent from ideal continuous-cycle calculations.
why: Small recurring transition penalties can erase gains predicted for the main separation step.
key_works: D. Patel et al. (2025), *Experimental challenges and troubleshooting in operating batch reverse osmosis system for brackish water desalination*, DOI:10.1016/j.jwpe.2025.108652.

title: Selective crystallization from multicomponent desalination brines
open: Recover useful individual salts or controlled mixtures while accounting for competing precipitation, impurities, nucleation, and changing brine composition.
status: Zhang, Atia, and Fthenakis modeled multicomponent precipitation and crystallization for zero-liquid-discharge desalination in 2025.
why: Converting brine into solids does not automatically produce useful or marketable products.
key_works: Z. Zhang, A. A. Atia, and V. Fthenakis (2025), *Modeling of multi-component precipitation and crystallization for zero-liquid-discharge desalination*, DOI:10.1016/j.desal.2025.119006.

title: Whole-system optimization of zero-liquid-discharge treatment
open: Minimize total energy, chemicals, waste, and cost across concentration, crystallization, product purification, and residual disposal rather than optimizing evaporation alone.
status: Multicomponent models make more realistic optimization possible, but product quality and complete processing burdens must be included before claiming resource recovery benefits.
why: Zero liquid discharge can move the burden into energy demand or difficult solid waste.
key_works: Zhang, Atia, and Fthenakis (2025), zero-liquid-discharge modeling, DOI:10.1016/j.desal.2025.119006.

title: Useful low-humidity water production within complete energy bounds
open: Deliver drinking water at useful daily output in low-humidity environments while counting air movement, capture, regeneration, condensation, purification, and standby losses.
status: Lord and colleagues quantified global potential and climatic constraints in 2021. Favorable thermodynamics or sorbent uptake alone does not establish an affordable device for a particular location.
why: Water-production claims must correspond to real climate and service requirements.
key_works: J. Lord et al. (2021), *Global potential for harvesting drinking water from air using solar energy*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-021-03900-w.

title: Whole-cycle validation of ultrasonic water extraction
open: Demonstrate that reduced extraction energy translates into lower complete-device energy per unit of usable water after capture, airflow, electronics, and recovery are included.
status: Shuvo and colleagues reported a large extraction-stage energy improvement in 2025. That comparison should not be interpreted as the same improvement in every component or in total water-production energy.
why: Component-level advantages can be diluted or reversed by the rest of the device.
key_works: I. I. Shuvo et al. (2025), *High-efficiency atmospheric water harvesting enabled by ultrasonic extraction*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-65586-2.

title: Solute and particle carryover during ultrasonic water recovery
open: Quantify and prevent sorbent fragments, dissolved capture chemicals, and aerosols from entering recovered water during repeated ultrasonic extraction.
status: Ultrasonic extraction establishes a different recovery mechanism from conventional evaporation and condensation. Its long-term purity behavior must be characterized for the actual capture material and operating conditions.
why: Low extraction energy is insufficient if substantial downstream purification becomes necessary.
key_works: Shuvo et al. (2025), ultrasonic atmospheric-water recovery, DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-65586-2.

title: Reliability of passive “all-weather” water harvesters
open: Maintain useful output through realistic sequences of cloudy, dry, humid, and cold conditions, including periods when capture and release requirements do not align.
status: Ji and colleagues demonstrated a hygroscopic wood-sponge architecture with dual phase-change functions in 2026. Operation across selected conditions does not establish uninterrupted service through arbitrary weather sequences.
why: Users need dependable water availability, not favorable isolated-day yields.
key_works: X. Ji et al. (2026), *Hygroscopic wood sponge with dual phase change function for enhanced all-weather atmospheric water harvesting*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-72723-y.

title: Long-term purity of hygroscopic water-harvesting materials
open: Prevent capture-material leaching and contaminant accumulation while preserving uptake after exposure to realistic dust, atmospheric pollutants, microbes, and repeated wetting.
status: New hygroscopic composites demonstrate attractive capture and release behavior. Their initial water quality does not establish lifetime purity under uncontrolled ambient air.
why: Sorbent replacement and purification requirements can determine whether decentralized harvesting is useful.
key_works: Ji et al. (2026), hygroscopic wood-sponge study, DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-72723-y.

title: Scalable synthesis of genuinely ordered bulk tetrataenite
open: Produce substantial quantities of ordered L1₀ FeNi at practical processing times and temperatures, with independently verified ordering rather than diffraction features attributable to other phases.
status: A prominent 2022 bulk-casting claim was reinterpreted and retracted; 2025 work re-examines phosphorus-assisted ordering. The corrected evidence does not establish that phosphorus alone solves rapid bulk production.
why: Tetrataenite remains attractive only if its ordered phase can be manufactured reliably rather than obtained through geological timescales or ambiguous measurements.
key_works: S. R. Maness, S. M. Pennell, and D. C. Dunand (2025), *Investigating the effect of phosphorus on L1₀ ordering in melt-solidified Fe-Ni alloys*, DOI:10.1016/j.mtla.2025.102617.

title: Tetrataenite microstructures with useful permanent-magnet coercivity
open: Combine chemical ordering with grain size, texture, defects, and domain structure that produce useful coercivity and energy product at bulk scale.
status: Houghton and colleagues emphasize that identifying an ordered phase is not equivalent to producing an effective permanent magnet. Suitable magnetic microstructure remains an additional requirement.
why: A material can possess favorable intrinsic anisotropy while remaining a poor practical magnet.
key_works: O. S. Houghton et al. (2025), *Reinterpretation of Report of Tetrataenite in Bulk Alloy Castings*, DOI:10.1002/advs.202408796.

title: Artifact-resistant identification of weakly ordered magnetic phases
open: Establish cross-validated structural and magnetic measurements that distinguish genuine L1₀ ordering from secondary phases, preparation artifacts, and overlapping diffraction signals.
status: The tetrataenite reinterpretation identified misleading contributions from phosphides and specimen-preparation-related features. The lesson is a concrete metrology problem, not simply a need for more measurements of the same kind.
why: Materials discovery cannot progress reliably if the target phase is misidentified.
key_works: Houghton et al. (2025), tetrataenite reinterpretation, DOI:10.1002/advs.202408796.

title: Adjacent-lanthanide selectivity from lanmodulin-derived peptides
open: Engineer peptide binders that discriminate sufficiently between neighboring rare-earth elements in realistic mixtures, rather than merely binding all lanthanides more strongly.
status: Gutenthaler-Tietze and colleagues increased lanthanide affinity by reversing lanmodulin-derived binding sequences in 2025. Higher affinity does not automatically improve adjacent-element separation.
why: The difficult industrial task is often separating chemically similar neighbors, not extracting rare earths as a group.
key_works: S. M. Gutenthaler-Tietze et al. (2025), *Reversing Lanmodulin’s Metal-Binding Sequence in Short Peptides Surprisingly Increases the Lanthanide Affinity*, DOI:10.1002/anie.202510453.

title: Thousand-cycle durability of immobilized protein separators
open: Achieve a **proposed 1,000 capture–release cycles with at least 90% retained useful separation performance**, including realistic contaminants and regeneration conditions.
status: Ye and colleagues demonstrated protein-functionalized magnetic particles with more than 90% retained activity over five studied cycles. That is proof of reuse, not evidence for the proposed longer-life target.
why: Protein replacement and regeneration can govern the economics of biologically inspired separation.
key_works: Q. Ye et al. (2025), *Group Separation of Rare Earth Elements by Protein-Functionalized Magnetic Nanoparticles*, DOI:10.1021/acsestengg.5c00508.

title: Cascading biological group separation into pure rare-earth products
open: Design a complete sequence that converts mixed feeds into individual products at specified purity and recovery while minimizing binders, regeneration chemicals, and stages.
status: Protein-functionalized particles have demonstrated group enrichment from complex feeds. Group separation is not equivalent to isolating every neighboring element.
why: A selective first step must connect to the actual product specifications required by industry.
key_works: Ye et al. (2025), protein-functionalized rare-earth separation, DOI:10.1021/acsestengg.5c00508.

title: Predicting rare-earth selectivity from binding-site structure
open: Predict selectivity and release behavior from coordination geometry, hydration, conformational flexibility, and immobilization, with validation on sequences not used to fit the model.
status: Smerigan and colleagues applied X-ray absorption spectroscopy to rare-earth-bound lanmodulin-derived peptides in 2025. Structural characterization provides constraints but does not by itself establish a predictive design model.
why: Sequence screening becomes more efficient when affinity and selectivity can be forecast mechanistically.
key_works: A. Smerigan et al. (2025), *X-ray absorption spectroscopy of lanmodulin-derived peptides bound to rare earth elements*, PMID:40982250.

title: Regenerable electrokinetic rare-earth separation in complex feeds
open: Maintain useful separation factors through repeated ligand redox cycles while controlling ligand degradation, competing ions, electrical consumption, and product recovery.
status: Fang and colleagues demonstrated electrokinetic separation using a redox-active ligand in 2017, including strong discrimination in a studied binary system.
why: Binary-mixture selectivity must survive a complete process with recycle streams and trace contaminants.
key_works: H. Fang et al. (2017), *Electro-kinetic Separation of Rare Earth Elements Using a Redox-Active Ligand*, DOI:10.1002/anie.201706894.

title: Mechanism-based healing of spent graphite
open: Determine which treatments restore useful graphite structure and surfaces without creating excessive porosity, first-cycle loss, or new impurities.
status: Markey and colleagues demonstrated healing-and-doping-based direct regeneration in 2020. Recovery of selected electrochemical properties does not uniquely identify which damage mechanisms were reversed.
why: Different spent materials may need different treatment rather than one increasingly severe purification recipe.
key_works: B. Markey et al. (2020), *Effective Upcycling of Graphite Anode: Healing and Doping Enabled Direct Regeneration*, DOI:10.1149/1945-7111/abcc2f.

title: Electrolyte removal without damaging recyclable graphite
open: Remove electrolyte residues and decomposition products while preserving graphite properties and minimizing solvent use, thermal treatment, and secondary emissions.
status: Rothermel and colleagues compared graphite-recycling approaches, including carbon-dioxide-assisted extraction, in 2016. A method effective for one returned-cell stream may not tolerate different binders and electrolyte histories.
why: Purification can destroy part of the material value that recycling is intended to preserve.
key_works: S. Rothermel et al. (2016), *Graphite Recycling from Spent Lithium-Ion Batteries*, DOI:10.1002/cssc.201601062.

title: Complete energy accounting for flash graphite recycling
open: Scale rapid electrical treatment while counting feed preparation, pulse-generation losses, gas handling, contaminant capture, yield, and subsequent electrode processing.
status: Chen and colleagues demonstrated flash recycling of graphite anodes. Short treatment time alone does not determine low total energy or industrial throughput.
why: Rapid heating can be valuable, but its benefits must survive the complete processing chain.
key_works: W. Chen et al., *Flash Recycling of Graphite Anodes*—published online in 2022; OSTI record 2418214.

title: Transferable full-cell qualification of recycled graphite
open: Predict performance in new full cells from measured recycled-graphite properties, including lithium inventory, electrode loading, electrolyte quantity, fast charging, and calendar life.
status: Direct regeneration has produced promising electrochemical results, and recycled-electrode full cells have been demonstrated. The remaining target is reliable transfer across returned feedstocks and new cell designs.
why: Half-cell capacity does not capture every penalty that matters in a lithium-limited commercial cell.
key_works: Markey et al. (2020), DOI:10.1149/1945-7111/abcc2f; Rothermel et al. (2016), DOI:10.1002/cssc.201601062.

title: Reconciling magnetic reversibility with thermal hysteresis
open: Predict useful repeated-cycle cooling when magnetic measurements appear reversible but structural or thermal hysteresis still dissipates energy.
status: Revuelta-Losada and colleagues directly examined this distinction using lock-in thermography in 2025. Reversible magnetization is not sufficient evidence for reversible heat pumping.
why: Caloric materials must be assessed by the thermodynamic cycle they actually execute.
key_works: J. Revuelta-Losada et al. (2025), *Magnetic reversibility accompanied by thermal hysteresis in magnetocaloric materials: A lock-in thermography study*, DOI:10.1016/j.matdes.2025.114372.

title: Controlling magnetostructural transformation paths
open: Tune microstructure and loading history so magnetostructural transitions retain useful caloric response while minimizing hysteresis, incomplete transformation, and cyclic damage.
status: Hao and colleagues studied temperature-dependent transitions in MnCoGe-based compounds in situ in 2025. Observing the transformation does not establish a durable low-loss path through it.
why: Large single-cycle effects can coexist with poor regenerative-cycle performance.
key_works: X. Hao et al. (2025), *In-situ study of the temperature effects on the magneto-structural transition in the MnCoGe-based magnetocaloric compounds*, DOI:10.1016/j.actamat.2025.121241.

title: Barocaloric refrigeration with realistic pressure hardware
open: Convert a large material entropy change into useful cooling after pressure generation, containment, heat exchange, and mechanical losses are included.
status: Bao and colleagues reported a large barocaloric effect at 20 MPa in 2025. “Low pressure” relative to other barocaloric experiments still requires substantial engineered pressure equipment.
why: The complete device, rather than the material entropy change, determines whether the route can compete.
key_works: C. Bao et al. (2025), *Low-Pressure-Driven Colossal Barocaloric Effect in an Organometallic Sandwich Compound*, DOI:10.1021/acsmaterialslett.5c00620.

title: Functional fatigue of large-effect barocaloric materials
open: Preserve transformation completeness and caloric response through repeated pressure cycling while preventing cracking, phase segregation, plastic deformation, and chemical change.
status: Large barocaloric responses have been measured, but those results do not establish appliance-relevant cycling life under coupled thermal and mechanical loads.
why: A refrigerant replacement must repeatedly perform the same useful transformation.
key_works: Bao et al. (2025), barocaloric-material study, DOI:10.1021/acsmaterialslett.5c00620.

title: Sustained power from thermodiffusion-assisted thermogalvanic cells
open: Separate transient charging from continuously recoverable electrical power and demonstrate stable average output under realistic maintained temperature gradients.
status: Baek, Seog, and Jang reported high normalized performance in solid-state thermodiffusion-assisted thermogalvanic cells in 2025. Peak or discharge-stage power does not alone establish indefinite continuous generation.
why: Waste-heat applications need an honest account of the full charge–discharge or steady-state cycle.
key_works: J.-Y. Baek, H. J. Seog, and S.-Y. Jang (2025), *Solid-state n-type thermodiffusion-assisted thermogalvanic cells with unprecedented thermal energy conversion*, DOI:10.1039/D5EE01216C.

title: Lifetime-stable packaging for ionic heat-to-electricity devices
open: Maintain electrolyte composition, electrode contact, ionic distributions, and useful thermal gradients despite evaporation, mechanical cycling, and ambient changes.
status: Solid-state architectures reduce some containment problems, but laboratory cycling does not establish long-term stability in a packaged thermal environment.
why: Modest material drift can substantially change ionic thermopower and internal resistance.
key_works: Baek, Seog, and Jang (2025), thermodiffusion-assisted cell study, DOI:10.1039/D5EE01216C.

title: Closed-cycle accounting for water-formation heat-recovery cells
open: Regenerate all consumed chemical inventories and measure net electricity after accounting for both thermal input and chemical free energy.
status: Mondal and colleagues demonstrated a non-isothermal water-formation cell in 2025. Because acid–base chemistry contributes free energy, electricity divided only by heat input is not the efficiency of a standalone heat engine.
why: Establishes what portion of the output is genuinely recoverable from waste heat over a repeatable cycle.
key_works: R. Mondal et al. (2025), *A non-isothermal water formation cell for electrochemical heat recovery*, DOI:10.1039/D5SC00892A.

title: Wetting-resistant membranes for liquid-desiccant air treatment
open: Maintain selective water-vapor transport without desiccant leakage when membranes encounter surfactants, dust, condensation, pressure changes, and long service.
status: Membrane-based liquid-desiccant systems have been extensively investigated. Initial vapor-transfer performance does not establish durable separation between indoor air and the desiccant.
why: Desiccant carryover can turn an energy-saving component into an indoor-air-quality problem.
key_works: X. Liu et al. (2019), *Membrane-based liquid desiccant air dehumidification: A comprehensive review on materials, components, systems and performances*, DOI:10.1016/j.rser.2019.04.018.

title: Complete regeneration-energy optimization for desiccant cooling
open: Optimize moisture removal and desiccant regeneration together under variable humidity and available heat, including pumps, fans, heat rejection, and imperfect recovery.
status: Numerous component and system configurations exist; low dehumidifier energy alone can conceal a larger regeneration burden elsewhere.
why: The system should reduce total energy, not relocate consumption to a less visible subsystem.
key_works: Liu et al. (2019), liquid-desiccant system assessment, DOI:10.1016/j.rser.2019.04.018.

title: Verified whole-system savings from electrochemical dehumidification
open: Demonstrate net reductions in HVAC electricity across representative climates and loads, including electrochemical losses, air movement, regeneration, and durability.
status: DOE-supported electrochemical membrane concepts have projected substantial savings. Projected savings are not equivalent to independently measured seasonal performance in complete buildings.
why: Promising moisture-separation mechanisms require validation against the equipment they would replace.
key_works: U.S. DOE (2020), *Electrohydrodynamic Enabled Electrochemical Membrane Dehumidifier* research project.

title: Which complementary investments make electrification economically useful?
open: Identify when appliances, credit, skills, market access, or improved service quality produce additional benefits beyond a new connection, using designs that separate their individual and joint effects.
status: Lee, Miguel, and Wolfram’s rural-electrification experiment documented limited early demand and economic effects in its studied setting. That does not establish that electrification has uniformly small benefits everywhere.
why: Connection subsidies may underperform when the missing constraint lies elsewhere.
key_works: K. Lee, E. Miguel, and C. Wolfram (2020), *Experimental Evidence on the Economics of Rural Electrification*, DOI:10.1086/705417.

title: Long-run electrification effects with migration and spillovers
open: Estimate effects over longer periods while accounting for business formation, migration, neighboring communities, changing tariffs, and improvements in reliability.
status: Experimental studies provide stronger identification than simple connected-versus-unconnected comparisons, but their time horizons and local treatment contrasts do not automatically identify wider equilibrium effects.
why: Short-run household outcomes may miss delayed benefits, displacement, or costs borne elsewhere.
key_works: Lee, Miguel, and Wolfram (2020), rural-electrification experiment, DOI:10.1086/705417.

title: Battery-supported electric cooking under actual household duty cycles
open: Size and operate battery-supported cooking so it reliably serves complete meals despite outages, simultaneous appliance use, battery aging, and changing household schedules.
status: SEforALL, MECS, and GeCCo assessed battery-supported cooking technologies and swap models in 2026, identifying opportunities alongside a need for further practical evidence.
why: Demonstrating that a battery can power a cooker does not establish dependable daily cooking service.
key_works: SEforALL, MECS, and GeCCo (2026), *Battery Supported Electric Cooking Technologies and Battery Swap Models*.

title: Financeable battery-swapping models for cooking
open: Allocate battery ownership, charging, logistics, replacement, and payment risk so households receive affordable cooking service without hidden long-term subsidy or unsafe informal charging.
status: The 2026 battery-cooking assessment examines swapping as a possible access model. Its viability depends on utilization, logistics, and battery-life assumptions that require field testing.
why: A useful technical architecture can fail when the party financing batteries cannot recover costs.
key_works: SEforALL, MECS, and GeCCo (2026), battery-supported cooking assessment.

title: Reliable electric cooking for institutional meal schedules
open: Provide school meals on schedule despite outages, large batch sizes, menu variation, maintenance delays, and limited local technical support.
status: Khalifa and colleagues synthesized electric-school-cooking experience in several countries in 2025. The evidence includes useful cases but does not establish a universally reliable implementation model.
why: A missed institutional cooking window can affect hundreds of meals at once.
key_works: Y. Khalifa et al. (2025), *The role of electric cooking in providing sustainable school meals in low-income and lower-middle-income countries*, DOI:10.1016/S2542-5196(25)00004-X.

title: Longitudinal outcomes of institutional cooking transitions
open: Measure sustained changes in cost, staff exposure, meal provision, food quality, and equipment availability against credible counterfactuals.
status: The 2025 school-cooking assessment documents limited and heterogeneous evidence. Installation counts or favorable initial demonstrations do not establish long-term outcomes.
why: Public investment should be guided by delivered service and health benefits, not appliance distribution.
key_works: Khalifa et al. (2025), institutional electric-cooking assessment, DOI:10.1016/S2542-5196(25)00004-X.

title: Solar irrigation incentives compatible with groundwater limits
open: Design tariffs, pumping rights, buyback arrangements, or service models that preserve affordable irrigation while preventing inexpensive pumping from accelerating groundwater depletion.
status: The World Bank’s 2024 assessment highlights both opportunities and risks of solar irrigation. Lower operating costs can change water extraction behavior rather than merely replace the original energy source.
why: Decarbonizing pumping should not make the underlying water resource less sustainable.
key_works: S. Balasubramanya (2024), *Navigating the opportunities and risks of solar irrigation: The importance of comprehensive accounting and smart regulations*, World Bank.

title: Complete causal emissions accounting for solar irrigation
open: Estimate emissions changes after accounting for additional pumping, continued use of old pumps, expanded cultivation, crop changes, and altered fertilizer consumption.
status: The 2024 World Bank analysis emphasizes comprehensive accounting rather than assuming that every unit of solar generation displaces an unchanged amount of fossil-fueled pumping.
why: Equipment-level emissions reductions can differ from the consequences of the resulting agricultural transition.
key_works: Balasubramanya (2024), solar-irrigation opportunities and risks assessment.

title: Inclusive solar-irrigation service markets
open: Develop ownership and service arrangements that make useful irrigation available to smallholders and tenants without concentrating water access or financial risk among already advantaged landowners.
status: Lefore and colleagues proposed a framework for inclusive solar irrigation in 2021. Equipment availability alone does not establish equitable access to finance, land, water, and maintenance.
why: Deployment can increase aggregate agricultural output while excluding households most constrained by unreliable irrigation.
key_works: N. Lefore et al. (2021), *Solar for all: A framework to deliver inclusive and environmentally sustainable solar irrigation for smallholder agriculture*, Energy Policy, PII:S0301421521001828.

title: Predicting strontium-vanadate cathode burn-in
open: Predict the time-dependent emitting state of SrVO₃ from temperature, oxygen activity, surface termination, and prior operation, then identify preparation conditions that reliably produce stable emission.
status: Experiments published in 2024 document substantial changes in emission during extended heating, associated with evolving surface composition. Initial work-function measurements therefore do not establish operating performance.
why: A reproducible low-work-function material is useful only if its favorable surface survives and can be manufactured consistently.
key_works: M. S. Sheikh et al. (2024), *Time dependence of SrVO3 thermionic electron emission properties*, DOI:10.1063/5.0186012.

title: From low-work-function patches to total useful emission
open: Predict whole-cathode current from spatially heterogeneous work functions, including patch fields, emitting-area fractions, temperature variation, and space-charge effects.
status: Direct microscopy and photoemission measurements in 2024 identified low-work-function regions on SrVO₃. The lowest measured local work function is not automatically the effective value governing an entire converter.
why: Prevents material screening from selecting rare favorable patches that contribute little usable current.
key_works: Sheikh et al. (2024), *Direct evidence of low work function on SrVO3 cathode using thermionic electron emission microscopy and high-field ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy*, DOI:10.1063/5.0211701.

title: Predictive theory of the thermionic obstructed mode
open: Explain the obstructed operating mode of cesium-plasma thermionic converters using a kinetic model that reproduces measured current–voltage behavior without device-specific empirical corrections.
status: The 2026 thermionic roadmap retains difficulties involving ionization pathways and disparate electron and ion timescales; simplified plasma descriptions remain inadequate in relevant regimes.
why: Unexplained operating branches obstruct reliable converter design.
key_works: A. Bellucci et al. (2026), *The 2026 thermionic converters roadmap*, DOI:10.1088/1361-6463/ae611e.

title: Thermally isolated micrometre gaps that remain dimensionally stable
open: Meet a **proposed joint qualification target** of a 1–4 μm gap over a square-centimetre active area at temperatures above 1,500 K, with spacer conductance below approximately 10 mW cm⁻² K⁻¹ and no progressive gap collapse.
status: Micrometre-gap converters exist; the roadmap identifies support conduction and dimensional stability as coupled constraints.
why: Reducing space charge must not introduce overwhelming conductive heat leakage.
key_works: Bellucci et al. (2026), thermionic roadmap, DOI:10.1088/1361-6463/ae611e.

title: Stability boundaries of trapped-ion thermionic enhancement
open: Determine the experimentally accessible stability domain in which trapped ions reduce a virtual-cathode barrier, including finite geometry, collisions, ion escape, and changing emission.
status: A 2026 analytical treatment predicts enhancement beyond the traditional space-charge-limited current in specified geometries. A steady analytical solution does not establish stable converter operation.
why: Distinguishes useful barrier neutralization from unstable charge accumulation.
key_works: Z. L. Idema and M. D. Campanell (2026), *Theory of the thermionic current beyond the traditional space charge limit enabled by trapped ions in the virtual cathode*, DOI:10.1063/5.0335982.

title: Nonlinear quenching oscillations in ion-assisted thermionic diodes
open: Derive and validate oscillation periods, amplitudes, and onset conditions when ion accumulation removes the virtual cathode, releases trapped ions, and permits the barrier to reform.
status: Idema and Campanell identify quenching behavior as requiring further time-dependent analysis; their steady-state treatment does not determine the complete cycle.
why: Oscillatory current can invalidate steady-output forecasts.
key_works: Idema and Campanell (2026), thermionic trapped-ion theory, DOI:10.1063/5.0335982.

title: Photon-enhanced thermionic conversion with bidirectional emission
open: Optimize and experimentally validate photon-enhanced thermionic converters when both electrodes emit electrons, including self-consistent collector heating and space charge.
status: Lin and colleagues’ 2024 model shows that reverse collector emission changes predicted operating optima. Neglecting it becomes particularly consequential for warm, low-work-function collectors.
why: Improvements to the collector can inadvertently increase reverse current.
key_works: X. Lin et al. (2024), *The effect of space charge on photon-enhanced thermionic emission in the presence of the bidirectional discharge*, arXiv:2410.19298.

title: Physically attainable thermoradiative efficiency–power frontiers
open: Determine how closely thermoradiative devices made from causal, finite-bandwidth materials can approach ideal conversion bounds after nonradiative recombination and parasitic heat transfer are included.
status: Giteau, Picardi, and Papadakis derived fundamental limits in 2025. The bounds themselves are not the open problem; attaining them with realizable optical and electronic responses is.
why: Separates material-design opportunities from performance available only to idealized emitters.
key_works: M. Giteau, M. F. Picardi, and G. T. Papadakis (2025), *Fundamental limitations of thermoradiative energy conversion*, arXiv:2507.19864.

title: Experimental multijunction thermoradiative advantage
open: Demonstrate that a multijunction thermoradiative device outperforms a comparable single-junction device after interconnection, optical coupling, and thermal losses are counted.
status: A 2025 idealized analysis predicts relative efficiency and power improvements at a 500 K emitter and 300 K sink. These are calculated gains, not a completed multijunction experiment.
why: Establishes whether junction complexity produces a net benefit.
key_works: P. Bohm, A. K. Menon, and Z. M. Zhang (2025), *Fundamental advantages of multijunction thermoradiative cells*, DOI:10.1063/5.0273591.

title: Nonradiative feedback in negative-illumination devices
open: Predict how nonradiative carrier processes change temperature, chemical potential, current, and emitted radiation together in operating thermoradiative cells.
status: Ideal radiative calculations establish possible multijunction benefits but do not close the feedback produced by real narrow-bandgap semiconductor losses.
why: A loss mechanism can alter the operating state, not merely subtract a fixed percentage from efficiency.
key_works: Bohm, Menon, and Zhang (2025), thermoradiative multijunction analysis, DOI:10.1063/5.0273591.

title: Experimental proof of cation-vacancy-mediated water splitting
open: Directly test whether changing cation-vacancy populations, rather than the usually assumed oxygen-vacancy mechanism, controls hydrogen production in relevant iron-aluminate cycles.
status: Szymanski and colleagues’ 2025 preprint, revised in 2026, proposes a cation-vacancy mechanism supported by calculations and consistency with reported yields. Agreement with yield alone does not uniquely identify the reacting defects.
why: A different active defect changes which compositions and treatments should be optimized.
key_works: N. J. Szymanski et al. (2025–2026), *Cation vacancies mediate thermochemical water splitting with iron aluminates*, arXiv:2510.05328.

title: Ceria reactor topology that remains optimal as the material changes
open: Design graded porous ceria structures whose optical absorption, reaction access, and heat transport remain favorable as reduction state and microstructure evolve.
status: Sas Brunser’s 2025 thesis demonstrates optimized hierarchical structures and reports 6.29% solar-to-fuel efficiency at its experimental boundary. An optimum based on initial properties need not remain optimal during cycling.
why: Reactive structures simultaneously serve as absorbers, heat exchangers, and chemical inventories.
key_works: S. Sas Brunser (2025), *Optimized Ceria Structures for Enhanced Efficiency in Solar Thermochemical Fuel Production*, ETH dissertation 30924, DOI:10.3929/ethz-b-000738921.

title: Closing the solar-reactor heat-recovery performance gap
open: Demonstrate complete redox-cycle efficiency gains from recuperation, including both heating and cooling stages, gas circulation, switching, and transient losses.
status: Lidor and colleagues measured approximately 70% heat-extraction effectiveness in a 4 kW experiment. Their 14.7% solar-to-fuel result for a larger configuration was modeled, not a measured complete-cycle efficiency.
why: Extracting heat successfully does not prove that it can all be returned usefully to the next cycle.
key_works: A. Lidor et al. (2023), *High-temperature heat recovery from a solar reactor for the thermochemical redox splitting of H2O and CO2*, DOI:10.1016/j.apenergy.2022.120211.

title: Oxygen-removal work in realistic thermochemical cycles
open: Optimize reduction conditions while counting the actual work and heat needed for oxygen removal, sweep-gas handling, and gas regeneration.
status: Lidor and Bulfin’s 2024 analysis questions favorable cycle assessments that do not adequately connect material behavior to complete process requirements.
why: A low oxygen partial pressure is a maintained operating condition, not a free thermodynamic resource.
key_works: A. Lidor and B. Bulfin (2024), *A critical perspective and analysis of two-step thermochemical fuel production cycles*, DOI:10.1016/j.solcom.2024.100077.

title: Achievable volumetric power density of redox fuel reactors
open: Establish experimentally attainable tradeoffs among fuel-production rate per reactor volume, conversion efficiency, temperature swing, and material utilization.
status: The 2024 critical analysis identifies low volumetric power density as a consequential scaling constraint. High yield per gram does not establish a compact, productive reactor.
why: Reactor size can dominate economics even when the redox material is inexpensive.
key_works: Lidor and Bulfin (2024), two-step thermochemical-cycle assessment, DOI:10.1016/j.solcom.2024.100077.

title: Transferring near-unity quantum yield into the visible spectrum
open: Achieve comparably efficient overall water splitting under visible photons while retaining stoichiometric gas production, catalyst stability, and useful solar-to-hydrogen efficiency.
status: Takata and colleagues reported approximately 96% apparent quantum yield at 350–365 nm in 2020. That ultraviolet result is not 96% solar-to-hydrogen efficiency and does not establish equivalent visible-light performance.
why: Solar usefulness depends on the captured spectrum as well as the efficiency of individual absorbed photons.
key_works: T. Takata et al. (2020), *Photocatalytic water splitting with a quantum efficiency of almost unity*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-2278-9.

title: Gas recovery from large photocatalyst-sheet fields
open: Recover hydrogen efficiently from distributed photocatalytic sheets while controlling back-reaction, variable gas production, contamination, and separation losses across day–night operation.
status: Nishiyama and colleagues demonstrated a 100 m² photocatalytic system in 2021. The remaining problem is not first scaling to 100 m², but dependable net production and recovery over representative operation.
why: Gas evolved at a catalyst is not yet a purified, delivered fuel.
key_works: H. Nishiyama et al. (2021), *Photocatalytic solar hydrogen production from water on a 100-m2 scale*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-021-03907-3.

title: Mediator transport between separated photocatalytic half-reactors
open: Maintain efficient redox-mediator circulation as hydrogen- and oxygen-producing reactors become larger or more widely separated, without excessive pumping, crossover, or reverse reactions.
status: Fu and colleagues reported 2.47 ± 0.03% laboratory solar-to-hydrogen efficiency and a 692.5 cm² outdoor system in 2025. Spatial separation introduces transport costs absent from a well-mixed small reactor.
why: Separating products safely must not consume the conversion advantage.
key_works: H. Fu et al. (2025), *A scalable solar-driven photocatalytic system for separated H2 and O2 production from water*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-56314-x.

title: Selective protection against visible-light photocorrosion
open: Protect visible-light absorbers against self-oxidation and dissolution while preserving the interfacial reactions and charge transfer required for overall water splitting.
status: The 2024 field roadmap identifies stability as a continuing barrier for useful visible-light materials. A protective layer can suppress both corrosion and desired catalysis.
why: Lifetime and catalytic access must improve together.
key_works: T. Hisatomi et al. (2024), *Photocatalytic water splitting for large-scale solar-to-chemical energy conversion and storage*, DOI:10.3389/fsci.2024.1411644.

title: Annual yield of concentrated-light photocatalytic hydrogen
open: Validate annual net hydrogen production while accounting for optical concentration, tracking, thermal management, fluctuating sunlight, and catalyst aging.
status: Zhou and colleagues reported 9.2% efficiency under concentrated illumination and elevated operating temperature in 2023, with different results under natural sunlight. The concentrated-light figure is not an unconcentrated annual-system efficiency.
why: A high instantaneous conversion measurement must translate into useful fuel per installed collector area.
key_works: P. Zhou et al. (2023), *Solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of more than 9% in photocatalytic water splitting*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-022-05399-1.

title: Simultaneous high efficiency and decade-scale PEC lifetime
open: Demonstrate the paired requirements represented by DOE’s historical ultimate target: 25% solar-to-hydrogen efficiency and ten years of operation before output falls to 80% of its initial value.
status: These are historical program targets, not a newly issued standard or an achieved combined result. High-efficiency demonstrations, including a 19% monolithic device, do not establish decade-scale qualification.
why: Efficiency and lifetime jointly determine whether semiconductor-intensive direct solar hydrogen is economical.
key_works: DOE, *Technical Targets for Hydrogen Production: Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting*; W. H. Cheng et al. (2018), *Monolithic photoelectrochemical device for direct water splitting with 19% efficiency*.

title: Independent certification of solar-to-hydrogen measurements
open: Establish reproducible interlaboratory certification covering illumination, illuminated area, gas balances, dissolved products, sacrificial reagents, and complete system boundaries.
status: The 2024 photocatalysis roadmap calls for stronger certification and standardized evaluation. Comparable-looking efficiency values can otherwise describe different experiments.
why: Reliable ranking requires comparable denominators and independently verified products.
key_works: Hisatomi et al. (2024), photocatalytic water-splitting roadmap, DOI:10.3389/fsci.2024.1411644.

title: Low-loss ion separation in a closed ionocaloric refrigerator
open: Reduce the work of restoring the working mixture after ion-induced melting while preserving useful cooling rate, temperature lift, and cycle efficiency.
status: Lilley and Prasher demonstrated an ionocaloric refrigeration cycle in 2022. The existence of the cycle is established; competitive, durable separation and regeneration at useful scale remain the engineering target.
why: A large phase-change cooling effect does not eliminate the work needed to reset the mixture.
key_works: D. Lilley and R. Prasher (2022), *Ionocaloric refrigeration cycle*, DOI:10.1126/science.ade1696.

title: Continuous transport of ionocaloric slurries
open: Pump, mix, separate, and exchange heat with partially solidified working fluids without blockage, excessive pressure loss, unstable solids fractions, or rapid component wear.
status: ILK Dresden’s ionocaloric research program identifies continuous working-fluid handling and system integration as development tasks beyond the original thermodynamic demonstration.
why: Practical refrigerators need repeated or continuous heat delivery rather than isolated material transitions.
key_works: ILK Dresden, *Ionocaloric Refrigeration* research project; Lilley and Prasher (2022), DOI:10.1126/science.ade1696.

title: Refrigeration cycles through non-eutectic phase regions
open: Design ionocaloric cycles that remain efficient when melting and crystallization change local composition, produce multiple phases, or depart from equilibrium.
status: Wang and colleagues experimentally analyzed non-eutectic transitions in sodium-iodide/ethylene-carbonate solutions in 2025. A single idealized melting point does not describe the complete operating path.
why: Composition drift can reduce temperature lift and prevent repeatable regeneration.
key_works: L. Wang et al. (2025), *Impact of non-eutectic phase transitions in NaI-EC solutions on ionocaloric refrigeration: experiments and thermodynamic diagram analysis*, article PII:S0196890425008489.

title: Separating hydrovoltaic conversion from electrode consumption
open: Quantify the contributions of evaporation-driven transport, concentration gradients, corrosion, and galvanic reactions using matched electrode controls and complete material balances.
status: Zheng and colleagues demonstrated in 2023 that electrode selection can fundamentally affect interpretation of hydrovoltaic measurements. Observing a voltage during evaporation does not uniquely identify its source.
why: Sustainable energy conversion must be distinguished from gradual consumption of a chemical inventory.
key_works: C. Zheng et al. (2023), *Role of electrodes in study of hydrovoltaic effects*, DOI:10.1007/s12274-023-5881-x.

title: Closed-cycle power accounting for high-current hydrovoltaics
open: Demonstrate repeatable useful electrical work after restoring all chemical and concentration reservoirs, rather than reporting peak current or charge released during a favorable transient.
status: Lin and colleagues reported high-current devices involving synergistic physical and chemical processes in 2026. A large current density does not determine net cycle energy or identify how much output comes from each process.
why: Establishes whether high-current architectures deliver renewable conversion, storage discharge, or a combination.
key_works: S. Lin et al. (2026), *High-Current Hydrovoltaic Devices Enabled by Synergistic Physicochemical Processes via a Dynamic Liquid-Hydrogel Interface*, DOI:10.1002/aenm.70777.

title: Flexoelectric versus mechanochemical origins of tribovoltaic current
open: Quantitatively distinguish strain-gradient fields, interfacial bond reactions, defect generation, and conventional junction effects during semiconductor sliding.
status: Lyu and colleagues used a surface-chemistry isotope effect to probe silicon tribovoltaic devices in 2025. Such interventions provide mechanistic leverage, but a transferable partition of the current remains unresolved.
why: Different mechanisms imply different routes to higher efficiency and longer life.
key_works: X. Lyu et al. (2025), *Silicon-based tribovoltaic nanogenerators: Surface chemistry isotope effect on device performance and durability*, DOI:10.26599/FRICT.2025.9440939.

title: Lubrication that preserves conversion rather than only reducing wear
open: Maintain favorable electrical coupling while lowering friction and surface damage, including lubricant redistribution, contamination, and long operating histories.
status: Graphene-enhanced interfacial lubrication was investigated for tribovoltaic conversion in 2025. Improved short-term output or reduced friction does not establish a durable net-energy advantage.
why: The interface must remain both mechanically survivable and electrically productive.
key_works: J. Yuan et al. (2025), *Boosting energy conversion efficiency in tribovoltaic nanogenerators through graphene-enhanced interfacial lubrication*, DOI:10.1016/j.cej.2025.170088.

title: Motion-normalized useful-power benchmarks for nanogenerators
open: Compare devices under matched mechanical work, motion spectra, available volume, and electrical loads, using delivered average energy rather than incompatible peak voltage and current measurements.
status: Zi and colleagues introduced standards and figures of merit in 2015. The remaining problem is transferable application-level comparison, not the absence of any prior standardization.
why: Geometry or test-motion changes can otherwise masquerade as conversion improvements.
key_works: Y. Zi et al. (2015), *Standards and figure-of-merits for quantifying the performance of triboelectric nanogenerators*, DOI:10.1038/ncomms9376.

title: Net benefit of triboelectric charge-excitation circuits
open: Optimize complete charge-excitation systems while counting startup energy, stored electrical inventory, leakage, switching losses, and variable mechanical input.
status: Integrated self-excitation and charge-shuttling architectures were demonstrated in 2019–2020. Increased charge density is not, by itself, a measure of increased net harvested energy under every duty cycle.
why: Excitation electronics should improve useful output rather than merely enlarge internal circulating charge.
key_works: W. Liu et al. (2019), *Integrated charge excitation triboelectric nanogenerator*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-019-09464-8; H. Wang et al. (2020), *Pumping up the charge density … by charge-shuttling*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17891-1.

title: Breakdown-limited charge density under evolving real contacts
open: Predict sustainable charge density as microscopic contact area, humidity, wear, contamination, and gap distributions change during operation.
status: Liu and colleagues combined contact-efficiency measurements with an air-breakdown model in 2020, reporting 2.38 mC m⁻² under specified dry conditions. That value is not a universal ambient-service limit.
why: Reliable output depends on the evolving interface and surrounding gas, not only dielectric material selection.
key_works: Y. Liu et al. (2020), *Quantifying contact status and the air-breakdown model of charge-excitation triboelectric nanogenerators to maximize charge density*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-15368-9.

title: Optimal three-dimensional betavoltaic geometry
open: Optimize radioactive-energy absorption and carrier collection together while accounting for source self-absorption, inactive material, interfaces, and recombination.
status: Murphy and colleagues analyzed three-dimensional design constraints in 2019. More source–semiconductor interface area does not automatically produce more useful electricity.
why: Small geometric changes can determine whether deposited energy creates collected charge or heat.
key_works: J. W. Murphy et al. (2019), *Design considerations for three-dimensional betavoltaics*, DOI:10.1063/1.5097775.

title: Surface-recombination control in nanowire betavoltaics
open: Preserve the collection advantage of nanowire architectures after realistic surface states, interfaces, and passivation aging are included.
status: Thomas and LaPierre’s 2024 analytical model predicts favorable performance for specified nanowire conditions. Its modeled efficiency is not an experimentally established packaged-device result.
why: Increasing interfacial area simultaneously increases opportunities for energy capture and carrier loss.
key_works: A. Thomas and R. R. LaPierre (2024), *Analytical model of a nanowire-based betavoltaic device*, DOI:10.1063/5.0202949.

title: Package-level power density over a betavoltaic service life
open: Predict and verify usable lifetime output per complete packaged mass and volume, including containment, interconnects, conversion electronics, isotope decay, and semiconductor aging.
status: Active-region design studies do not establish package-level performance or its evolution.
why: Remote devices are powered by complete sources, not isolated active layers.
key_works: Murphy et al. (2019), three-dimensional betavoltaic design assessment, DOI:10.1063/1.5097775.

title: Measurement-independent dynamic on-resistance in GaN
open: Recover dynamic on-resistance at a clearly specified instant after switching while correcting for measurement delay, parasitic circuits, heating, and rapid trap relaxation.
status: Dedicated characterization frameworks and instruments exist, but reported values depend on waveform and measurement timing.
why: Device rankings can change when measurements observe different stages of the same recovery transient.
key_works: S. Yang et al. (2019), *Dynamic On-Resistance in GaN Power Devices: Mechanisms, Characterizations, and Modeling*, DOI:10.1109/JESTPE.2019.2925117; T. Arai et al., Keysight dynamic-resistance measurement application note.

title: Waveform-history prediction of GaN trapping losses
open: Predict conduction losses under arbitrary switching histories using identifiable trap dynamics rather than a fitted multiplier derived from one stress waveform.
status: Dynamic-resistance research establishes dependencies on operating conditions and prior stress. Transfer from laboratory double-pulse tests to changing converter workloads remains a separate modeling requirement.
why: An efficient device at one test condition may incur substantial unmodeled losses in service.
key_works: G. Zulauf, M. Guacci, and J. W. Kolar (2020), *Dynamic on-resistance in GaN-on-Si HEMTs: Origins, dependencies, and future characterization frameworks*, DOI:10.1109/TPEL.2019.2955656.

title: Interpreting nonmonotonic resistance during GaN aging
open: Distinguish beneficial trap redistribution from accumulating damage when measured dynamic resistance initially decreases and subsequently rises.
status: Pan and colleagues reported such nonmonotonic behavior under power cycling in 2026. A falling resistance is therefore not necessarily evidence that device health is improving.
why: Conventional monotonic health indicators can miss damage or report false recovery.
key_works: C. Pan et al. (2026), *Anomalous dynamic on-resistance instability mechanisms of p-GaN gate AlGaN/GaN HEMTs under power cycling tests*, DOI:10.1063/5.0311656.

title: Separating recoverable trapping from new defect creation in SiC gates
open: Predict threshold-voltage evolution under realistic switching by distinguishing reversible charge trapping from stress-induced creation of additional oxide defects.
status: Volosov and colleagues investigated positive-bias temperature instability in 2024, including different contributions from existing and developing defects. Recovery after stress does not uniquely reveal permanent damage.
why: Lifetime forecasts require knowing which part of a threshold shift can reverse.
key_works: V. Volosov et al. (2024), *Positive Bias Temperature Instability in SiC-Based Power MOSFETs*, DOI:10.3390/mi15070872.

title: Synthesizing low-tortuosity electrodes without losing capacitance
open: Manufacture carbon networks with fast long-range ionic transport while preserving high accessible charge storage, electrode density, and mechanical integrity.
status: Kress, Liu, and Forse showed that network tortuosity controls fast charging; local diffusion or mesopore abundance alone is insufficient.
why: Opening transport pathways can improve rate while sacrificing the material that stores charge.
key_works: T. Kress, X. Liu, and A. C. Forse (2025, online), *Pore network tortuosity controls fast charging in supercapacitors*, DOI:10.1038/s41563-025-02404-6.

title: Charging waveforms that avoid ionic clogging
open: Design charging and discharging protocols that exploit pore-transport dynamics while respecting energy losses, voltage limits, and electrode heterogeneity.
status: Breitsprecher and colleagues demonstrated in 2020 that appropriately changing voltage protocols can accelerate transport; applying the maximum voltage immediately need not charge fastest.
why: Charge control can improve performance without replacing the electrode.
key_works: K. Breitsprecher et al. (2020), *How to speed up ion transport in nanopores*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-19903-6.

title: Relating measured self-diffusion to collective charging
open: Infer charging-relevant collective transport coefficients from operando ion-motion measurements, accounting for correlations, adsorption, and changing cation–anion populations.
status: In-situ diffusion NMR directly measures ion dynamics in operating electrodes. A tracer-like self-diffusion coefficient is not automatically the coefficient governing collective electrical response.
