why: Prevents a convenient microscopic measurement from being mistaken for a complete rate-performance predictor.
key_works: A. C. Forse et al. (2017), *Direct observation of ion dynamics in supercapacitor electrodes using in situ diffusion NMR spectroscopy*, DOI:10.1038/nenergy.2016.216.

title: Identifiability of charging bottlenecks in opaque carbon networks
open: Determine which measurements distinguish inaccessible pores, long pathways, constrictions, and local mobility limitations in an assembled electrode.
status: Tortuosity-sensitive measurements establish the importance of network connectivity, but different pore networks can share similar surface-area and pore-size summaries.
why: Synthesis cannot target the actual bottleneck when the diagnostic descriptors are nonunique.
key_works: Kress, Liu, and Forse (2025), pore-network tortuosity study, DOI:10.1038/s41563-025-02404-6.

title: Coupled cavitation and water hammer during load rejection
open: Predict pressure extremes and flow-state transitions when rapid electrical unloading produces cavitation, cavity collapse, and pressure waves throughout a pumped-storage waterway.
status: Liu and colleagues analyzed cavitation during load rejection in 2022. A steady cavitation map does not determine the consequences of a rapidly evolving hydraulic transient.
why: Safe flexibility depends on the complete hydraulic response to grid disturbances.
key_works: K. Liu et al. (2022), *Evolution and influence of pump-turbine cavitation during load rejection transients of a pumped-storage plant*, DOI:10.1080/00221686.2021.2004253.

title: Cavitation-safe contra-rotating pump-turbine operation
open: Optimize interacting rotor speeds and operating trajectories so acceptable efficiency and cavitation margins persist in both pumping and generating modes.
status: Fahlbeck and colleagues studied contra-rotating pump-turbines under cavitating conditions in 2024. Favorable nominal performance does not establish a safe envelope during reversals and off-design operation.
why: Additional rotor-control freedom is valuable only if it does not introduce unstable interactions.
key_works: J. Fahlbeck et al. (2024), *Performance characteristics of a contra-rotating pump-turbine in turbine and pump modes under cavitating flow conditions*, article PII:S0960148124016732.

title: Brine availability near heated waste in salt
open: Predict how much brine can reach a heated repository region, when it arrives, and how damage, inclusions, excavation history, and temperature gradients alter the supply.
status: The Brine Availability Test in Salt program provides targeted experiments and model comparisons. Bulk low permeability does not establish that no chemically consequential brine reaches a local heated surface.
why: Local water availability influences corrosion, gas production, and coupled repository evolution.
key_works: K. L. Kuhlman et al. (2023), *Brine Availability Test in Salt (BATS) FY23 Update*, DOI:10.2172/2369628.

title: Gas-driven damage in indurated clay
open: Predict whether repository gas moves through existing pathways, creates temporary openings, or causes persistent damage, with transfer from laboratory specimens to field scale.
status: DECOVALEX-2027’s HyMAR task explicitly addresses coupled gas transport and rock failure using laboratory and underground research evidence.
why: A gas-transport model must predict the pathways that gas itself changes.
key_works: DECOVALEX-2027, *HyMAR* task; Quintessa’s DECOVALEX research program description.

title: Seals that release gas while retaining water-barrier performance
open: Demonstrate repository seals that accommodate gas migration without developing persistent preferential pathways for groundwater.
status: DECOVALEX-2027’s BaSISS task investigates this coupled requirement using evidence associated with Andra’s underground research program.
why: Preventing pressure accumulation and preventing water flow can impose competing design requirements.
key_works: DECOVALEX-2027, *BaSISS* task; Quintessa’s coupled-model validation program.

title: Distinguishing numerical agreement from repository-model validity
open: Construct benchmarks that separate numerical implementation errors, parameter uncertainty, and disagreement between physical models when long-term direct validation is unavailable.
status: DECOVALEX Task F supplies structured repository-model comparisons, including salt cases. Agreement among codes using shared assumptions is not independent evidence that those assumptions are correct.
why: Long-horizon assurance requires explicit uncertainty about physical models, not only converged simulations.
key_works: T. C. LaForce et al. (2023), *DECOVALEX-2023: Task F Specification, Revision 10*, DOI:10.2172/2431152; *Task F2—Salt Final Report*, DOI:10.2172/2430083.

title: Predicting and recovering large solar-array deployment jams
open: Detect, localize, and recover deployment failures in extremely lightweight power structures without relying on unplanned ground intervention.
status: Caltech’s first space-solar mission experienced deployment problems not reproduced in ground testing and ultimately completed deployment using recovery actions.
why: Mass-efficient structures provide no energy if they cannot unfold reliably.
key_works: Caltech (2024), *Space Solar Power Project Ends First In-Space Mission with Successes and Lessons*.

title: Self-calibration of flexible wireless-power arrays
open: Maintain useful beam formation as a lightweight transmitter deforms, heats, ages, and loses individual elements, without calibration overhead consuming its benefit.
status: Caltech’s MAPLE experiment demonstrated wireless transfer and detectable transmission to Earth. Those demonstrations do not establish lifetime operation of a large power-delivery array.
why: Beam coherence depends on the actual deployed structure, not its design geometry.
key_works: Caltech (2024), first space-solar mission results and lessons.

title: Lunar power transmission beyond short thermal-vacuum trials
open: Qualify kilometre-scale lunar power delivery through repeated environmental cycles, cable deployment, dust exposure, faults, and long unattended service.
status: NASA’s 2024 competition finale tested systems against a 3 km transmission scenario in 48-hour thermal-vacuum trials. This is not equivalent to years of lunar operation.
why: Short qualification events must lead to credible surface-infrastructure reliability.
key_works: R. Bardan/NASA (2024), *NASA Awards $1.5 Million at Watts on the Moon Challenge Finale*.
prize: **Historical, awarded:** $1 million to H.E.L.P.S. and $500,000 to Orbital Mining; the cited finale is closed, not an available bounty.

title: Independently reproducible conductivity improvements
open: Demonstrate conductor improvements across independent laboratories using traceable geometry, temperature, contact, and composition measurements, while retaining useful mechanical properties.
status: DOE’s CABLE prize uses staged testing and manufacturing development. A favorable measurement on a short specimen does not establish transferable bulk performance.
why: Small claimed conductivity gains are vulnerable to dimensional and temperature errors.
key_works: DOE/HeroX, *Conductivity-enhanced materials for Affordable, Breakthrough Leapfrog Electric and thermal applications: CABLE Conductor Manufacturing Prize*.
prize: The official page advertises **$4.8 million overall**, but states that entry is closed and continuation is pending administration guidance; it should not be represented as an open application opportunity.

title: Preserving copper–graphene gains through ordinary wire processing
open: Retain conductivity and mechanical advantages through drawing, annealing, joining, bending, and production-length manufacturing rather than only in specially prepared short samples.
status: DOE’s CABLE Stage 2 selections include advanced copper-based processing approaches. Selection and prototype performance do not establish compatibility with every subsequent manufacturing step.
why: A conductor must survive the operations required to turn it into cables and windings.
key_works: DOE, *CABLE Conductor Manufacturing Prize Stage 2 Selections*, including copper–carbon manufacturing approaches.

title: Verifying a nominally all-metallic carbon-nanotube feedstock
open: Produce conductor-scale nanotube feedstock with a specified extremely low semiconducting fraction and verify that fraction with quantified detection limits and representative sampling.
status: The CABLE workshop explicitly identified both “100% metallic” nanotube supply and the question of how to measure that claim. Absolute purity cannot be established simply by failing to detect impurities.
why: Electronic-type heterogeneity can undermine reproducible conductor performance.
key_works: DOE AMMTO, *CABLE 2022: Big Idea Workshop Summary Report* (published 2023).

title: Partial-discharge qualification with two-phase cryogenic cooling
open: Predict insulation behavior when cryogenic coolant changes phase, producing moving interfaces and voids under electrical stress.
status: The CABLE workshop identifies two-phase cryogenic flow and partial-discharge testing as coupled gaps for cryo-resistive conductors.
why: Lower conductor resistance is useful only with dependable cooling and insulation.
key_works: DOE AMMTO, *CABLE 2022: Big Idea Workshop Summary Report*.

title: Causal partition of efficiency droop in green LEDs
open: Independently quantify Auger-related losses, polarization effects, carrier leakage, and heating under matched operating conditions rather than fitting several indistinguishable mechanisms to one efficiency curve.
status: Thirasuntrakul and colleagues apportioned droop contributors in studied devices in 2025. Such percentages are device- and model-dependent, not universal constants.
why: Design effort should target the loss that actually dominates a particular device.
key_works: P. Thirasuntrakul et al. (2025), *Efficiency droop contributors in InGaN green light emitting diodes*, Applied Physics Letters 126, 211103.

title: Certified carrier-density predictions from localization landscapes
open: Extend localization-landscape methods into error-controlled, self-consistent predictions of finite-temperature carrier populations and transport in disordered semiconductor devices.
status: Mathematical landscape laws bound the integrated density of states. Those established results do not automatically certify a nonlinear, biased, operating LED calculation.
why: Computational shortcuts become more trustworthy when their approximation errors are explicit.
key_works: G. David, M. Filoche, and S. Mayboroda (2019), *The landscape law for the integrated density of states*, arXiv:1909.10558.

title: Manufacturable cubic-nitride green LEDs
open: Realize the predicted benefits of cubic InGaN/GaN while controlling defects, phase purity, interfaces, and optical extraction at manufacturable device scale.
status: Lee, Leburton, and Bayram quantified design tradeoffs between cubic and conventional hexagonal structures in 2023. Removing a polarization penalty does not eliminate growth and defect penalties.
why: A theoretically favorable crystal symmetry must survive actual fabrication.
key_works: J. Lee, J.-P. Leburton, and C. Bayram (2023), *Design tradeoffs between traditional hexagonal and emerging cubic InxGa1−xN/GaN-based green light-emitting diodes*, DOI:10.1364/JOSAB.483832.

title: Simultaneously exploiting localization and maintaining carrier transport
open: Design disordered quantum-well structures that localize carriers enough to reduce harmful recombination while still delivering carriers uniformly to useful emitting regions.
status: Small-signal electroluminescence measurements distinguish carrier dynamics across blue, cyan, and green devices. Strong localization and efficient transport are not interchangeable benefits.
why: Prevents solving one loss mechanism by starving parts of the active region of carriers.
key_works: X. Li et al. (2023), *Carrier dynamics in blue, cyan, and green InGaN/GaN LEDs measured by small-signal electroluminescence*, DOI:10.1063/5.0151301.

title: Is a packed plasma catalyst actually catalyzing the surface reaction?
open: Separate chemical surface catalysis from changes in discharge geometry, local fields, heating, and plasma composition caused by inserting packing material.
status: Ndayirinde and colleagues found that packed catalysts acted principally as plasma modifiers in their 2023 ammonia experiments. A yield change upon adding a catalyst therefore does not, by itself, establish surface catalysis.
why: Otherwise, catalyst screening can optimize an electrical packing effect while assigning it the wrong chemical explanation.
key_works: C. Ndayirinde et al. (2023), *Plasma-catalytic ammonia synthesis: Packed catalysts act as plasma modifiers*, DOI:10.1016/j.cattod.2023.114156.

title: Catalysts that do not destroy plasma-produced ammonia
open: Identify surfaces that support useful formation pathways without accelerating ammonia decomposition enough to erase the nonequilibrium production advantage.
status: Lefferts’ 2024 analysis explains why catalysts effective under thermal conditions can be counterproductive when plasma changes the balance of forward and reverse reactions.
why: More catalytic activity is not necessarily more net product.
key_works: L. Lefferts (2024), *Leveraging Expertise in Thermal Catalysis to Understand Plasma Catalysis*, DOI:10.1002/ange.202305322.

title: Selective nitrogen excitation without wasteful hydrogen activation
open: Couple plasma and catalyst operation so useful nitrogen activation is preserved while unnecessary dissociation, vibrational relaxation, and other energy losses are suppressed.
status: Rouwenhorst and colleagues’ 2020 analysis identifies selective activation as central to competitive plasma-driven ammonia synthesis. A high conversion rate alone does not show that excitation energy is being used efficiently.
why: Plasma energy can disappear into species and pathways that do not increase ammonia output.
key_works: K. H. R. Rouwenhorst et al. (2020), *Plasma-driven catalysis: green ammonia synthesis with intermittent electricity*, DOI:10.1039/D0GC02058C; P. Mehta et al. (2020), *Plasma-Catalytic Ammonia Synthesis beyond the Equilibrium Limit*, DOI:10.1021/acscatal.0c00684.

title: Product removal that preserves plasma-synthesis efficiency
open: Integrate ammonia capture and regeneration with plasma synthesis so suppressing back-reaction yields a net benefit after separation, recycle, and pressure losses.
status: Lower product concentration can reduce undesired reverse reactions, but it also creates a harder downstream separation problem.
why: An improved reactor can become a worse complete process.
key_works: Lefferts (2024), plasma-catalysis perspective, DOI:10.1002/ange.202305322.

title: Spectral-gap lower bounds for the piston energy-exchange model
open: Prove a system-size-dependent lower bound for the spectral gap of the piston model’s energy-exchange process strong enough to support a diffusive hydrodynamic limit, including configurations with very little energy at individual sites.
status: Szász’s April 2026 workshop presentation explicitly identifies this bound as open. Corresponding results for the original Gaspard–Gilbert model do not automatically transfer to the piston model.
why: Quantifies whether local energy exchanges equilibrate sufficiently quickly for macroscopic heat diffusion.
key_works: D. Szász (2026), *Fourier law from Hamiltonian dynamics*, Erwin Schrödinger Institute workshop presentation, April 17.

title: Hydrodynamic limit of the piston model
open: Derive the macroscopic heat equation from the piston energy-exchange process, with a justified transport coefficient and controlled initial conditions.
status: The 2026 workshop account distinguishes obtaining a Markov process in a rare-interaction limit from obtaining its hydrodynamic limit; it explicitly lists the latter as unresolved.
why: A stochastic description of microscopic exchanges is not yet a derivation of Fourier-scale transport.
key_works: Szász (2026), *Fourier law from Hamiltonian dynamics*, discussing the Bálint–Nándori–Szász–Tóth piston-model program.

title: Autonomous anharmonic derivation of normal heat diffusion
open: Derive a heat equation with finite, positive conductivity for a specified class of pinned, genuinely anharmonic Hamiltonian lattices without adding stochastic noise or an externally prescribed chaotic drive.
status: Canestrari, Liverani, and Olla’s 2026 theorem treats a harmonic chain with deterministic chaotic forcing. It does not settle this autonomous anharmonic formulation.
why: Connects irreversible heat conduction to ordinary interacting mechanical constituents.
key_works: G. Canestrari, C. Liverani, and S. Olla (2026), *Heat equation from a deterministic dynamics*, DOI:10.1007/s00222-026-01429-1.

title: From mean heat evolution to a law of large numbers
open: Strengthen deterministic heat-equation results from convergence of average energy density to concentration of the empirical energy field, with adequate control of higher moments.
status: The 2026 Canestrari–Liverani–Olla result establishes averaged evolution; its discussion distinguishes this from stronger fluctuation control.
why: Macroscopic predictability requires typical realizations to resemble the mean.
key_works: Canestrari, Liverani, and Olla (2026), *Heat equation from a deterministic dynamics*, DOI:10.1007/s00222-026-01429-1.

title: Microscopic origin of thermal Hall signals in nonmagnetic crystals
open: Predict the sign, magnitude, temperature dependence, and field dependence of transverse phonon heat transport in nonmagnetic crystals without fitting an unexplained transverse-scattering coefficient separately for every material.
status: Jin and colleagues reported signals across several nonmagnetic crystals in 2025 and proposed an empirical relationship between longitudinal and transverse conductivities. Broad observation and scaling do not uniquely establish a microscopic mechanism.
why: Determines whether transverse heat transport can become a predictable materials property.
key_works: X. B. Jin et al. (2025), *Discovery of Universal Phonon Thermal Hall Effect in Crystals*, DOI:10.1103/r572-5dfm; arXiv:2404.02863.

title: The crystal-to-glass boundary of phonon Hall transport
open: Determine how the thermal Hall response changes under controlled loss of crystalline order while independently measuring changes in phonon transport, impurities, and local structure.
status: Ling, Fauqué, and Behnia reported a finite response in quartz but no detected response in amorphous silica within their measurement resolution in 2026. That comparison does not isolate which aspect of disorder suppresses the effect.
why: Distinguishes mechanisms requiring crystalline coherence from mechanisms compatible with local structural motifs.
key_works: Y. Ling, B. Fauqué, and K. Behnia (2026), *Phonon Thermal Hall Effect in quartz and its absence in silica*, arXiv:2604.01908; DOI:10.21468/SciPostPhys.21.2.036.

title: Separating magnetic and nonmagnetic phonon Hall contributions
open: Quantify how magnetic-ion scattering, ordinary disorder, and nonmagnetic mechanisms combine, using substitutions that distinguish their effects rather than changing all three simultaneously.
status: Sharma, Valldor, and Lorenz compared nonmagnetic and magnetic titanates in 2024. Similarities in Hall ratios despite substantial changes in longitudinal transport challenge simple attribution to magnetic scattering alone.
why: A successful explanation must account for both magnetic and nonmagnetic control samples.
key_works: R. Sharma, M. Valldor, and T. Lorenz (2024), *Phonon thermal Hall effect in nonmagnetic Y₂Ti₂O₇*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.110.L100301.

title: Lifetime-optimal circular versus figure-eight flight
open: Select airborne-wind trajectories using measured fatigue and replacement consequences, not average cycle power alone.
status: A 2026 comparison finds different power and load-oscillation advantages for circular and figure-eight trajectories. It explicitly leaves quantitative fatigue assessment for further work.
why: The most productive flight pattern per cycle may be the least economical over equipment life.
key_works: D. Eijkelhof, N. Rossi, and R. Schmehl (2026), *Optimal flight pattern debate for airborne wind energy systems: circular or figure of eight?*, DOI:10.5194/wes-11-1287-2026.

title: Hard-constraint guarantees through airborne-wind pumping transitions
open: Guarantee tether-force, actuator, and flight-envelope constraints during transitions between power production and tether retrieval, including gusts and winch saturation.
status: The 2026 trajectory study uses modeling simplifications and does not impose its studied force restrictions uniformly through every transition.
why: Short transition intervals can govern peak loads and loss-of-control risk.
key_works: Eijkelhof, Rossi, and Schmehl (2026), flight-pattern comparison, DOI:10.5194/wes-11-1287-2026.

title: Distinguishing wind changes from airborne sensor failure
open: Determine when kite measurements uniquely identify wind, aerodynamic changes, and sensor faults, and specify the minimum additional sensing needed when they do not.
status: Cayon, Watson, and Schmehl documented cases where sensor saturation or modeling errors produced misleading inferred winds. Constraining an estimated wind component can suppress artifacts while also hiding real flow.
why: A controller should not respond to an instrument artifact as though it were a gust.
key_works: O. Cayon, S. Watson, and R. Schmehl (2025), *Kite as a sensor: wind and state estimation in tethered flying systems*, DOI:10.5194/wes-10-2161-2025.

title: Recovering atmospheric turbulence from a moving kite
open: Reconstruct turbulence statistics while correcting for kite motion, changing altitude, estimator filtering, and the difference between moving and fixed sampling.
status: The 2025 kite-sensing study resolves a useful frequency band but also documents filtering and comparison limitations.
why: A kite’s measured time series is not automatically the stationary atmospheric spectrum needed for design.
key_works: Cayon, Watson, and Schmehl (2025), *Kite as a sensor*, DOI:10.5194/wes-10-2161-2025.

title: The controllability boundary of depowered membrane wings
open: Predict the boundary beyond which reduced aerodynamic loading and slack steering lines prevent reliable turning, and preserve control while approaching that boundary.
status: Elfert, Göhlich, and Schmehl’s 2024 experiments show that steering response depends on depowering and line tension. A turning law calibrated in powered flight cannot simply be extrapolated to retrieval.
why: Reducing retrieval energy is useful only while the wing remains controllable.
key_works: C. Elfert, D. Göhlich, and R. Schmehl (2024), *Measurement of the turning behaviour of tethered membrane wings using automated flight manoeuvres*, DOI:10.5194/wes-9-2261-2024.

title: Closed-loop prediction of suspended control-unit swing
open: Predict coupled wing and suspended-control-unit motion when aerodynamic forces and steering evolve dynamically, rather than prescribing the measured wing trajectory.
status: Schelbergen and Schmehl’s 2024 analysis reproduces important swinging behavior using a two-mass representation, but deliberately excludes parts of unconstrained aerodynamic and yaw dynamics.
why: Swinging changes bridle loads, attitude measurements, and the effectiveness of control actions.
key_works: M. Schelbergen and R. Schmehl (2024), *Swinging motion of a kite with suspended control unit flying turning manoeuvres*, DOI:10.5194/wes-9-1323-2024.

title: Duty-cycle-based lifetime of airborne-wind tethers
open: Predict replacement life from combined tensile loading, repeated bending over drums, environmental exposure, and changing flight trajectories.
status: Joshi, von Terzi, and Schmehl’s 2025 system analysis identifies tether replacement as a consequential cost driver; uncertain lifetime remains embedded in scaling conclusions.
why: A lightweight tether can become expensive if service conditions consume it rapidly.
key_works: R. Joshi, D. von Terzi, and R. Schmehl (2025), *System design and scaling trends in airborne wind energy demonstrated for a ground-generation concept*, DOI:10.5194/wes-10-695-2025.

title: Airborne-wind capacity optimum after farm integration
open: Determine whether the preferred individual-system size changes once shared infrastructure, operating interactions, and replacement logistics are included.
status: The 2025 study finds a modeled 500 kW optimum among its examined sizes and assumptions. That is not an experimentally established universal optimum or a complete farm optimum.
why: Scaling a machine and scaling a power plant are different optimization problems.
key_works: Joshi, von Terzi, and Schmehl (2025), airborne-wind scaling study, DOI:10.5194/wes-10-695-2025.

title: Trajectory-dependent airborne-wind noise prediction
open: Predict field sound and perceived disturbance across flight paths, pumping phases, and launch or landing, with validation beyond short normalized listening samples.
status: Schmidt and colleagues’ 2025 listening experiment included 75 participants and several prototype recordings. Its controlled comparisons do not establish long-duration community response to complete operating cycles.
why: Sound characteristics can constrain acceptable flight schedules and installation layouts.
key_works: H. Schmidt et al. (2025), *Exploring noise annoyance and sound quality for airborne wind energy systems: insights from a listening experiment*, DOI:10.5194/wes-10-579-2025.

title: Trace-carbon control of iron-particle fragmentation
open: Predict when carbon impurities cause burning iron particles to fragment, distinguishing carbon-related gas generation from fragmentation associated with oxygen-rich oxide states.
status: Peng and colleagues compared powders containing 0.117 and 0.037 wt% carbon in 2025 and identified distinct fragmentation behavior. A transferable threshold and daughter-particle distribution remain to be established.
why: Fragmentation changes burnout, particle collection, and the material available for recycling.
key_works: F. Peng et al. (2025), *Micro-explosion of burning iron particles with carbon impurity*, DOI:10.1016/j.combustflame.2025.113974.

title: Nanoparticle birth versus nanoparticle-cloud visibility
open: Infer the actual onset and rate of nanoparticle formation separately from the time at which particles escape the parent-particle flow field and become optically visible.
status: Li and colleagues’ 2026 measurements and simulations show that flow toward a burning particle can delay observable nanoparticle release. A delayed visible cloud need not indicate delayed nucleation.
why: Incorrect onset inference leads to incorrect vaporization and nucleation models.
key_works: T. Li et al. (2026), *Critical nanoparticle formation in iron combustion: single particle experiments with in-situ multi-parameter diagnostics aided by multi-scale simulations*, DOI:10.1016/j.fuel.2025.136303.

title: Thermophoretic corrections to iron-nanoparticle recapture
open: Derive and validate nanoparticle-collection models that include large temperature gradients and temperature-dependent properties around burning iron particles.
status: Hartmann and colleagues’ 2026 model incorporates Stefan flow but assumes constant temperature; its conclusion explicitly leaves thermophoresis and variable properties to future work.
why: An isothermal collection model may mispredict how much iron escapes the recycling loop.
key_works: N. Hartmann et al. (2026), *Modelling nanoparticle deposition rate in iron particle combustion*, DOI:10.1016/j.fuel.2025.136268.

title: Validity of quasi-steady collection during flow reversal
open: Determine when nanoparticle capture can be approximated by successive steady states as oxidation draws gas inward and evaporation subsequently drives it outward.
status: Hartmann and colleagues explicitly identify time-dependent applicability as unresolved; their steady collection correlations do not settle memory effects during the reversal.
why: The same particle can alternate between collecting and expelling surrounding material.
key_works: Hartmann et al. (2026), nanoparticle-deposition study, DOI:10.1016/j.fuel.2025.136268.

title: Cycle-to-cycle evolution of recyclable iron-powder morphology
open: Predict whether repeated oxidation and reduction drive particle size, internal porosity, cracks, and phase distribution toward a stable population or progressive fragmentation.
status: Choisez and colleagues resolved major microstructural transformations during iron-powder combustion in 2022. Characterizing one transformation does not determine the trajectory of many complete recycling cycles.
why: Reaction rates and collection requirements may change as the fuel is reused.
key_works: L. Choisez et al. (2022), *Phase transformations and microstructure evolution during combustion of iron powder*, DOI:10.1016/j.actamat.2022.118261.

title: Useful cracking versus disintegration in steam–iron pellets
open: Control redox-generated cracks so they improve gas access without causing unacceptable loss of pellet strength or production of fines.
status: Knapp and colleagues’ 2026 experiments connect pellet processing, cracking, mechanical behavior, and hydrogen yield over ten cycles.
why: The microstructural change that accelerates reaction can also destroy the reactor’s packed material.
key_works: A. Knapp et al. (2026), *Iron as a recyclable energy carrier: Redox cycling of iron oxide pellets for hydrogen storage*, DOI:10.1016/j.proci.2026.106158.

title: Predictable benefits from impurities in steam–iron storage
open: Specify impurity and processing windows that preserve useful hydrogen yield and pellet integrity across variable low-cost iron-oxide feeds.
status: Knapp and colleagues found favorable cycling behavior in studied lower-purity material containing trace aluminum and chromium. “Higher purity” was not automatically better.
why: Useful impurity effects must be reproducible before they can support low-cost feed specifications.
key_works: Knapp et al. (2026), steam–iron pellet-cycling study, DOI:10.1016/j.proci.2026.106158.

title: Redox-aware oxygen-carrier attrition qualification
open: Develop a test that predicts reactor particle loss under coupled chemical, thermal, and mechanical cycling, rather than relying on cold mechanical attrition alone.
status: A 2026 50 kW thermal-scale study reports favorable standard attrition indices despite consequential deterioration during operation.
why: A material can pass a screening test yet fail economically in its intended reactor.
key_works: A. Filsouf et al. (2026), *Physicochemical evolution of a Cu/Mn/Fe oxygen carrier in a 50 kWth chemical looping with oxygen uncoupling unit with solid fuels*, DOI:10.1016/j.fuel.2025.137162.

title: Designing for the oxygen carrier’s evolved phase assemblage
open: Optimize oxygen release and mechanical stability using the phases formed during operation, including copper redistribution, rather than only the fresh material’s nominal composition.
status: Filsouf and colleagues observe substantial phase and microstructural evolution; retained chemical activity does not imply retained particle strength.
why: The durable operating material may differ from the material initially loaded.
key_works: Filsouf et al. (2026), Cu/Mn/Fe carrier-evolution study, DOI:10.1016/j.fuel.2025.137162.

title: The ash-composition window between reinforcement and agglomeration
open: Predict which biomass-ash compositions strengthen oxygen carriers without suppressing oxygen transfer or promoting problematic agglomeration.
status: A 2023 red-mud study reduced cumulative attrition from 2.74% to 0.35% with one corn-straw-ash treatment. Different ashes produced different reactivity–strength tradeoffs; the improvement is not a universal ash-addition rule.
why: A variable waste stream could be a useful reinforcement or a source of failure.
key_works: L. Yang et al. (2023), *Improving attrition resistance of oxygen carriers by biomass ash in chemical looping process*, DOI:10.1016/j.fuel.2023.128352.

title: Mechanism-resolved activation of TiFe hydrogen-storage alloys
open: Determine when activation is controlled by surface oxide conversion, catalytic surface species, secondary phases, or exposure of fresh material through cracking.
status: TiFe has decades of successful activation methods, but different preparation and exposure histories support different explanations. The open problem is predictive mechanism selection, not first activation of TiFe.
why: Reliable low-temperature commissioning requires more than reproducing one preparation recipe.
key_works: T. Schober (1983), *On the activation of FeTi for hydrogen storage*, DOI:10.1016/0022-5088(83)90249-7; E. M. Dematteis et al. (2021), *Substitutional effects in TiFe for hydrogen storage*, DOI:10.1039/D1MA00101A.

title: Controlling substitution sites to maximize usable hydride capacity
open: Manufacture TiFe alloys with reliably controlled substitution-site populations and phase fractions so both hydrogenation stages remain inside a specified operating-pressure window.
status: Jung and colleagues showed in 2021 that vanadium on titanium and iron sites shifts the two plateaus differently. A nominal alloy composition does not uniquely specify those occupancies or secondary phases.
why: Total theoretical capacity is not the capacity recoverable between practical charging and discharge pressures.
key_works: J. Y. Jung et al. (2021), *Tailoring the equilibrium hydrogen pressure of TiFe via vanadium substitution*, DOI:10.1016/j.jallcom.2020.157263.

title: Testing temperature-dependent coherent phase transformation in palladium hydride
open: Experimentally distinguish coherent two-phase transformation from nearly homogeneous hydrogen uptake as temperature, specimen size, and defect-mediated strain relaxation change.
status: Rahm, Löfgren, and Erhart’s calculations predict a change in transformation character around 400 K under their coherent-system assumptions. Real specimens introduce relaxation pathways that must be separated from the predicted effect.
why: Hysteresis determines recoverable work and operating pressures in reversible hydrogen storage.
key_works: J. M. Rahm, J. Löfgren, and P. Erhart (2022), *Quantitative predictions of thermodynamic hysteresis: Temperature-dependent character of the phase transition in Pd–H*, DOI:10.1016/j.actamat.2022.117697; arXiv:2110.07883.

title: Isomer-resolved kinetics of commercial dibenzyltoluene
open: Predict hydrogenation and dehydrogenation across commercial feed lots using their actual isomer and intermediate distributions, rather than only an average hydrogenation degree.
status: Ji and colleagues’ 2023 analysis resolves substantial chemical complexity within material often treated as one carrier. A single global conversion measure can conceal different intermediate inventories.
why: Feed-lot changes can alter reaction behavior even when nominal specifications appear identical.
key_works: X. Ji et al. (2023), *Analysis of Dibenzyltoluene Mixtures: From Fast Analysis to In-Depth Characterization of the Compounds*, DOI:10.3390/molecules28093751.

title: Dehydrogenation activity without accelerated carrier destruction
open: Select catalyst modifications that increase useful hydrogen release without proportionally increasing irreversible side products, and validate the tradeoff over repeated carrier recycling.
status: Garidzirai, Modisha, and Bessarabov’s study finds that activity-enhancing modifications can also change by-product formation. Faster dehydrogenation alone is therefore an incomplete catalyst objective.
why: Carrier replacement and purification can consume the value of improved reactor productivity.
key_works: R. Garidzirai, P. Modisha, and D. Bessarabov (2024), *Assessment of Reaction Kinetics for the Dehydrogenation of Perhydro-Dibenzyltoluene Using Mg- and Zn-Modified Pt/Al₂O₃ Catalysts*, DOI:10.3390/catal14010032; published online December 2023.

title: Residual heat-transport losses after Gedeon-streaming suppression
open: Predict temperature profiles and heat flows after the mean circulation around a thermoacoustic loop has been suppressed, including local streaming and other unmodeled transport.
status: Kruse, Schmiel, and Tajmar achieved good acoustic agreement after tuning their model, yet thermal discrepancies persisted; eliminating Gedeon streaming did not eliminate the mismatch.
why: Matching pressure oscillations is insufficient evidence that a heat-engine model predicts efficiency.
key_works: A. Kruse, T. Schmiel, and M. Tajmar (2018), *Experimental validation of a looped-tube thermoacoustic engine with a stub for tuning acoustic conditions*, DOI:10.1016/j.enconman.2018.09.069.

title: Using turbulence beneficially in thermoacoustic jet pumps
open: Predict and exploit the operating region where turbulence reduces flow separation and improves useful pressure bias, while accounting for the complete acoustic dissipation.
status: Oosterhuis and colleagues experimentally found that turbulence can improve jet-pump behavior relative to laminar separated flow. “Avoid turbulence” is therefore not a universally correct design rule.
why: Streaming suppression should cost as little acoustic power as possible.
key_works: J. P. Oosterhuis et al. (2017), *Flow Separation and Turbulence in Jet Pumps for Thermoacoustic Applications*, DOI:10.1007/s10494-016-9731-8; published online 2016.

title: Aircraft-level benefit of thermoacoustic heat transport
open: Demonstrate a net aircraft benefit from thermoacoustic thermal management after system mass, acoustic losses, heat rejection, operating variability, and conventional alternatives are included.
status: NASA’s 2025 work reports development and testing of thermoacoustic thermal-management concepts. Component operation does not establish a mission-level energy or payload advantage.
why: A heat-management improvement can be offset by the mass and equipment needed to obtain it.
key_works: L. A. Rodriguez et al. (2025), *Thermoacoustic Thermal Management for Electric Aircraft*, NASA NTRS:20240015017.

title: Conductivity-anisotropy uncertainty in induced-current forecasts
open: Determine which subsurface conductivity measurements are necessary to predict local geomagnetically induced currents, and propagate unresolved anisotropy into operational uncertainty bounds.
status: Zhang and colleagues’ 2026 North China study compares simplified and anisotropic conductivity descriptions and finds consequential differences. A good regional magnetic-field estimate does not uniquely determine local geoelectric forcing.
why: Limited geological surveys should target the uncertainties that matter most to exposed assets.
key_works: X. Zhang et al. (2026), *Estimating the Geomagnetically Induced Currents in the 1,000 kV Power Grid Over North China During the May 2024 Geomagnetic Storm: Accounting for Anisotropic Earth Conductivity*, DOI:10.1029/2026SW004996.

title: End-to-end uncertainty for storm-induced grid currents
open: Forecast local current timing and extremes with calibrated uncertainty across the complete chain from space-weather forcing through ground conductivity and network response.
status: Wilkerson and colleagues compare measurements and models for the May 2024 storm; predictive agreement varies substantially by modeling stage and location.
why: Operators need the timing and severity of local consequences, not merely a global storm category.
key_works: L. A. Wilkerson et al. (2025–2026), *GIC-Related Observations During the May 2024 Geomagnetic Storm in the United States*, arXiv:2507.07009; DOI:10.1029/2025SW004758.

title: Cross-storm benchmarks with network and grounding context
open: Build reusable benchmarks pairing current measurements with sufficiently complete magnetic, geological, grounding, and network-state information across multiple storm types.
status: The Wilkerson dataset includes observations from 47 current-monitoring sites, but evidence from one major event does not establish performance on other storms or configurations.
why: Otherwise, a forecasting method can appear transferable because crucial site-specific assumptions remain hidden.
key_works: Wilkerson et al. (2025–2026), United States GIC observations, DOI:10.1029/2025SW004758.

title: Asset-specific induced-current-to-reactive-power response
open: Predict transformer saturation, harmonic production, and reactive-power demand from induced current while accounting for transformer construction and operating state.
status: Clilverd and colleagues measured different reactive-power responses in two transformers during the May 2024 storm. Their observed thresholds and slopes are asset-specific, not universal safe-current limits.
why: Equal measured neutral currents need not imply equal system consequences.
key_works: M. A. Clilverd et al. (2025), *Geomagnetically Induced Currents, Transformer Harmonics, and Reactive Power Impacts of the Gannon Storm in May 2024*, DOI:10.1029/2024SW004235.

title: Validating thermal damage from realistic geomagnetic waveforms
open: Calibrate component hot-spot and damage models against realistic intermittent current histories, distinguishing brief peaks from sustained thermal accumulation.
status: Rivers and colleagues’ 2024 global overheating study is a conditional model, not a measurement of worldwide transformer damage. Uncertain component response remains important to its interpretation.
why: An induced-current exceedance is not automatically a damaged transformer.
key_works: M. Rivers, Ł. G. Gajewski, and D. Denkenberger (2024), *Global transformer overheating from geomagnetic storms*, arXiv:2403.18070.

title: Desiccants that do not destroy fluoronitrile insulating gas
open: Remove water from C₄F₇N/CO₂ insulation systems without catalyzing gas decomposition or introducing products from degradation of the desiccant itself.
status: Gao and colleagues’ nine-month aging study found incompatibility for the tested zeolite sieve and possible decomposition of the tested organic alternative. High adsorption area can intensify unwanted chemistry.
why: A component intended to protect insulation can instead degrade the insulating medium.
key_works: W. Gao et al. (2021), *Compatibility of Molecular Sieves with C₄F₇N/CO₂ Insulating Gas Mixture*, DOI:10.1109/CEIDP50766.2021.9705379.

title: Spatial validation of HVDC cable aging during polarity reversal
open: Validate where insulation damage accumulates during voltage-polarity reversals, including the influence of temperature-dependent conductivity and residual charge.
status: Diban and colleagues’ 2024 model predicts strongly nonuniform lifetime reduction, especially in inner insulation. This is modeled damage distribution, not direct lifetime validation.
why: Average electric-field stress can conceal the region that governs failure.
key_works: B. Diban et al. (2024), *Life Estimation of HVDC Cables Subjected to Fast and Slow Polarity Reversals*, DOI:10.3390/en17133182.

title: State-dependent waiting times before HVDC polarity reversal
open: Select a reversal waveform and zero-voltage interval from the cable’s estimated charge and thermal state, balancing service interruption against insulation stress.
status: Diban and colleagues find that longer zero-voltage intervals reduce modeled stress through charge relaxation. Their results do not establish a universal waiting time for every material or operating history.
why: Conservative fixed delays can waste capacity, while short delays can retain damaging charge memory.
key_works: Diban et al. (2024), polarity-reversal lifetime study, DOI:10.3390/en17133182.

title: Demonstrated low-cost heliostats under a complete installation boundary
open: Achieve the program’s $50/m² heliostat target under an explicit cost boundary that includes installation and required optical performance, rather than a selected low-cost component.
status: The Heliostat Prize’s August 2026 winners demonstrated component advances; that does not establish a complete field at the target cost.
why: Component savings must survive assembly, alignment, and deployment.
key_works: DOE American-Made Program (2026), *Heliostat Prize*, final results announced August 6.
prize: **Closed and awarded:** $3 million program; three final winners received $300,000 each. This is not an open bounty.

title: Optical lifetime of thermoplastic-composite heliostat facets
open: Preserve mirror shape and pointing quality despite long-term creep, thermal gradients, moisture, and repeated wind loading.
status: A thermoplastic-composite sandwich facet was among the 2026 prize-winning prototypes. Structural strength and protective additives do not alone establish lifetime optical accuracy.
why: A mechanically intact reflector can become optically ineffective.
key_works: DOE American-Made Program (2026), *Heliostat Prize* results, Multiscale Systems component.

title: Direct observation of the spin Ettingshausen effect
open: Measure a transverse heat current generated by an injected spin current in a nonmagnetic conductor, separating it from ordinary Joule heating, interfacial Peltier heating, and magnetic proximity effects.
status: The reciprocal spin Nernst effect has experimental support. Uchida and Hirai’s May 2026 perspective still identifies direct spin Ettingshausen thermometry as an outstanding experiment.
why: Completes an experimentally incomplete transport relationship relevant to electrically controlled heat routing.
key_works: K. Uchida and T. Hirai (2026), *Spin caloritronics: History and future prospects of experiments*, arXiv:2605.01692; S. Meyer et al. (2017), *Observation of the spin Nernst effect*, DOI:10.1038/nmat4964.

title: Experimental separation of spin Thomson heating
open: Detect reversible heating or cooling proportional to both spin current and temperature gradient, and distinguish electron-mediated and magnon-mediated contributions where both are possible.
status: Spin-dependent Thomson responses have theoretical descriptions; the May 2026 experimental perspective identifies their observation as unresolved.
why: Determines whether distributed spin-dependent heating can supplement interface-localized thermal control.
key_works: Uchida and Hirai (2026), *Spin caloritronics: History and future prospects of experiments*, arXiv:2605.01692; A. Slachter et al. (2011), *Modeling of thermal spin transport and spin-orbit effects in ferromagnetic/nonmagnetic mesoscopic devices*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.84.174408.

title: The unexplained fraction of giant magnetothermal resistance
open: Explain the measured magnetic-state-dependent thermal-conductivity change in metallic multilayers using independently constrained electronic, lattice, interfacial, and magnetic transport contributions.
status: Makino and colleagues measured a change of approximately 37 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ in a Co₅₀Fe₅₀/Cu multilayer. Their electronic estimate accounts for roughly 35%; the remainder is not automatically proof of a particular alternative carrier.
why: Predictable thermal switching requires a mechanism that explains the full measured response.
key_works: F. Makino et al. (2025), *Study of magneto-thermal resistance effect in a Co50Fe50/Cu multilayer through the analysis of electron and lattice thermal conductivities*, arXiv:2505.09195.

title: Ferron-drag thermoelectricity beyond the screening length
open: Explain why a metal’s ferron-drag thermal response can increase with thickness beyond its charge-screening length, quantitatively distinguishing direct coupling from electron–phonon–ferron mediation.
status: Itoh and colleagues reported nonlocal ferron-drag thermoelectricity in August 2026, including thickness behavior not captured by the simplest interfacial picture.
why: Identifies the length scales that should govern device geometry.
key_works: T. Itoh et al. (2026), *Observation of nonlocal ferron-drag thermoelectricity*, arXiv:2608.15596.

title: Reciprocal transport closure for ferron-drag devices
open: Measure reciprocal electrical and thermal responses in the same metal–ferroelectric structure, with matched polarization states and quantified parasitic heat transport.
status: The 2026 observation establishes polarization-dependent thermal signals. A complete experimentally constrained transport matrix is a stronger requirement than detecting one response.
why: Enables credible predictions of loaded generation or cooling.
key_works: Itoh et al. (2026), arXiv:2608.15596; P. Tang, K. Uchida, and G. E. W. Bauer (2023), *Nonlocal drag thermoelectricity generated by ferroelectric van der Waals heterostructures*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.107.L121406.

title: Stable nanoclusters for flexible anomalous-Nernst conversion
open: Preserve the cluster size, distribution, and amorphous host structure responsible for enhanced transverse thermoelectric response through processing, bending, and thermal exposure.
status: Gautam and colleagues demonstrated flexible material with an anomalous Nernst coefficient around 3.7 μV K⁻¹ using nanostructure engineering. The remaining target is retention of the useful microstructure during service.
why: Flexible conversion performance should not disappear through cluster coarsening or host crystallization.
key_works: R. Gautam et al. (2024), *Creation of flexible spin-caloritronic material with giant transverse thermoelectric conversion by nanostructure engineering*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-46475-6.

title: Percolation without thermal short-circuiting in bulk spin-Seebeck materials
open: Optimize conducting networks in magnetic-insulator composites so electrical collection improves without excessively shunting the thermal gradients that drive spin transport.
status: Park and colleagues demonstrated a bulk spin-Seebeck composite using platinum-coated magnetic-insulator particles. Bulk operation is established; the coupled electrical, thermal, and spin-interface optimum remains a distinct design problem.
why: More conductive material can improve one transport channel while weakening the source of conversion.
key_works: S. J. Park et al. (2026), *Trans-scale spin Seebeck effect in nanostructured bulk composites based on magnetic insulator*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-75232-0; arXiv:2509.08327.

title: Experimental validation of screening-current-assisted quench propagation
open: Measure whether screening currents accelerate thermal propagation as predicted, and determine when that acceleration improves protection versus increasing damage elsewhere.
status: Pardo and colleagues predict enhanced propagation in a modeled ultra-high-field REBCO magnet. Agreement between numerical formulations does not replace spatially resolved quench measurements.
why: Screening currents could change protection requirements rather than merely perturb the magnetic field.
key_works: E. Pardo et al. (2025–2026), *Screening currents increase thermal quench propagation speed in ultra-high-field REBCO magnets*, arXiv:2509.06621.

title: Controlling the tails of turn-to-turn contact resistance
open: Specify and manufacture contact-resistance distributions whose local extremes remain safe under nonuniform pressure and temperature, rather than qualifying only their average.
status: Lu and colleagues demonstrated contact treatments stable through 30,000 pressure cycles at 4.2 K in studied samples. They also emphasize that excessively low and high contact resistance produce different hazards.
why: A small unfavorable region can govern a coil’s protection behavior.
key_works: J. Lu et al. (2026), *Control of turn-to-turn contact resistivity in resistively insulated REBCO coils*, arXiv:2604.15587.

title: Identifiability limits for superconducting inter-tape contact networks
open: Determine which internal contact resistances can be uniquely reconstructed from accessible cable terminals, and which require additional excitations or sensors.
status: The TITO method improves contact-resistance inference by accounting for parallel current paths. It does not establish arbitrary spatial reconstruction of every internal contact.
why: Prevents overinterpreting a terminal measurement as a unique internal defect map.
key_works: R. Teyber et al. (2025), *Tape-in-tape-out: a new approach for in-situ contact resistance measurements in high temperature superconducting CORC cables*, DOI:10.1088/1361-6668/aded3b.

title: Separating contact degradation from a developing normal zone
open: Infer whether changing cable voltages originate from altered inter-tape contacts, local loss of superconductivity, or both during a transient.
status: The TITO research identifies monitoring through superconducting-to-normal transitions as a further application; static contact characterization does not solve this dynamic attribution problem.
why: The appropriate protective response depends on which internal state is changing.
key_works: Teyber et al. (2025), TITO contact-resistance study, DOI:10.1088/1361-6668/aded3b.

title: Whole-system energy advantage of conduction-cooled flux pumps
open: Determine when contactless flux pumping reduces total electricity consumption after alternating-field losses, cryocooler work, switching, and avoided current-lead heat loads are included.
status: Iftikhar and colleagues demonstrated conduction-cooled flux pumping below 77 K. Successful current injection does not by itself identify the most efficient operating temperature and excitation schedule.
why: Eliminating a warm-to-cold conductor can introduce other refrigeration burdens.
key_works: M. H. Iftikhar et al. (2025), *A compact conduction cooled flux pump operating below 77 K*, DOI:10.1088/1361-6668/adaf5c.

title: Production-length suppression of the REBCO thickness effect
open: Preserve high critical-current density through thick superconducting layers over production-length tape, including deposition drift, defects, and position-dependent pinning.
status: Xia and colleagues demonstrated 6 μm layers without a discernible thickness penalty in their studied conductors, including 2,500 A per centimetre of tape width at 20 K and 10 T. Uniform production-length yield remains a stronger requirement.
why: Increasing superconducting thickness is useful only when long-length defects do not dominate usable current.
key_works: X. Xia et al. (2026), *Dual Modulation Strategy for Suppressing the Thickness Effect in REBCO Coated Conductors*, DOI:10.1002/adfm.77562.

title: Certified adaptive resolution of unknown superconducting hot spots
open: Develop error estimators that force local mesh refinement where previously unknown or evolving defects threaten peak-temperature accuracy.
status: The 2026 EXTRA formulation accelerates magnetothermal simulation by resolving selected critical turns and homogenizing others. Its deliberate resolution of known defects does not certify detection of unanticipated hot spots.
why: Accurate total losses can coexist with an inaccurate maximum temperature.
key_works: L. Denis et al. (2026), *Explicit Turn Resolution with Anisotropic Homogenisation for Efficient 3D Magneto-Thermal Finite-Element Simulation of Large-Scale No-Insulation HTS Magnets*, arXiv:2605.31009.

title: Verified homogenization with angle-dependent critical current
open: Validate reduced magnetothermal models when critical current depends on field orientation and winding coordinates vary along a three-dimensional conductor.
status: Denis and colleagues explicitly omit angular critical-current dependence from their numerical verification and identify its validation as outside the study.
why: A reduced model must preserve the anisotropy that determines local current sharing.
key_works: Denis et al. (2026), EXTRA magnetothermal formulation, arXiv:2605.31009.

title: Lifetime retention of composite-flywheel interference fits
open: Predict retained hub–rim contact pressure through viscoelastic relaxation, temperature changes, and repeated speed cycles, including the onset of slip or separation.
status: Skinner and colleagues modeled lifetime stress evolution in filament-wound rotors. Stress relaxation can reduce one damaging stress while simultaneously weakening the interference fit.
why: Lower internal stress is not automatically improved rotor reliability.
key_works: Skinner et al. (2021), *Effects of Viscoelasticity on the Stress Evolution over the Lifetime of Filament-Wound Composite Flywheel Rotors for Energy Storage*, DOI:10.3390/app11209544.

title: Nonisothermal windage across continuum and rarefied regimes
open: Predict flywheel drag when temperature, residual gas composition, pressure, and rotor–housing gaps evolve together across gas-flow regimes.
status: Venturini and colleagues developed experimentally validated windage descriptions including rarefaction corrections. Transfer to nonuniform temperatures and changing vacuum conditions is a further qualification problem.
why: Vacuum improvement has diminishing value if the wrong gas-transport regime is assumed.
key_works: S. Venturini, S. P. Cavallaro, and A. Vigliani (2024), *Windage loss characterisation for flywheel energy storage system: Model and experimental validation*, DOI:10.1016/j.energy.2024.132641.

title: Separating flywheel losses from spin-down measurements
open: Determine which combinations of spin-down tests and auxiliary measurements distinguish aerodynamic, bearing, and electromagnetic losses without an assumed decomposition.
status: Spin-down measurements support windage characterization, but the observed deceleration contains the sum of all resisting torques.
why: Incorrect attribution can direct efficiency improvements toward the wrong subsystem.
key_works: Venturini, Cavallaro, and Vigliani (2024), windage-characterization study, DOI:10.1016/j.energy.2024.132641.

title: Thermally robust active-magnetic-bearing stability
open: Guarantee stability when coil resistance, magnetic properties, physical clearances, and rotor speed change together during heating.
status: Rende and colleagues demonstrated temperature-induced instability in a deliberately simplified, non-spinning rotor experiment. Its measured threshold is apparatus-specific, not a universal bearing temperature limit.
why: A controller stable at commissioning can become unstable without any explicit hardware failure.
key_works: B. Rende, B. B. Sørensen, and I. F. Santos (2025), *Temperature-induced vibration instability in a non-spinning vertical rotor supported by active magnetic bearings—Theory and experiment*, DOI:10.1016/j.jsv.2025.119339.

title: Experimental basins of safe touchdown-bearing motion
open: Map the conditions separating harmless rebounds, persistent forward whirl, and dangerous backward whirl after shocks or temporary levitation loss.
status: Su and colleagues’ nonlinear simulations identify distinct motion regimes under strong base excitation. Their boundaries require validation under uncertain friction, clearances, and control saturation.
why: Backup bearings must be evaluated by the trajectories they permit, not only static load capacity.
key_works: Y. Su et al. (2021), *Nonlinear dynamic simulation and parametric analysis of a rotor-AMB-TDB system experiencing strong base shock excitations*, DOI:10.1016/j.mechmachtheory.2020.104071.

title: Certified re-levitation from persistent rotor contact
open: Detect contact and switch to a recovery controller that reliably returns the rotor to levitation without provoking a worse whirl mode.
status: Keogh and Cole showed that appropriately phased forcing can destabilize persistent rubbing. A controller designed for contact-free operation is not automatically appropriate after contact.
why: Recovery should restore service rather than merely keep an already rubbing rotor energized.
key_works: P. Keogh and M. Cole (2017), *Dynamic conditions to destabilize persistent Rotor/touchdown bearing contact in AMB systems*, DOI:10.1299/mej.17-00005.

title: Large-excursion validation of gimballed flywheel models
open: Predict rotor motion on moving platforms when magnetic forces leave their approximately linear range and platform translation couples to gyroscopic motion.
status: Dagnaes-Hansen and Santos developed and experimentally tested a gimballed flywheel bench. Agreement for moderate excursions does not establish accuracy near operational clearance limits.
why: Gimbals can reduce transmitted disturbances while introducing coupled motion that simple stationary models miss.
key_works: N. A. Dagnaes-Hansen and I. F. Santos (2019), *Magnetically suspended flywheel in gimbal mount—Test bench design and experimental validation*, Journal of Sound and Vibration, PII:S0022460X19300318.

title: Dynamic load margins after superconducting-bearing force creep
open: Predict safe clearance and load capacity after trapped-flux relaxation, repeated speed changes, and changing magnetic-field histories.
status: Miyazaki and colleagues demonstrated 158 kN static levitation capacity and investigated force creep. Static lifting capability does not establish dynamic margin throughout a flywheel duty cycle.
why: Slowly changing levitation force can alter the response to a later transient.
key_works: Y. Miyazaki et al. (2020), *Development of a Superconducting Magnetic Bearing Capable of Supporting Large Loads in a Flywheel Energy Storage System for Railway Application*, DOI:10.2219/rtriqr.61.1_54.

title: Million-cycle pyroelectric operation at higher temperature
open: Meet a **proposed qualification target** of one million complete 10–90 °C conversion cycles with less than 10% loss of net electrical output at a declared field and cycle rate.
status: Ni and colleagues’ 2026 accelerated analysis places their million-cycle temperature ceiling near 60 °C; they explicitly seek improved high-temperature, high-field endurance.
why: Wider usable temperature swings must not sharply shorten functional life.
key_works: F. Ni et al. (2026), *Heat-to-Electricity Conversion Using Barium Strontium Titanate Multilayer Capacitors*, DOI:10.1002/advs.77106.

title: Cascaded pyroelectric stages with different Curie temperatures
open: Demonstrate a cascade that gains net conversion efficiency after heat exchange, electrical cycling, and thermal coupling between stages are included.
status: Ni and colleagues identify compositionally varied multilayer-capacitor cascades as a natural next step. Their single-composition results do not establish cascade performance.
why: Different stages could exploit different parts of a finite-temperature heat stream.
key_works: Ni et al. (2026), barium-strontium-titanate conversion study, DOI:10.1002/advs.77106.

title: Separating donor chemistry from lattice-compatible leakage suppression
open: Determine how much reduced leakage comes from electronic defect chemistry versus improved phase-boundary compatibility, and predict the combination for untested compositions.
status: Zhang and colleagues connect donor impurities and lattice compatibility in phase-transforming ferroelectrics. Their joint improvement does not independently identify each mechanism’s contribution across materials.
why: Transferable design requires more than finding one favorable doped composition.
key_works: C. Zhang et al. (2026), *Mitigating electric leakage by donor impurity and lattice compatibility in phase-transforming ferroelectric materials*, DOI:10.1088/1361-648X/ae3350.

title: Oxygen-vacancy tradeoffs between pyroelectric response and charge retention
open: Control vacancy populations so the material retains useful polarization response without leakage shortening the number of cycles available after initial charging.
status: Zhang and colleagues found that vacancies can improve a conversion figure of merit while their removal improves endurance in strontium barium niobate. Treated material operated for roughly 7,000 cycles in the reported experiment.
why: Maximizing an instantaneous material metric can reduce total lifetime energy.
key_works: F. Zhang et al. (2025), *Enhanced figure-of-merit and fatigue resistance of strontium barium niobate for pyroelectric energy conversion*, DOI:10.1063/5.0256350.

title: Milliampere-scale pyroelectric output without continuous bias
open: Obtain milliampere-level current into a specified useful load while retaining positive net cycle energy and accounting for initial charging, leakage, and thermal-management work.
status: The 2026 assessment of operation without continuous external bias identifies multilayer scaling as a route beyond small currents. “No continuous bias” does not mean that initial preparation is absent.
why: Useful electronics require delivered current and voltage, not only measurable charge pulses.
key_works: C. Zhang et al. (2026), *Toward enduring pyroelectric energy harvesting without external bias field*, DOI:10.1063/5.0331971.

title: Generality of the intermediate-order phase-transition optimum
open: Determine whether the best compromise between polarization change, reversibility, and leakage systematically occurs near the crossover between first- and second-order behavior.
status: Geng and colleagues report a favorable intermediate composition in barium strontium titanate, including 10,000 conversion cycles without recharging. This demonstrates a material-specific optimum, not a universal selection rule.
why: A general criterion could replace extensive composition-by-composition screening.
key_works: R. Geng et al. (2026), *Compositionally tuned phase transformations enhance pyroelectric energy harvesting from low-grade heat*, arXiv:2605.01791.

title: Net benefit of combined electronic cooling and pyroelectric harvesting
open: Establish when switching a ferroelectric device between cooling and harvesting improves total electronic-system energy use under actual workload fluctuations.
status: Zou and colleagues demonstrated cooling and energy-harvesting functions using ferroelectric polymer composites. Combining functions does not automatically establish an advantage over separately optimized thermal management.
why: The device must not recover small electrical pulses while increasing the larger cooling burden.
key_works: K. Zou et al. (2024), *Electronic cooling and energy harvesting using ferroelectric polymer composites*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-51147-6.

title: Solar-spectrum charging of high-density Dewar pyrimidones
open: Shift useful charging toward abundant solar wavelengths while preserving high stored energy, conversion yield, and storage stability.
status: Nguyen and colleagues demonstrated storage above 1.6 MJ kg⁻¹ using excitation at 300 nm. High molecular energy density does not establish efficient capture of the complete solar spectrum.
why: A dense storage molecule still needs an effective route for absorbing sunlight.
key_works: H. P. Q. Nguyen et al. (2026), *Molecular solar thermal energy storage in Dewar pyrimidone beyond 1.6 megajoules per kilogram*, DOI:10.1126/science.aec6413.

title: Closed-cycle acid-triggered molecular heat release
open: Repeatedly charge and discharge Dewar-pyrimidone systems while recovering the triggering chemistry and preventing inactive-product accumulation.
status: The 2026 study demonstrates solvent-free operation and acid-triggered heat sufficient to boil a small water sample. Useful heat transfer is established; complete repeated-cycle material closure is the further target.
why: Triggering reagents and cleanup must not become hidden consumable inventories.
key_works: Nguyen et al. (2026), Dewar-pyrimidone storage study, DOI:10.1126/science.aec6413.

title: Predictive branching ratios in norbornadiene photocharging
open: Predict quantum yield and competing relaxation pathways across substituents and solvents using independently validated excited-state dynamics.
status: Kochman and Durbeej simulate ultrafast energy capture in push–pull norbornadiene–quadricyclane systems. A calculated reaction trajectory does not establish transferable product branching in every environment.
why: Red-shifting absorption is useful only if photons still populate the desired storage state.
key_works: M. A. Kochman and B. Durbeej (2025), *Simulating the Energy Capture Process in Push–Pull Norbornadiene–Quadricyclane Photoswitches*, DOI:10.1021/acs.jpclett.5c00634.

title: Radical-pathway selectivity during electrocatalytic heat release
open: Resolve the competition between desired quadricyclane-to-norbornadiene conversion and irreversible reactions after electron transfer, including electronic states inadequately described by a single reference configuration.
status: Franz and colleagues show strong substituent dependence and explicitly identify more advanced electronic-structure treatment as a remaining need.
why: Low triggering voltage is insufficient if it opens destructive reaction pathways.
key_works: E. Franz et al. (2025), *Tuning Electrocatalytic Energy Release in Norbornadiene Based Molecular Solar Thermal Systems Through Substituent Effects*, DOI:10.1002/chem.202502294.

title: Thousand-cycle retention for electrocatalytically discharged photoswitches
open: Meet a **proposed target** of at least 90% retained usable storage capacity after 1,000 complete charging–discharging cycles, including catalyst and electrolyte aging.
status: High single-discharge selectivity is reported for selected substituents. It does not determine cumulative full-cycle retention.
why: Small irreversible losses compound through repeated reuse.
key_works: Franz et al. (2025), electrocatalytic molecular-storage study, DOI:10.1002/chem.202502294.

title: Coupled protonation and association in aqueous molecular storage
open: Predict photoconversion, storage, and catalytic release as protonation and molecular association change with concentration and pH.
status: Castro Baroffio and colleagues demonstrate water-soluble norbornadiene chemistry with distinct solution regimes. Treating the carrier as one invariant dissolved species misses those changes.
why: Conditions that improve solubility can alter switching and heat-release behavior.
key_works: F. Castro Baroffio et al. (2026), *Water-Soluble Molecular Solar Thermal System: Photochemical Switching and Catalytic Back-Conversion of 2,5-Norbornadiene-2,3-Dicarboxylic Acid*, DOI:10.1002/chem.202502510.

title: Micelle-to-catalyst transfer in water-based solar storage
open: Preserve fast charging and heat release when surfactant assemblies solubilize the photoswitch but also regulate its access to catalytic surfaces.
status: Fernandez and colleagues demonstrated surfactant-enabled aqueous operation and measurable temperature rise. Their result opens, rather than eliminates, the need to understand partitioning and transport during repeated use.
why: A solubilizing environment can become a reaction barrier.
key_works: L. Fernandez et al. (2025), *Surfactant-enabled strategy for molecular solar thermal energy storage systems in water*, DOI:10.1039/D5GC04357C.

title: Bistable harvesting robust to changing excitation statistics
open: Select mechanical potential wells and electrical loading that remain beneficial when excitation changes between persistent oscillations, intermittent shocks, and drifting random spectra.
status: Xiao and colleagues model and experimentally investigate a bistable generator, including two random-excitation classes, in 2026. Random forcing itself is no longer an unstudied case; robustness beyond the calibrated classes remains open.
why: A tuned bistable device can remain trapped in a low-output well when its environment changes.
key_works: A. Xiao et al. (2026), *Vibration study of a bistable dielectric energy generator considering random excitations*, DOI:10.1007/s11071-026-12347-5.

title: Restoring dielectric strength after mechanical self-healing
open: Achieve a **proposed 90% recovery of original breakdown strength** after a specified damage-and-healing protocol while retaining low loss and useful mechanical compliance.
status: Ellingford and colleagues demonstrated self-healing elastomers that recovered 44% of breakdown strength in their energy-harvesting experiment. Mechanical rejoining is not equivalent to restoration of electrical reliability.
why: A healed membrane may otherwise require permanent operation far below its original field.
key_works: C. Ellingford et al. (2020), *Self-Healing Dielectric Elastomers for Damage-Tolerant Actuation and Energy Harvesting*, DOI:10.1021/acsami.9b21957.

title: Finite-rate, reliability-constrained elastomer conversion bounds
open: Derive achievable energy and power bounds including viscoelastic loss, leakage, finite charging rates, and an explicit probability of electrical or mechanical failure.
status: Established analyses bound idealized conversion using instability, tension, and breakdown constraints. Those bounds do not automatically describe finite-rate operation in an aging, statistically heterogeneous membrane.
why: A maximum-energy cycle is not necessarily a useful repeated-cycle design.
key_works: S. J. A. Koh et al. (2011), *Dielectric Elastomer Generators: How Much Energy Can Be Converted?*, DOI:10.1109/TMECH.2010.2089635.

title: Defect scaling and fault containment in stacked elastomer generators
open: Predict how increasing layer count and active area changes breakdown probability, and prevent a local electrical defect from disabling an entire stack.
status: McKay and colleagues demonstrated stacked generator architectures. Successful stacking does not establish how correlated defects and local discharge energy scale with production size.
why: Scaling output by adding layers must not increase replacement risk disproportionately.
key_works: T. G. McKay et al. (2015), *Dielectric elastomer generators that stack up*, DOI:10.1088/0964-1726/24/1/015014.

title: Low-temperature healing without high-temperature creep
open: Engineer reversible polymer interactions that permit useful healing when cold while resisting creep and dielectric loss when warm.
status: Ellingford and colleagues document temperature-dependent healing and electromechanical behavior in mixed-polar-group elastomers. Molecular mobility aids healing but can also undermine dimensional stability.
why: The same material must survive both recovery and ordinary service conditions.
key_works: C. Ellingford et al. (2020), *Understanding the enhancement and temperature-dependency of the self-healing and electromechanical properties of dielectric elastomers containing mixed pendant polar groups*, DOI:10.1039/D0TC00509F.

title: Choosing primed versus self-priming harvesting circuits
open: Select and adapt circuit architecture to maximize net energy when deformation and available priming energy vary, including monitoring and high-voltage conversion losses.
status: Rosset and colleagues experimentally optimize a simple cycle but explicitly leave the choice between that cycle and integrated self-priming dependent on energy availability and deformation.
why: A nearly ideal electrical cycle can be impractical when its startup energy cannot be supplied.
key_works: S. Rosset et al. (2022), *Squeezing More Juice out of Dielectric Elastomer Generators*, DOI:10.3389/frobt.2022.825148.

title: Causal origin of heavy-water-enhanced yarn harvesting
open: Separate the effects of isotope substitution on charge redistribution, equilibrium capacitance, viscosity, and interfacial chemistry using controls that independently constrain those changes.
status: Ekanayake and colleagues report enhanced low-frequency harvesting with D₂O in 2026. Multiple electrolyte properties change together, so the observed improvement does not by itself establish their individual contributions.
why: Identifying the mechanism could enable comparable gains without relying on the same isotope substitution.
key_works: I. Ekanayake et al. (2026), *D2O-Enhanced Twistron Yarn Harvesters for Low-Frequency Mechanical Energy Harvesting*, DOI:10.1021/acsnano.5c18352.

title: Maintaining opposed electrode deformation under irregular motion
open: Preserve beneficial phase relationships between mechanically active anode and cathode yarns when the driving motion is multidirectional or nonperiodic.
status: Wang and colleagues demonstrated opposed deformation using hinged structures, increasing voltage and reducing required mechanical input in studied conditions. A prescribed 180° relationship is not guaranteed in an unconstrained textile.
why: Electrode motions can reinforce or cancel each other’s electrical response.
key_works: Z. Wang et al. (2022), *More Powerful Twistron Carbon Nanotube Yarn Mechanical Energy Harvesters*, DOI:10.1002/adma.202201826.

title: Constitutive prediction of homochiral-yarn densification
open: Predict lateral compaction, inter-ply contact, capacitance change, and output from yarn geometry without refitting a separate electromechanical law for each construction.
status: Zhang and colleagues demonstrated 17.4% tensile and 22.4% torsional conversion efficiencies in studied homochirally plied yarns. These results establish performance, not a universal constitutive model.
why: Predictive geometry selection could replace extensive empirical twisting and plying trials.
key_works: M. Zhang et al. (2023), *Mechanical energy harvesters with tensile efficiency of 17.4% and torsional efficiency of 22.4% based on homochirally plied carbon nanotube yarns*, DOI:10.1038/s41560-022-01191-7.

title: Optimal yarn chirality under constrained end rotation
open: Determine which twist and ply arrangement maximizes usable output when mounting prevents free rotation or imposes cyclic torsional loads.
status: Homochiral construction outperformed alternatives in the cited experiments. Its advantage cannot simply be assumed under every rotational boundary condition.
why: A yarn installed in fabric or a mechanism may behave differently from a freely configured specimen.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2023), homochirally plied yarn study, DOI:10.1038/s41560-022-01191-7.

title: Dynamic pore accessibility versus static capacitance in twistrons
open: Predict harvesting output from nanotube-diameter distributions and evolving pore access, rather than using initial capacitance as the principal screening metric.
status: Goh and colleagues found that nanotube curvature affects capacitance change and electrical output differently from static gravimetric capacitance. A larger initial capacitance is not necessarily the better harvesting material.
why: The useful quantity is deformation-induced recoverable electrical energy, not charge storage measured in an undeformed state.
key_works: B. Goh et al. (2021), *Outer diameter curvature effects in multi-walled carbon nanotubes on the twistron energy harvester*, DOI:10.1016/j.apsusc.2021.150075.

title: Unambiguous rarefaction-shock identification in dense organic vapor
open: Observe a finite-amplitude rarefaction shock while independently excluding temperature inhomogeneity, fluid decomposition, and measurement artifacts, and verify the thermodynamic states required for its nonclassical interpretation.
status: The 2025 ASTER experiments report repeatable departures from classical gas dynamics near the working fluid’s thermal-stability limit. Such departures do not, by themselves, uniquely identify a rarefaction shock.
why: Tests a distinctive prediction of nonconvex-fluid thermodynamics relevant to dense-vapor machinery.
