key_works: C. Medipati et al. (2025), *Rarefaction Shockwave Experiments in Dense Organic Vapours*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_16; N. Chandrasekaran et al. (2024), *Nonclassical wave propagation measurements in the high temperature vapor of D6…*, DOI:10.1007/s00348-024-03843-8.

title: Affordable nonclassical Riemann solvers with certified wave selection
open: Compute physically admissible compound-wave solutions cheaply enough for repeated numerical flux evaluations, without misclassifying wave structure near changes in thermodynamic convexity.
status: Sirianni, Guardone, and Re’s 2025 solver automatically identifies reference wave structures, but the authors explicitly describe its cost as unsuitable for routine Godunov flux evaluation.
why: Reliable dense-fluid simulations need correct wave selection at millions of cell interfaces.
key_works: G. Sirianni, A. Guardone, and B. Re (2025), *Automatic Wave Curve Structure Detection for the Computation of Reference Solutions of Non-Classical Riemann Problems*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_1.

title: Subgrid closure for the filtered real-fluid equation of state
open: Predict the difference between applying an equation of state to filtered variables and filtering the actual thermodynamic response, including correlated density and internal-energy fluctuations.
status: Lea and colleagues’ 2025 simulations demonstrate differences in mean values and probability distributions even where aggregate discrepancies appear modest. Their studied conditions do not establish a universal closure near critical regions.
why: A turbulence model can mispredict pressure and temperature even if its momentum closure is adequate.
key_works: B. Lea, W. Sadowski, and F. di Mare (2025), *Evaluating Differences Between the Computable and Filtered State Variables in Supercritical Carbon Dioxide*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_5.

title: Thermodynamically stable adaptive property tables
open: Construct adaptive equation-of-state tables that preserve thermodynamic identities, physically required stability, and controlled derivative accuracy near sharp property changes and phase boundaries.
status: Errante and Corre demonstrate thermodynamically consistent interpolation in 2025. Consistency alone does not certify every interpolated derivative or prevent inappropriate interpolation between thermodynamic branches.
why: Small property-table errors can change wave speeds, stability predictions, and calculated cycle performance.
key_works: P. Errante and C. Corre (2025), *Thermodynamically Consistent Interpolation for Tabulated Equations of State*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_10.

title: Experiments that actually discriminate competing fluid equations of state
open: Design dense-vapor experiments whose joint pressure, temperature, density, and flow measurements distinguish competing equations of state from boundary-condition and numerical errors.
status: Fernandes and colleagues’ 2025 validation study finds that Mach-number uncertainty can exceed the differences being tested. More operating points do not resolve a fundamentally nondiscriminating observable.
why: Model agreement inside large error bars is weak evidence for predictive accuracy.
key_works: D. S. C. Fernandes, M. Majer, and A. J. Head (2025), *Towards a Thermodynamic Validation Map for Non-Ideal Compressible Flows*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_6.

title: Nonreflecting boundaries for multidimensional real-fluid waves
open: Develop stable boundary conditions that transmit oblique acoustic, entropy, and vortical disturbances through strongly varying real-fluid states without introducing consequential reflections.
status: Li and colleagues’ 2025 assessment demonstrates improvements in one-dimensional acoustic tests. That evidence does not establish multidimensional performance under interacting disturbances and thermodynamic gradients.
why: Artificial boundary reflections can be mistaken for a physical instability of the machinery.
key_works: Z. Li et al. (2025), *An Assessment of Navier-Stokes Characteristic Boundary Conditions for Real Fluids in a Non-Dissipative Numerical Framework*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_11.

title: Removing numerical startup waves without damping physical weak waves
open: Initialize and reconstruct nonideal-fluid discontinuities so numerical methods do not emit spurious acoustic waves, while retaining conservation and genuine weak-wave propagation.
status: Pederzolli and Guardone identify startup waves associated with nonlinear jump relations in 2025, including acoustic waves generated from nominal contact discontinuities. Explaining the artifact does not supply a generally robust removal method.
why: Weak physical signals can be overwhelmed by waves created by the discretization.
key_works: M. Pederzolli and A. Guardone (2025), *Start-Up Waves in Shock-Capturing Schemes for Ideal and Non-Ideal Compressible Flows*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_4.

title: Dense-vapor trailing-edge base-pressure prediction
open: Predict trailing-edge base pressure and associated losses across organic working fluids, blade geometries, and thermodynamic states without relying on unvalidated ideal-gas correlations.
status: Oliveti, Wheeler, and Persico report preliminary Reynolds-averaged calculations and direct simulations in 2025. These provide detailed cases rather than a transferable dense-vapor loss law.
why: Small trailing-edge loss errors can materially distort organic Rankine-cycle turbine optimization.
key_works: M. Oliveti, A. P. S. Wheeler, and G. Persico (2025), *Direct Simulations of Non-Ideal Supersonic Flows in the Trailing Edge Region*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_8.

title: Predicting buoyancy-driven reversal of supercritical heat-transfer behavior
open: Predict when heating supercritical fluid suppresses vertical turbulence through stratification and when it generates transport-enhancing plumes, across orientation and operating conditions.
status: Draskic, Westerweel, and Pecnik demonstrate both behaviors in studied supercritical-CO₂ conditions. A heat-transfer correlation that averages them together can conceal the transition controlling performance.
why: The same nominal heat input can improve or degrade heat removal.
key_works: M. Draskic, J. Westerweel, and R. Pecnik (2025), *Mixed Convection at Supercritical Pressures*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_15.

title: Joint admissibility guarantees for real-fluid multiphase solvers
open: Establish a solver that simultaneously preserves energy, admissible phase fractions, positive thermodynamic states, and appropriate entropy behavior through stiff real-fluid transitions.
status: Sirianni and colleagues’ 2025 temperature-update formulation achieves energy conservation and demonstrates multiphase applications. The joint guarantee is a stronger target than conserving total energy alone.
why: An exactly conserved calculation can still enter an unphysical state.
key_works: G. Sirianni et al. (2025), *Conservative Temperature Update for the Efficient Simulation of Single and Multi-Phase Flows using the Span-Wagner Equation of State*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_2.

title: The factor-of-two discrepancy in interfacial-wave damping
open: Resolve the disagreement between higher-mode damping predictions through independent experiments and asymptotic analysis spanning free-surface and two-liquid limits.
status: Hegde and colleagues identify a factor-of-two adjustment that reconciles one comparison but breaks agreement with established free-surface damping. They explicitly request higher-mode experiments.
why: Incorrect damping shifts predicted instability thresholds.
key_works: P. Hegde, W. Herreman, and G. M. Horstmann (2025), *Stability theory for metal pad roll with consideration of viscous and magnetic damping*, arXiv:2507.18301.

title: Magnetic damping of bidirectional metal-pad waves
open: Measure magnetic damping for interfacial modes varying in both horizontal directions, resolving the complex induced-current patterns rather than extrapolating from one-dimensional modes.
status: Hegde and colleagues validate magnetic damping only for the particular mode \(m=1,n=0\); bidirectional-mode validation is explicitly outstanding.
why: These modes participate in instabilities of conducting liquid layers.
key_works: Hegde, Herreman, and Horstmann (2025), *Stability theory for metal pad roll with consideration of viscous and magnetic damping*, arXiv:2507.18301.

title: Geometry-robust stability design around metal-pad resonances
open: Choose cell geometry with defensible stability margins under uncertain dimensions, depth, damping, and electromagnetic forcing, rather than maximizing the threshold of one idealized model.
status: Politis and Priede prove a fractal inviscid threshold structure and show its smoothing by viscous friction. Their model’s preferred aspect ratio is not a universal optimum for manufactured cells.
why: Near-resonant mode pairs can make apparently favorable geometries sensitive to small changes.
key_works: G. Politis and J. Priede (2021), *Fractality of metal pad instability threshold in rectangular cells*, DOI:10.1017/jfm.2021.100.

title: Equilibrium-preserving acceleration with correct conservation laws
open: Accelerate mirror-plasma equilibration while preserving the intended stationary distribution and conservation balances under sources and collisions.
status: Rosen and colleagues report approximately 25,000-fold computational acceleration in a studied setup. Their time-dilation and modified-Hamiltonian approaches do not automatically preserve the same combination of equilibrium and conservation properties.
why: Rapid convergence is useful only to the intended physical equilibrium.
key_works: M. H. Rosen et al. (2026), *Gyrokinetic equilibria of high temperature superconducting magnetic mirrors*, arXiv:2604.11684.

title: Self-consistent drift-cyclotron loss-cone closures
open: Couple loss-cone-driven instability and transport to evolving mirror distributions without prescribing an arbitrary anomalous-loss coefficient.
status: The 2026 gyrokinetic-equilibrium study explicitly omits this instability and identifies reduced modeling as future work; detailed simulations of related mirror configurations provide partial evidence.
why: Instability-driven losses can invalidate an otherwise converged equilibrium prediction.
key_works: Rosen et al. (2026), arXiv:2604.11684; A. Tran et al. (2025), *Drift-cyclotron loss-cone instability in 3-D simulations of a sloshing-ion simple mirror*, Journal of Plasma Physics 91, E85.

title: Physical versus numerical trapping in mirror expanders
open: Determine the continuum-limit trapped-electron population, separating genuine formation-history effects from particle-in-cell noise and finite-resolution scattering.
status: Tyushev and colleagues obtain substantial trapped populations in collisionless simulations and discuss initialization, transients, and numerical effects as possible contributors.
why: Trapped electrons influence the potential and energy carried out of the device.
key_works: M. Tyushev et al. (2025), *Drift-kinetic PIC simulations of plasma flow and energy transport in the magnetic mirror configuration*, arXiv:2501.15604.

title: Cold-electron control of mirror-expander heat losses
open: Predict the self-consistent potential and heat transport when secondary emission and local ionization supply cold electrons to the expander.
status: These electron sources are omitted from Tyushev and colleagues’ studied model and identified as relevant extensions. A collisionless injected distribution does not represent every operating boundary.
why: Boundary-created populations can change upstream confinement and exhaust power.
key_works: Tyushev et al. (2025), *Drift-kinetic PIC simulations of plasma flow and energy transport in the magnetic mirror configuration*, arXiv:2501.15604.

title: Centrifugal-trap inversion with realistic loss boundaries
open: Determine whether composition-induced trap inversion survives self-consistent sheath, presheath, and truncated-loss-cone distributions outside the deeply trapped limit.
status: Kolmes, Ochs, and Fisch demonstrate inversion using tractable distribution assumptions and discuss extensions; those results do not settle every open-boundary regime.
why: Selective confinement depends on the potential actually maintained by escaping particles.
key_works: E. J. Kolmes, I. E. Ochs, and N. J. Fisch (2025), *Ion Mix Can Invert Centrifugal Traps*, arXiv:2504.18634.

title: Charge-selective trapping with nonthermal ion mixtures
open: Predict and sustain selective centrifugal confinement when beam-like distributions replace Maxwellian mixtures, including the power required to maintain those distributions.
status: The ion-mixture study identifies qualitatively different selection possibilities for nonthermal populations but does not provide a complete kinetic operating model.
why: Nonthermal control may change which species are retained or removed.
key_works: Kolmes, Ochs, and Fisch (2025), *Ion Mix Can Invert Centrifugal Traps*, arXiv:2504.18634.

title: Self-consistent alpha-channeling and ash-removal balances
open: Calculate energy extraction, alpha ejection, thermal-ash inventory, and remaining plasma heating jointly rather than selecting channeling efficiency and ejection fraction independently.
status: Parisi and colleagues’ 2026 analysis explicitly uses simplified ash and ejection accounting. Enhanced wave interaction alone does not establish the resulting steady operating benefit.
why: Removing ash can also remove energy needed to sustain fusion.
key_works: J. F. Parisi, A. Diallo, and J. W. S. Cook (2026), *Enhanced alpha channeling with spin-polarized fuel*, arXiv:2607.25313.

title: Launchable waves for polarization-enhanced alpha channeling
open: Design an antenna and propagation path that produce the required wave spectrum and amplitude in a self-consistent polarized-fuel equilibrium.
status: The 2026 study leaves antenna coupling and propagation as separate engineering questions; prescribed wave amplitudes are not demonstrated launch efficiencies.
why: A favorable particle–wave interaction is useful only if the necessary wave can be supplied.
key_works: Parisi, Diallo, and Cook (2026), *Enhanced alpha channeling with spin-polarized fuel*, arXiv:2607.25313.

title: Slowing-down-driven capture of proton–boron fusion ash
open: Determine whether fast alpha particles can supply useful heating and subsequently enter selectively confined removal populations as they slow, with quantitatively controlled diffusion.
status: Ochs, Kolmes, and Fisch explicitly propose this kinetic alternative to prescribed species-selective potentials and leave its detailed validation outside their 2025 treatment.
why: Ash removal should preserve useful energy deposition.
key_works: I. E. Ochs, E. J. Kolmes, and N. J. Fisch (2025), *Preventing ash from poisoning proton-boron 11 fusion plasmas*, DOI:10.1063/5.0266369.

title: Suppressing alpha-induced neutron side reactions without sacrificing heating
open: Reduce energetic-alpha overlap with boron while maintaining sufficient useful alpha-energy transfer to the plasma.
status: The 2025 ash study distinguishes thermal-ash control from neutron-producing reactions involving fast alphas. Removing already thermalized helium does not solve that separate problem.
why: “Aneutronic” primary fuel does not eliminate all neutron-producing pathways.
key_works: Ochs, Kolmes, and Fisch (2025), *Preventing ash from poisoning proton-boron 11 fusion plasmas*, DOI:10.1063/5.0266369.

title: Covariance-resolved proton–boron cross sections near the useful resonance
open: Meet a **proposed target of approximately 2% uncertainty** in the relevant cross-section interval around the principal resonance, with correlated normalization and energy-calibration errors explicitly reported.
status: Wang and colleagues’ 2026 reassessment discusses approximately 10% uncertainty near 0.6 MeV and its effect on calculated reactivity. Independently varying data points does not represent shared calibration uncertainty.
why: Reactor optimization should not treat uncertain reaction data as exact.
key_works: H.-Y. Wang et al. (2026), *Revisiting p-11B Fusion: Updated Cross-sections, Reactivity, and Energy Balance*, arXiv:2601.00241.

title: Identity of the intermediate state in lead zirconate
open: Determine when the narrow intermediate regime in PbZrO₃ is a distinct equilibrium phase, a mixture, or a kinetically retained structure.
status: Zhang and colleagues’ 2024 simulations reproduce major thermal behavior but not every reported intermediate state; its interpretation remains dependent on conditions and modeling.
why: Phase identity controls how switching pathways should be modeled.
key_works: H. Zhang et al. (2024), *Finite-temperature properties of antiferroelectric perovskite PbZrO3 from deep learning interatomic potential*, arXiv:2406.09011.

title: Long-range-interaction errors in antiferroelectric machine-learned potentials
open: Quantify how interaction truncation changes competing-phase free energies and switching predictions, with error control fine enough to preserve their ordering.
status: The 2024 PbZrO₃ model uses a finite interaction cutoff and explicitly identifies long-range treatment as a question for further comparison.
why: Small energy errors can change the predicted storage mechanism.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2024), *Finite-temperature properties of antiferroelectric perovskite PbZrO3 from deep learning interatomic potential*, arXiv:2406.09011.

title: Deposition-to-clearing prediction for metallized-film electrodes
open: Predict how electrode deposition conditions determine local current paths, clearing energy, and permanently lost capacitance, while preserving required current-carrying capability.
status: Wu and colleagues link evaporation rate to metallization structure and clearing behavior. Lower clearing damage cannot be optimized independently of electrode continuity and resistance.
why: Capacitor “self-healing” isolates a defect by sacrificing material; the amount sacrificed matters.
key_works: Z.-Y. Wu et al. (2025, online), *Correlation Between Evaporation Dynamics and Self-Healing Characteristics in Metallised Polypropylene Films*, DOI:10.1049/hve2.70074.

title: Experimental validation of ozone-assisted capacitor clearing
open: Demonstrate that oxidation of breakdown residues improves electrical isolation without causing unacceptable prior damage to the intact dielectric.
status: Andreeva, Liu, and Chaban’s 2026 quantum-chemical study predicts changes in residue composition and conductivity. It is a simulation result, not qualification of an operating capacitor.
why: Chemistry that removes conductive residue may also attack the material that must survive.
key_works: N. A. Andreeva, C. Liu, and V. V. Chaban (2026), *Ozonation of Dielectric Fosters Self-Healing Efficiency in Metalized-Film Capacitors: Quantum-Chemical Simulation*, arXiv:2602.08451.

title: Predicting insulating versus conductive breakdown residues
open: Predict which combinations of polymer chemistry, electrode material, and deposited breakdown energy produce a passivating residue rather than a persistent conductive path.
status: Fan and colleagues demonstrate phosphorus–nitrogen-cage polymers whose inorganic-rich residues support self-healing. Their result shows that residue removal is not the only viable mechanism, but does not provide a general residue-selection rule.
why: Residue chemistry could become a design variable instead of an uncontrolled failure product.
key_works: L. Fan et al. (2026), *PN-Cage-Based Hybrid Inorganic–Organic Polymers for Self-Healing High-Energy Density Capacitors*, DOI:10.1002/adfm.202532164.

title: Preserving polar-crystal benefits above a polymer’s glass transition
open: Retain useful crystalline dipole alignment and low electrical loss while controlling mechanical creep during prolonged operation above the amorphous phase’s glass-transition temperature.
status: Chen and colleagues demonstrate improved dielectric response above approximately 140 °C in their sulfonylated polymer. Favorable short-term electrical behavior does not establish coupled structural and electrical lifetime.
why: Increased molecular mobility can improve dielectric response while weakening dimensional stability.
key_works: J. Chen et al. (2025), *Linear Dielectric Polymers with Ferroelectric-Like Crystals for High-Temperature Capacitive Energy Storage*, DOI:10.1002/adma.202417072.

title: Electrochemical hydrogen recovery from odorized gas mixtures
open: Recover hydrogen from multicomponent, odorant-containing feeds while controlling sulfur poisoning, purification burden, and catalyst replacement.
status: Aziz and colleagues’ 2025 experiments deliberately use odorant-free binary mixtures; mercaptan-containing feed is explicitly outside their evidence.
why: Clean binary-mixture results do not qualify recovery from actual distribution gas.
key_works: M. Aziz et al. (2025), *Electrochemical Hydrogen Separation and Compression*, DOI:10.1007/s10800-025-02312-2.

title: Regeneration after carbon-dioxide-induced compressor poisoning
open: Maintain productive operation through changing CO₂ exposure while removing generated poisons without accumulating regeneration damage or excessive downtime.
status: The 2025 separation study reports CO₂-related performance loss and recovery procedures. Recovery in selected tests does not establish indefinite repeated regeneration.
why: A nominally recoverable poison can still impose an unacceptable operating burden.
key_works: Aziz et al. (2025), *Electrochemical Hydrogen Separation and Compression*, DOI:10.1007/s10800-025-02312-2.

title: Humidity-aware control during hydrogen-compressor transients
open: Coordinate temperature, humidification, and current so changing operation avoids both membrane drying and excessive water handling while minimizing total compression energy.
status: Pineda-Delgado and colleagues’ controlled tests show strong humidity–temperature dependence. Steady operating optima do not supply a control law for mismatched thermal response times.
why: A temperature change intended to improve conduction can temporarily make hydration worse.
key_works: J. L. Pineda-Delgado et al. (2022), *Effect of relative humidity and temperature on the performance of an electrochemical hydrogen compressor*, DOI:10.1016/j.apenergy.2022.118617.

title: Pressure–throughput limits with evolving hydrogen back-diffusion
open: Predict the attainable pressure, delivered flow, and efficiency together when membrane permeability changes with hydration, temperature, pressure history, and aging.
status: Chouhan, Bahar, and Prasad established and validated back-diffusion-aware compression models in 2020. Reaching a high pressure in a confined volume does not determine useful continuous throughput at that pressure.
why: Compression performance should be specified at a product-delivery condition, not only an endpoint pressure.
key_works: A. Chouhan, B. Bahar, and A. K. Prasad (2020), *Effect of back-diffusion on the performance of an electrochemical hydrogen compressor*, DOI:10.1016/j.ijhydene.2020.02.048.

title: Optimal hybrid staging with unequal electrochemical compressor cells
open: Select and control combinations of series and parallel gas paths when cells differ in resistance, crossover, and degradation.
status: Chouhan and colleagues analyze the pressure–flow tradeoff between two basic stack configurations. Their equal-cell framework does not settle heterogeneous stacks under changing demand.
why: The best configuration can change as membranes age.
key_works: A. Chouhan et al. (2020), *Analysis of an electrochemical compressor stack*, DOI:10.1016/j.ijhydene.2020.08.164.

title: Lifetime-uniform compression of high-pressure membrane stacks
open: Preserve adequate sealing and electrical contact without damaging membranes as gaskets creep, temperatures cycle, and stack pressure changes.
status: End-plate optimization studies assess initial pressure distribution and stack geometry. A favorable initial finite-element result is not lifetime qualification of the deforming assembly.
why: Mechanical nonuniformity can create both leakage and localized electrochemical losses.
key_works: S. D. Seo and W. T. Kwon (2023), *Structural Analysis and Optimization of Electrochemical Hydrogen Compressor End Plate Using Taguchi Method and Gray Relational Analysis*, DOI:10.7736/JKSPE.023.083.

title: Causal descriptors for suppressing nitrogen poisoning on platinum
open: Separate electronic support effects from altered interfacial chemistry and morphology, then predict poisoning resistance on supports not used in model fitting.
status: Paliwal and colleagues report slower deactivation on TiO₂-supported platinum and correlations with adsorbed nitrogen and electronic structure. Correlation does not uniquely identify the controlling mechanism.
why: Transferable descriptors would improve catalyst selection.
key_works: A. Paliwal et al. (2025), *Inhibition of Nitrogen Poisoning on Pt during Ammonia Oxidation through Early Transition Metal Oxide Supports*, DOI:10.1021/acscatal.5c01870.

title: Lifetime-positive pulsed regeneration during ammonia oxidation
open: Optimize regeneration pulses using complete energy, productive-time, and degradation accounting rather than recovered current alone.
status: The 2025 study demonstrates extended membrane-electrode operation using alternating potentials. Selected-hour performance does not establish whether repeated regeneration remains beneficial over component life.
why: Restoring activity can accelerate another failure mechanism.
key_works: Paliwal et al. (2025), *Inhibition of Nitrogen Poisoning on Pt during Ammonia Oxidation through Early Transition Metal Oxide Supports*, DOI:10.1021/acscatal.5c01870.

title: Closing the buffer-chamber ammonia regeneration loop
open: Recover and redistribute ammonia accumulated in an intermediate chamber while preserving the benefit of reduced crossover after regeneration heat and auxiliary work are counted.
status: Ko and colleagues extend studied discharge duration from 330 to 800 minutes using a buffer chamber. Longer discharge does not, by itself, establish improved efficiency of the complete repeated thermal cycle.
why: Crossover suppression can move the separation burden into a new inventory.
key_works: Y. M. Ko et al. (2025), *Enhancing thermally regenerative battery performance by mitigating ammonia crossover*, DOI:10.1016/j.apenergy.2025.126337.

title: Stability of density-stratified “virtual membranes”
open: Maintain sufficiently separated electrolytes without a physical membrane as current, temperature, density, and pumping disturbances change during repeated thermal regeneration.
status: Shi and colleagues demonstrate membrane-free power generation using electrolyte density differences, including high peak power under studied conditions. Those measurements do not determine the instability boundary of a complete cycling system.
why: Removing membrane resistance is useful only while unwanted mixing remains controlled.
key_works: Y. Shi et al. (2023), *Power generation enhancement of a membrane-free thermally regenerative battery induced by the density difference of electrolytes*, DOI:10.1016/j.apenergy.2023.121302.
